scholarships.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM)
scholarships.name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM)
scholarships.deadline: Varies by consortium/programme - typically Dec-Feb for a Sept/Oct intake; no single central deadline
scholarships.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are high-level, integrated transnational study programmes at master's level designed and delivered by international partnerships of higher education institutions. An EMJM involves at least three higher education institutions from at least three different countries, and includes periods of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence. Each edition runs 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits) and awards either a joint degree or multiple degrees. A new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the list each year, and students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme.
scholarships.duration: 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits)
scholarships.application_period: Varies by consortium/programme - typically Dec-Feb for a Sept/Oct intake; no single central deadline
scholarships.image_alt_text: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters students on a European university campus
eligibility: ["Bachelor's degree (first degree) completed, or the candidate is in the final year of a bachelor's programme", "Graduation before the master's programme starts", "Officially recognised bachelor-equivalent level of learning (recognised under the legislation and practices of the degree-awarding country) is also accepted"]
scholarships.eligibility_summary: Bachelor's degree (3-4 years) in a relevant field, or final-year students may apply if the programme allows (must graduate before the program starts). No fixed CGPA requirement - selection weighs motivation, relevant background, and clarity of goals more heavily than grades.
benefits: ["Full tuition, approx. EUR 1,400/month stipend, travel allowance, installation allowance (exact figures vary slightly by consortium)"]
coverage: ["Full tuition, approx. EUR 1,400/month stipend, travel allowance, installation allowance (exact figures vary slightly by consortium)"]
documents: ["Academic transcripts/certificates (Bachelor's, HSC, SSC)", "CV", "Motivation letter", "2 recommendation letters (typical)", "Proof of English proficiency"]
required_documents: ["Academic transcripts/certificates (Bachelor's, HSC, SSC)", "CV", "Motivation letter", "2 recommendation letters (typical)", "Proof of English proficiency"]
scholarships.english_requirement: IELTS/TOEFL, OR a Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate from a prior English-medium degree - accepted by many (not all) programmes as a substitute for a test score
application_method: ["Apply directly to the institution running the selected Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programme.", "Erasmus+", "Depending on what part of the programme you are applying for, you will need to fill out a specific application form.", "For the decentralised activities managed by National Agencies , please apply using the Erasmus+ and European Solidarity Corps page .", "The partner search on the EU's Funding and Tenders portal helps you search for potential partners for your proposal.", "This page focuses on guidance for organisations to apply for grants and calls for proposals under Erasmus+ and the European Solidarity Corps."]
scholarships.selection_notes: Highly competitive. Selection depends on academic background, motivation, recommendation letters and programme-specific requirements.
scholarships.program_type: Joint Master Programme
scholarships.best_fit: Accessible for average-CGPA applicants with a strong personal motivation/story - no fixed CGPA cutoff, evaluated more holistically than most government scholarships
scholarships.notes: This is a category of 50+ separate Joint Master's programmes (each its own university consortium), not one application. Applicants pick and apply directly to specific joint-programme(s) via the Erasmus Mundus Catalogue on erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu. Deadlines are set per-programme.

scholarships.name: ICCR Scholarship (Suborno Jayanti Scheme)

scholarships.description: The Suborno Jayanti Scholarship Scheme is the ICCR scheme for nationals of Bangladesh, subsuming the earlier Bangladesh schemes previously offered by ICCR. Under it, the Government of India through ICCR provides scholarship at UG, PG and Ph.D level in Indian universities. Applications are made online on the ICCR A2A Scholarship Portal and must be submitted through the Indian Mission in the applicant's country, which then forwards them to empanelled Indian State and Central Universities. Registration for the 2026-27 academic year is closed and the portal currently lists 2026-27 as the only registration year.

scholarships.title: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS)
scholarships.name: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS)
scholarships.description: The Global Korea Scholarship is the Republic of Korea's representative government-invited scholarship programme, administered by the National Institute for International Education (NIIED), which invites outstanding students from around the world to study at Korean universities. It funds Korean language training plus associate degree, bachelor's, master's and doctoral degree programmes across more than 80 GKS universities, and also runs an exchange students programme and Korea-Japan exchange programmes. Applicants apply either through their Korean embassy (Embassy Track) or directly to a GKS university (University Track), and the scholarship covers airfare, Korean language training fees, tuition and monthly allowances.
scholarships.duration: Korean language training (1 year) + associate degree (2-3 years), bachelor's degree (4-6 years), master's degree (2 years), doctoral degree (3 years)
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle: NIIED announces in September, Embassy Track applications are submitted in September and University Track applications in September to November, screening runs October to December and final results are announced in December.

benefits: ["Round-trip airfare; tuition support; Korean language training; monthly stipend; settlement allowance; medical insurance and other official benefits depending on track."]

There are two application routes: a recommendation from a Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission, or a recommendation from a Japanese university. The scholarship pays a monthly stipend, exempts tuition and provides a round-trip travel allowance (airfare), and in most tracks includes Japanese language training before or during study.

scholarships.description: France Excellence Charpak is the French government scholarship programme in India, divided into four sub-programmes that allow Indian students to study at undergraduate or postgraduate level in public and private institutions in France. The Master track is designed for one to two years of study at Master's level across all streams and fields, and awardees receive the status of Boursier du Government Français. The Master track pays a monthly living allowance of EUR 860 and covers visa and Campus France procedure fee exemption, student social security and complementary health insurance, accommodation assistance through Campus France in France, and reduced university restaurant meals at EUR 1. The scholarship does not cover travel expenses from India to France or within France, or any other expenses related to the awardee's stay.

scholarships.description: Since 2018 the Make Our Planet Great Again (MOPGA) initiative has been a flagship programme for postdoctoral mobility in France and one of the leading fellowship programmes of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. The 2027 call is the tenth edition, funded by MEAE in partnership with MESRE and implemented by Campus France, and enables young international researchers to carry out a research project in France. Each fellowship runs for 12 months and provides a monthly allowance of EUR 2,500, a EUR 500 settling-in allowance and health coverage including health insurance, civil liability insurance and repatriation assistance. Successful applicants receive the status of French Government Scholarship holder (BGF) and the fellowship is paid directly by Campus France.

scholarships.deadline: Varies by university (typically 1–3 months before departure)
scholarships.description: Erasmus+ helps organise student and doctoral candidate exchanges within countries fully part of the Erasmus+ programme and to and from countries associated to Erasmus+. It is open to short-cycle, Bachelor's and Master's students and to doctoral candidates registered at a participating higher education institution and enrolled in studies leading to a recognised degree. There is no central application form: students apply through the international or Erasmus+ office of their own institution, which selects applicants fairly and transparently. The grant contributes to travel and daily living costs with amounts varying by destination and demand, and Erasmus+ students are exempt from tuition, registration, examination and laboratory or library fees at the receiving institution. Mobilities run from 2 to 12 months for long-term study, or 5 to 30 days for short-term blended mobility, with up to 12 months in total per study cycle.
scholarships.duration: Long-term mobility: minimum 2 months to maximum 12 months abroad, including blended mobilities with a virtual component. Short-term mobility: 5 to 30 days abroad, which must be blended mobilities; only doctoral candidates can do a short-term mobility without a virtual component. Maximum total duration is 12 months within one study cycle, with more than one exchange possible within that limit. For one-cycle courses such as medicine or architecture, up to 24 months.
scholarships.application_period: Year-round through the sending institution, which publishes its own Erasmus+ selection deadlines for each academic year.

scholarships.description: France Excellence-Major is a French government scholarship run by AEFE for the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs that supports the best non-French baccalaureat holders from the network of French schools abroad to continue their higher education in France. Around 800 foreign students are supported at any one time over five years of study, and about 200 new holders join each year. Applications require pre-selection by the head of the French school abroad and online entry on the dedicated Cascade application, followed by assessment by the French embassy's cultural cooperation service and a selection commission convened by AEFE each May. Selection weighs school results, a coherent orientation project, involvement in school life and extracurricular activity, and motivation for demanding French higher education. Holders receive a family-need-rated monthly allowance of EUR 280 or EUR 860, complementary health cover, and, at the higher rates, round-trip travel and CROUS housing.

scholarships.title: Humboldt Research Fellowship
scholarships.name: Humboldt Research Fellowship
scholarships.deadline: Three calls annually: March 15, July 15, November 15 (2026 schedule)
scholarships.description: The Humboldt Research Fellowship sponsors researchers with above-average qualifications from across the globe to conduct their own research at a German host institution. For postdocs the monthly fellowship amount is €3,000 and for experienced researchers €3,600, plus additional benefits. On top of the fellowship amount the Foundation provides family benefits for children and partners, subsidies for private full health insurance, and travel expense allowances, as well as personal support throughout the sponsorship. The host institute generally receives an allowance for research costs of €800 per month for natural sciences and engineering, or €500 for humanities and social sciences.
scholarships.duration: Postdocs: 6 to 24 months, divided into up to three stays within three years. Experienced researchers: 6 to 18 months, divided into up to three stays within three years.

scholarships.selection_notes: The decision to award research fellowships is taken by a selection committee consisting of 60-70 researchers from various fields. Applications are academically evaluated by a peer review process based on: academic career and academic record to date (mobility, determination, thematic scope, academic productivity); quality of the key publications named in the application; originality and innovative potential of your proposed research; your future potential; and your independent research profile (for experienced researchers). The assessment also considers the individual life journey and educational background in terms of equal opportunities and accessibility. The Foundation expects 20-25% of the applications received to be approved.

scholarships.description: The Lester B. scholarships.description: The Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program is a U.S. Department of State fellowship, administered by the Institute of International Education, for mid-career professionals from eligible countries. It is a non-degree program: fellows may take academic coursework at a U.S. host university but do not earn a degree. The package covers host-university tuition and fees, a maintenance allowance with a one-time settling-in allowance, accident and sickness insurance, a book allowance, a one-time computer subsidy, international and programme-event air travel, and a professional development allowance. Applications go through each applicant's Binational Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy Public Affairs Section, so deadlines vary by country and nominations must reach IIE by mid-September.

scholarships.selection_notes: UBC states there are no exceptions to the eligibility criteria. As part of the evaluation process a financial assessment is carried out, reviewing documents outlining family gross income, expenses and family assets. Applicants are assessed on demonstrated leadership qualities, exceptional contributions to their communities, and outstanding academic performance (all As or equivalent standard). Applicants may be invited to a video interview to share more about themselves and reflect on past educational and leadership experiences beyond the written application. You do not select which award you wish to receive; the team automatically considers you for the awards you are eligible for. Applicants who apply to the International Scholars Program will not be considered for merit-based awards.

scholarships.best_fit: International students completing secondary school outside Canada who will enter UBC Vancouver or UBC Okanagan directly from an accredited secondary school for their first undergraduate degree, hold an all-As or equivalent record, can document a significant financial need, and can secure a nomination from a high school or qualifying registered non-profit.
scholarships.notes: Non-renewable status, deferral and return-home requirements are not published on the programme page. There is no published clinical restriction, but the following degrees are explicitly not eligible for UBC International Scholars Program awards: Bachelor of Nursing degree (Okanagan and Vancouver), Bachelor of Dental Science in Dental Hygiene, Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science, Bachelor + Master of Management degree, dual degrees, joint degrees between UBC Okanagan and UBC Vancouver, and joint degrees with other post-secondary institutions. Applicants may only be considered for either UBC's merit-based or its financial need-based award programme. Applicants must hold a Canadian study permit. Applicants started shortly before the deadline are less likely to be successful. Housing should not be applied for until award decisions are released, because the housing application deadline is May 1.

scholarships.deadline: Application deadline: February 19, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. ET. Applications open November 1st, 2026.
scholarships.description: The McMaster University Award of Excellence is McMaster's most prestigious international entrance award, valued at up to $200,000 over four years and renewable in Levels 2 to 4. It is open to international students paying international tuition fees who enter the Faculty of Business, Engineering, Humanities, Science or Social Sciences and who exemplify the highest standards of academic and personal achievement. Applicants must apply through AwardSpring and are assessed on personal growth and achievement, community engagement and contribution, and self-reflection. For the 2027 entry cycle applications open on November 1, 2026 and close on February 19, 2027 at 11:59 p.m. ET. Recipients must remain in their originally admitted faculty, stay enrolled full-time and continue paying international tuition fees in order to renew, so the award does not cover tuition.

scholarships.description: A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (AGS) funds up to four years of PhD or EngD study at an autonomous university in Singapore, jointly supervised by an A*STAR researcher and a university faculty member, with research conducted at an A*STAR Research Institute. Support published for up to 4 years comprises full tuition fees, a monthly sustenance allowance inclusive of CPF contribution where applicable, book, computer, conference and thesis allowances, and support for up to 12 months of overseas attachment. Monthly allowance is a published matrix by track and residency status: AGS (STEM) $4,500 for Singapore Citizens, $4,100 for Singapore Permanent Residents and $3,600 for International Students; AGS (Specialised Tracks: Semiconductor, Quantum, Computing) $6,200, $5,600 and $5,000 respectively.

scholarships.selection_notes: Referees can be academic referees from universities or supervisors/PIs whom you have worked with. There will be at least 2 rounds of interviews involving the senior management of the Biomedical Research Council or Science & Engineering Research Council, and researchers from A*STAR's Research Entities. The nomination of supervisor(s) has to be approved by A*STAR; in most cases the main and co-supervisors should hold at least the designation of Principal Investigator or Principal Scientist at an A*STAR RI. Final approval of the PhD supervisor(s), research project and university for successful applicants is subject to A*STAR's approval. A*STAR makes a holistic assessment of each application and takes into consideration factors such as achievements in science/maths related competitions and CCAs; prior research experience helps but is not mandatory. The application process typically takes about 5 months from submission of a complete application to notification of results.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: Final-semester undergraduates and Master's students at, or on track to graduate from, a Singapore autonomous university, and mid-PhD students already enrolled in a Singapore autonomous university, who want to do a research-intensive PhD at an A*STAR Research Institute. International students without Singapore Permanent Residence should be comfortable with a 3-year service commitment in a Singapore-based company.
scholarships.notes: Bond-free for Singapore citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents. Foreigners who are non-SPRs must serve a 3-year service commitment in Singapore-based companies, without commitment to any specific organisation; Singapore-based companies refer to local companies and international companies that have a base in Singapore and which is registered with the Accounting & Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA). The area of work should preferably be in Biomedical Sciences, Physical Sciences, Engineering or Computing and Information Sciences. Not deferrable within the 4-year funding period without approval: if you need more time to complete your PhD you will have to seek approval from A*STAR's management for your PhD extension. A*STAR does not pay for consumables or research fees; fees involved in the lab should be borne by the university. All scholars need to seek A*STAR's written permission before changing your course of study/research project. scholarships.description: The NUS International Undergraduate Scholarship is a University-level scholarship offered by the National University of Singapore to support exceptional students from all countries except Singapore who apply as freshmen to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NUS. Candidates are considered and shortlisted through their application for undergraduate admission to NUS, and selection interviews are held from January to July with outcomes notified by mid-July. Benefits comprise 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant, an S$5,800 annual living allowance, an S$5,000 annual accommodation allowance and a S$1,750 one-time computer allowance upon enrolment. The award is renewed each semester provided the holder maintains a GPA of at least 3.5 (or top 80% of cohort for Dentistry, Law and Medicine) and good conduct.

scholarships.description: The Nanyang President's Graduate Scholarship (NPGS) is a competitive and prestigious scholarship scheme offered by Nanyang Technological University to encourage outstanding graduates or final-year students to take their first step towards a leading research career by studying full-time for a PhD at NTU. It is described as the premier scholarship granted by NTU's President, recognising PhD students who exemplify exceptional academic, research and leadership qualities. Open to all nationalities, it requires an Honours (Highest Distinction) or equivalent at Bachelor's level, or official documentation confirming the candidate is on track to achieve it. Monthly stipends revised with effect from January 2026 are S$5,300 for Singapore Citizens, S$4,800 for Singapore Permanent Residents and S$4,300 for international students, with CPF contributions on top for Citizens. The award also covers the annual tuition fee and provides an overseas conference allowance of up to S$5,000 per financial year, an annual book allowance of S$500, a one-off IT allowance of S$1,500, a one-off thesis allowance of S$600 and priority for campus accommodation. There is no bond attached to the scholarship, though international students must perform teaching or laboratory supervision duties under the Graduate Assistantship Programme.
scholarships.duration: The award is tenable for one year in the first instance and is renewable subject to good progress. The maximum period of the Scholarship is 4 years for PhD candidates, as determined by school as well as availability of research funding in each case.

scholarships.description: The Lee Kong Chian Scholars' Programme is one of Singapore Management University's most prestigious undergraduate scholarships, made possible by a gift from the Lee Foundation, with up to 60 scholarships funded. It is open to full-time SMU first-year undergraduates of any nationality taking a single or double degree programme, and requires a second major or an equivalent breadth requirement, demonstrated leadership and communications skills, and a substantial record of co-curricular activity or community service. Benefits comprise a waiver of annual subsidised tuition fees for regular terms for up to four years, a S$16,000 Global Opportunities grant funding overseas exchange, community service or competitions, a S$5,000 annual living allowance, a S$1,800 one-time computer allowance, and development opportunities from SMU's Student Success Centre. Applicants are considered through the Scholarship section of the standard admission application, with no separate scholarship form. The scholarship is bond-free, but non-Singaporean scholars must sign a Ministry of Education Tuition Grant agreement obliging them to work for Singapore-based companies for three years after graduation.

Berea advises that "Applying by the Early Action deadlines is highly recommended, as admission is selective and space in the incoming class is limited." All applicants must also submit a FAFSA, which is available from October 1 with an expected priority filing date of October 31.
scholarships.description: Berea College plans to move to a fully funded program model for all students by fall 2027, expanding its tuition-free approach to cover housing and meal plans with no student loans.
scholarships.duration: Four years, renewed annually while the student remains enrolled and files the FAFSA each year

International applicants use 15 October for Early Action and 15 January for Regular Decision. The FAFSA is refiled every year, available from 1 October with a 31 October priority date.

scholarships.eligibility_summary: First-year applicants, domestic or international, who show strong academic accomplishments and come from families with limited financial resources and who meet Berea's financial eligibility requirement, which the College assesses from the FAFSA using household size and adjusted gross income bands. scholarships.english_requirement: Not specified on the Berea Tuition Promise pages. International applicants are welcomed and must meet the College's general admission requirements; the College states it welcomes applicants "from across the United States and from other countries".
application_method: ["Complete the Application for Admission and Scholarship online at the Berea admissions portal at no cost", "File the FAFSA, which the FAFSA becomes available each October 1", "Ask a high school guidance counsellor to complete the School Counselor Evaluation Form, unless exempt", "Ask a core subject teacher to submit the teacher recommendation", "Submit by the applicable Early Action or Regular Decision date for domestic or international applicants", "Complete any additional financial documentation the Office of Admissions requests during the financial eligibility assessment"]
scholarships.selection_notes: The admissions process is holistic, weighing the completed application, official academic records, test scores where submitted, financial eligibility, recommendations and endorsements, conversations with an admissions counsellor, extracurricular and co-curricular activity, community service, character and personal qualities, and demonstrated interest in the College. Admitted students average a 3.65 high school GPA and qualify for federal Pell Grants, and Berea is academically competitive with an average ACT of about 25 and more than half of first-year students ranked in the top fifth of their high school class. Well qualified applicants may be accepted for fall admission as early as December, though an early application alone does not ensure admission.
scholarships.program_type: Need-aware tuition promise awarded to all admitted students, not a competitive merit scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: Students with strong academic potential from families with limited financial resources who want a tuition-free bachelor's degree at a work college in Kentucky, and who are willing to meet Berea's unique financial eligibility test.
scholarships.notes: This is not a competitive merit award that applicants win. Berea has not charged tuition for more than 130 years, and the Tuition Promise Scholarship is applied after all other aid is considered, so every admitted student receives it. It is awarded to admitted students rather than at application stage, which matters for applicants who assume they must win it. Housing, food and fees remain payable for current cohorts, but from Fall 2027 the College's Financial Freedom Pledge guarantees 100% of tuition, housing, food, fees and supplies without loans for all students until graduation. Endowment earnings provide 74% of the College's operating budget, state and federal aid 19% and donors the remaining 7%.

Families with income up to $200,000 receive free tuition plus aid for additional costs. Aid is need-blind with respect to admission.

scholarships.description: Dartmouth College meets 100% of the demonstrated need of all admitted financial aid applicants, regardless of citizenship or entry round, and its financial aid packages never include a required student loan. Need is calculated as cost of attendance minus family contribution, with direct expenses of tuition, fees, food and housing and indirect expenses such as travel, books, supplies and laundry. Families with total annual income below $125,000 with typical assets can expect no parent contribution, while families earning between $125,000 and $175,000 with typical assets can expect a scholarship or grants covering the full cost of tuition. International applicants file the CSS Profile with school code 3351, or the International Student Financial Aid Application if the CSS fee is a serious hardship. Financial aid deadlines are November 1 for Early Decision and February 1 for Regular Decision.

scholarships.name: Rotary Peace Fellowship
scholarships.deadline: Applications are submitted online to The Rotary Foundation and the global deadline is 15 May. scholarships.description: The Rotary Peace Fellowship is funded by The Rotary Foundation and awards up to 170 fellowships a year for leaders with work experience in peace and development to study at one of eight Rotary Peace Centers. Each year up to 50 fellowships fund master's degrees and up to 120 fund professional development certificate studies at partner universities. Fellowships cover tuition and fees, room and board, round-trip transportation, and internship and field-study expenses. Master's programmes run 15 to 24 months and include a self-designed two- to three-month field study, while the certificate programme is a one-year blended learning course for working professionals that includes field studies and a social change initiative. Fellowships cannot be used for doctoral study. Applications open in February and the global deadline is 15 May; the 2027-28 cycle is closed and the 2028-29 cycle opens in February 2027.

scholarships.description: The University of Bologna awards 30 International Talents @unibo study grants each year to international students who matriculate for the first time in the first year of a Second Cycle (Laurea Magistrale) degree programme. Each grant is worth EUR 6,500 gross per academic year and is awarded for two academic years, and successful applicants also receive a full tuition fee waiver, paying only EUR 157.04 in regional taxes, stamp duty and insurance premium. Selection is based on GRE General Test scores, with minimum scores of 290 in the combined Verbal and Quantitative Reasoning sections and 3.0 in Analytical Writing, together with a family economic situation within an ISEE band of EUR 16,000 to EUR 35,000. scholarships.description: Politecnico di Milano runs an annual merit-based scholarship scheme for international candidates applying to the first year of an English-taught Master of Science programme. The 2027/2028 call offers 64 awards: 10 Platinum (Milan), 18 Gold (Milan), 16 Gold Piacenza Campus, 10 Bronze Piacenza Campus and 10 Silver scholarships for the Cremona, Lecco, Mantova and Piacenza campuses. Every award includes a full tuition-fee waiver for the academic year, and the cash tiers add a gross allowance of EUR 10,000 (Platinum), EUR 8,000 (Gold), EUR 5,000 (Gold Piacenza) or EUR 2,500 (Bronze); the Silver tier is a waiver only. Recipients must pay a non-refundable administrative fee of about EUR 170 on acceptance, and the awards can be renewed for a second year on academic points.

scholarships.deadline: There is no separate scholarship deadline: the application for the degree programme automatically makes the candidate eligible, so the deadline is the admission deadline of the chosen degree programme, published in its Admission Notice. scholarships.description: The University of Padua awards up to 76 Padua International Excellence Scholarships each year to the most deserving international candidate on each degree programme delivered entirely in English. Each scholarship is worth EUR 8,000.00 gross per academic year plus full exemption from student fees, leaving only the regional right-to-education tax and the revenue stamp payable. There is no separate scholarship application: applying to an eligible English-taught degree programme by its admission deadline makes the candidate eligible automatically. Selection is made by the Teaching Committee of each degree programme on academic excellence and the quality of the candidate's prior academic record, with the youngest candidate preferred in a tie.

scholarships.application_period: Aligned with each degree programme's admission call. The 2027/2028 call is due in November 2026.

scholarships.description: The University of Trento awards a limited number of merit scholarships to citizens of countries outside the European Union who live outside Italy and enrol in a degree programme, based on their admission score and programme of study. The scholarship is worth EUR 7,200 per year, or EUR 8,500 per year for female students enrolled in STEM programmes, and scholarship holders are also exempted from paying tuition fees for that year. It is paid in two instalments, the second conditional on earning at least half of the credits required by the course in the January and February exam sessions. The award lasts a maximum of two years on a master's programme and three years on an undergraduate programme.

For first-year Master of Science international candidates the windows are 28 January to 8 February 2027, 4 to 18 March 2027, 13 to 27 April 2027 and 10 to 18 June 2027.
scholarships.description: The ISU Bocconi Scholarship is Bocconi University's implementation of the Italian Right to University Education Scholarship for students entering the first year of a Bachelor of Science, Integrated Master of Arts in Law or Master of Science programme in academic year 2027-2028. It combines a cash stipend with services and supplements, including a free daily meal valued at EUR 829.00 for a.y. 2026-27, access to preferential-rate canteen services and a 200-hour work-study programme. Eligibility depends on three separate tests: enrolment for the absolute first year, an economic test set annually by the Lombardy Region (ISEE/ISEEU Parificato not above EUR 26,887.93 and ISPE/ISPEEU Parificato not above EUR 58,452.06 for a.y. 2026-27), and a merit test verified after the fact through credit thresholds. International candidates apply under this call, while Bocconi and Italian applicants are directed to the separate Bocconi4Access to Education call.
scholarships.duration: One academic year per application; the benefit is not automatic and must be reapplied for each year of enrolment
scholarships.application_period: Multiple fixed windows per admission session, not yet open on the verification date: from 12 November 2026 for the first Bachelor of Science and Law international window, then 15 March to 5 April 2027, with Master of Science international rounds between 28 January and 18 June 2027. Applications submitted after the deadline or in a different modality will not be evaluated.

scholarships.title: Talents 4 UniTo — Two-Year Scholarships for International Students Enrolling in English-Taught Master's Degrees (University of Turin)
scholarships.name: Talents 4 UniTo — Two-Year Scholarships for International Students Enrolling in English-Taught Master's Degrees (University of Turin)
scholarships.deadline: Applications had to be submitted on apply.unito.it between 25 November 2025 and 29 January 2026 for the a.y. 2026-2027 cycle, and that call is now closed. Rankings were published from 14 May 2026, and ranking scroll was not possible after 30 November 2026. The next edition's window had not been published on 4 October 2026.
scholarships.description: Talents 4 UniTo is the University of Turin's programme of 40 two-year scholarships for talented international students enrolling for the first time in a postgraduate degree without a restricted number of places taught in English. Each scholarship is worth EUR 20,000 gross in total (EUR 10,000 per academic year) and holders are exempt from university tuition fees, except for the first instalment due for enrolment in each academic year. Candidates are international students who hold a qualification obtained outside the Italian system valid for admission to a postgraduate degree, do not hold Italian citizenship and are not resident in Italy. There is no separate application form: applicants are included automatically if they apply on apply.unito.it for up to two eligible programmes during the published window. Selection is carried out per programme by an Evaluation Teaching Committee on a 50-point scale with a 36-point eligibility threshold, and two scholarships are awarded per programme.
scholarships.duration: 2 years (two academic years), paid in four instalments of EUR 5,000 gross
scholarships.application_period: Annual call with a fixed window. For a.y. 2026-2027 the Apply@Unito application window opened on 25 November 2025 and closed on 29 January 2026; rankings followed from 14 May 2026. The previous edition funded 38 scholarships, and the 2027-2028 call was not published at the verification date.

scholarships.title: UNICORE 8.0 University Corridors for Refugees — University of Turin Scholarship (a.y. 2026-2027 / 2027-2028)
scholarships.name: UNICORE 8.0 University Corridors for Refugees — University of Turin Scholarship (a.y. 2026-2027 / 2027-2028)
scholarships.deadline: Applications had to be submitted exclusively through the online procedure at https://universitycorridors.unhcr.it/ by 17 April 2026 at 12:00 (noon, Italian time, UTC+2). That window has closed and the 2026/2028 edition is complete; the next edition had not been published on 4 October 2026.
scholarships.description: UNICORE 8.0 (University Corridors for Refugees) is a project promoted by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees that creates educational corridors from selected countries in Africa and Asia to Italy, in partnership with MAECI, Caritas Italiana, Diaconia Valdese and a group of Italian universities. For the 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 academic years the University of Turin awards three two-year cash-and-services scholarships for refugee students to access its open-access, English-taught Master's degree programmes. Each scholarship provides a cash benefit of EUR 7,000 gross per academic year plus exemption from all amounts due for university enrolment, except the first instalment of the student contribution. The award is paid in four instalments by bank transfer to an Italian bank account, with each payment conditional on enrolment and credit milestones.

scholarships.application_period: Annual project edition with a single common deadline across participating universities. scholarships.description: The Taiwan Scholarship Program of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of China (Taiwan), funds international students for degree programmes or a pre-degree Mandarin Language Enrichment Program at Mandarin-teaching institutions affiliated with MOE-accredited universities. Recipients receive a monthly stipend of NT$33,000 for degree programmes or NT$28,000 for the LEP, plus one-way economy-class air tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan, and must cover all other expenses themselves. The award period is one year for the LEP, up to four years for undergraduate and doctoral study and two years for a master's, with a five-year total cap. Applications are accepted from 1 February to 31 March each year, and the programme is open to students of any country except mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, in principle prioritising Taiwan's diplomatic partners.
scholarships.duration: Pre-degree LEP: one year. Degree programmes: undergraduate maximum four years, master's maximum two years, doctoral maximum four years. Award periods must be continuous with no breaks and cannot exceed five years in total.
scholarships.application_period: Annual window from 1 February to 31 March, applying to the Taiwan Scholarship cycle for the following academic year. The February-March 2026 window has closed; the next is expected 1 February to 31 March 2027.

scholarships.description: The Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) established the Huayu Enrichment Scholarship to encourage international students to study Mandarin Chinese in Taiwan. The award funds a 2-month summer course or a 3-month, 6-month, 9-month or one-year course, and pays a monthly stipend of NT$28,000. Applicants must be foreign nationals aged 18 or over with an excellent academic record and good moral character, must already have applied to a Chinese language centre, and must submit their documents to the ROC overseas office for their country of nationality. MOE publishes no single deadline date, noting only that applications are made 'before the deadline specified in the scholarship guidelines issued by that authorized overseas office (usually in January or February each year)'.
scholarships.duration: A 2-month summer course, or a 3-month, 6-month, 9-month or one-year course.
scholarships.application_period: Annual, with the deadline set by each applicant's own ROC overseas mission or representative office, which MOE says is 'usually in January or February each year'. The round for the current cycle has closed as of 2026-10-04; the next nominations are expected in January or February 2027.

scholarships.title: Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP) - Ph.D. Scholarship and Stipend, Academia Sinica
scholarships.name: Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP) - Ph.D. Scholarship and Stipend, Academia Sinica
scholarships.deadline: The TIGP Admission Office receives online applications 'from November 1st to February 1st every year' (GMT+8). The most recent cycle, for fall 2026 entry, closed at 1 February 2026 and admissions results were announced on 20 July 2026. No application announcement for the next cycle had been posted as of 2026-10-04, so no exact calendar date is recorded.
scholarships.description: The Taiwan International Graduate Program (TIGP), administered by Academia Sinica with partner universities, admits international students to fourteen English-taught Ph.D. programmes and pays a tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month for the first year, extendable for one further year for students who perform well. Academia Sinica also subsidises the difference between international and domestic tuition fees for five consecutive years, but students still pay the domestic tuition rate, stated as roughly NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 per semester for the remainder. Applications are submitted online between 1 November and 1 February (GMT+8) with no application fee, and admission results are usually announced in late June or early July for enrolment the following fall.

scholarships.title: International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program)
scholarships.name: International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program)
scholarships.deadline: There is no single INTENSE deadline. Each participating university sets its own application window and nomination deadline per intake, and the two intakes do not coincide. Windows published by partner universities for 2027 Spring include 10 September to 12 October 2026 (NCHU), 1 to 22 October 2026 (NCU) and 21 September to 23 October 2026 (KMU), all GMT+8; for 2027 Fall, NTUT publishes a student nomination deadline of 10 March 2027. Applications for several 2027 Spring intakes are open as of 2026-10-04.
scholarships.description: The International Industrial Talents Education Special Program (INTENSE Program) is a Ministry of Education initiative, run with the National Development Council, participating universities and partner companies to recruit international students into industry-linked degree programmes in key fields such as STEM, finance and semiconductors. Admitted students receive full tuition and credit waivers for up to two years, a one-way flight ticket to Taiwan, initial administrative expense support and a monthly living allowance of at least NT$10,000 paid by the partner company, plus paid internships, in exchange for an obligation to work in Taiwan after graduation. Applications are made to individual participating universities, which publish their own deadlines for each Spring and Fall intake, so there is no single programme-wide application date.
scholarships.duration: Typically a two-year degree programme of study plus internship, followed by employment in Taiwan.
scholarships.application_period: Two intakes a year. Spring intake first round runs from early October to late December and second round from early April to late June; the Fall intake mirrors those two rounds. Each participating university publishes its own exact dates, so no single application period applies.
scholarships.official_source: Ministry of Education (MOE), Republic of China (Taiwan), with the National Development Council, participating universities and partner companies

English-taught programmes require CEFR B1 English at admission; Chinese-taught programmes require TOCFL Level B1.

Admission is therefore per programme and per intake, with results typically announced in the middle of the year for a September start and in mid-January for a February start.

scholarships.notes: This is a multi-university national programme, so benefits and deadlines are not uniform. Published packages differ by university: one partner advertises full tuition and credit waivers for up to two years, a one-way flight ticket, initial administrative expense support and an NT$10,000 monthly industry-sponsored stipend, while another caps tuition and miscellaneous-fee subsidy at NT$50,000 per semester for up to two years and lists partner-company stipends between NT$10,000 and NT$15,000 depending on the job and Chinese-proficiency requirement. The scheme carries an employment obligation: the stipend duration matches the work-obligation duration and repayment may be requested if the contract is violated. The stored official_source_url and application_link both point to NTU's Overseas Compatriot and Mainland Chinese Students Advising Division, which does not host this programme.

scholarships.title: NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship
scholarships.name: NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship
scholarships.deadline: The published application period on NTU's International Student Services scholarships page is April 23, 2026 - May 15, 2026, submitted through the International Degree Current Student System. The 2026 window has closed; the same window is expected for the next cycle.
scholarships.description: The NTU International Outstanding Graduate Student Scholarship supports current international graduate students at National Taiwan University through a matching-fund structure: NTU waives the student's tuition, while the student's thesis or dissertation supervisor pays a monthly research-assistant salary, with published minimums of TWD 6,000 per month for two years for master's students and TWD 8,000 per month for three years for PhD students, before tax. Applicants must first secure a professor willing to sponsor them and sign the university's word form, and must pass an annual review to keep the award. The published application period is 23 April to 15 May, through NTU's International Degree Current Student System, and roughly half of applicants are awarded.
scholarships.duration: Minimum monthly support for two years for master's students and three years for PhD students, subject to passing an annual review.
scholarships.application_period: Annual, with a published application period of 23 April to 15 May for existing international degree students at NTU, applying through the International Degree Current Student System.

Applicants should approach potential supervisors before applying. Do not confuse it with NTU's other awards on the same pages, which have different amounts: the NTU Scholarship for International Degree Student (undergraduate) carries a tuition waiver plus a monthly stipend of NTD 8,000, with tuition fees waived up to NTD 65,000; the NTU Loyalty Award pays NTD 100,000 for master's and NTD 200,000 for PhD places; and the Financial Assistance Grant for International Students is a tuition waiver plus a TWD 6,000 monthly stipend. scholarships.title: NTHU International Student Scholarship
scholarships.name: NTHU International Student Scholarship
scholarships.deadline: The scholarship has no separate deadline: NTHU instructs applicants to 'Apply scholarship through the same online system for international degree programs', so the deadline is the admission deadline for the relevant intake. NTHU's published Spring 2027 international degree application period was 3 August to 30 September 2026 at 15:00 Taiwan time, which has closed.
scholarships.description: The NTHU International Student Scholarship, funded by the Office of Global Affairs at National Tsing Hua University, is applied for through the same online system as admission to an NTHU international degree programme. It provides a full tuition and credit-fee waiver plus a tiered monthly stipend: NTD 20,000 to 40,000 per month for doctoral students, NTD 10,000 per month for doctoral students in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences or the International Intercollegiate PhD Program with supervisors from that college, and NTD 5,000 per month for master and bachelor students. It is restricted to applicants who and whose parents have always held foreign nationality and never held Taiwan nationality, excludes overseas Chinese student status, and is not available for Medicine, Dentistry, Traditional Chinese Medicine, the College of Semiconductor or ICDF programmes.
scholarships.duration: Follows the duration of the degree programme enrolled in; no separate award period is published.
scholarships.application_period: Applied for together with the international degree programme admission, in NTHU's published intake windows. The published Spring 2027 international degree application period was 3 August to 30 September 2026 (15:00 Taiwan time), with admission results on 1 December 2026 and scholarship results in late December 2026.

scholarships.title: NYCU Elite Ph.D. Scholarship for New Students
scholarships.name: NYCU Elite Ph.D. Scholarship for New Students
scholarships.deadline: No application deadline exists for this award. NYCU states that the Elite Ph.D. Scholarship "is awarded based on recommendations from the college and a review by the scholarship committee, not through the application submitted by the students". The only recurring dates are the per-semester deadline by which existing recipients must submit transcripts and tuition payment receipts to stay eligible the following semester.
scholarships.description: The NYCU Elite Ph.D. Scholarship for New Students awards a monthly stipend of NT$33,000 together with a tuition waiver for two years to new doctoral students at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University who have outstanding grades and hold no other scholarship or grant from the Taiwan government. It is not open to direct application: NYCU states that the award is made on the basis of recommendations from the college and a review by the scholarship committee. Recipients must submit semester transcripts and tuition payment receipts before a per-semester deadline to remain eligible, and the stipend is in principle deposited on the 10th of each month. The tuition waiver covers basic tuition only, with dormitory, insurance and campus facility fees remaining payable.
scholarships.duration: Two years of monthly stipend plus tuition waiver, per NYCU's published 'Scholarship Content and Duration'.
scholarships.application_period: Not student-applied. New Ph.D. places are nominated by the candidate's college and reviewed by the scholarship committee within NYCU's doctoral admission cycle. Existing recipients must submit transcripts and tuition payment receipts each semester before a per-semester deadline to remain eligible in the following semester, and renewals are handled in the application period announced by the OIA.

scholarships.title: MOE Elite Scholarship Program for Lecturers from South and Southeast Asian and African Countries
scholarships.name: MOE Elite Scholarship Program for Lecturers from South and Southeast Asian and African Countries
scholarships.deadline: There is no single ministry deadline. Applicants apply through the participating university's admission application, and the published application windows have been mid-December to mid-March for Fall entry (National Cheng Kung University's AY2026/27 window was mid-December 2025 to mid-March 2026). After admission results, the university emails the MOE-Elite guidelines, forms and upload links, and applicants must submit by the deadline stated in that email. MOE then announces recipients, around late October for Fall intake and late April for the African Spring intake.
scholarships.description: The MOE Elite Scholarship Program was created by the Ministry of Education of the Republic of China (Taiwan) under its New Southbound Policy to encourage university lecturers from South and Southeast Asian and African countries to pursue graduate degrees in Taiwan, with priority given to doctoral study. Awardees receive a total monthly award of NT$25,000 for up to two years of a master's programme or three years of a doctorate, reviewed annually; participating universities deduct tuition and credit fees from that total and pay the remainder to the student as a monthly stipend, which at Taipei Tech works out at around NT$14,000 per month in years one to three and NT$12,000 in year four. Applicants must currently hold a lecturer or more senior post at a university in an eligible country with that position on hold, must supply an up-to-date English Lecturer Certificate, and apply through the participating university, which submits the case for MOE review. Around 100 places are awarded per academic year across a three-year cycle.
scholarships.duration: Up to 2 years for a master's programme and up to 3 years for a doctoral programme under the standard MOE terms, reviewed annually. Some participating universities extend this, and Taipei Tech runs the award for up to 4 years.
scholarships.application_period: Tied to each participating university's admission cycle, with published Fall application windows running from around mid-December to mid-March, followed by a post-admission document submission stage with its own email-stated deadline. MOE announces recipient lists around late October for Fall and late April for the African Spring intake. The AY2026/27 Fall window closed in mid-March 2026; the next is expected to open around mid-December 2026 for 2027 Fall entry.

scholarships.selection_notes: The programme is administered under the MOE Elite Scholarship Program Action Plan and was created in accordance with the New Southbound Policy Work Plan announced by the Executive Yuan in December 2016, under the MOE New Southbound Policy Talent Development Program. Priority is given to doctoral programmes. The university evaluates the admission application by department, and the MOE then reviews and determines the scholarship award. Published quota: one hundred students per academic year over three academic years, for a total of three hundred students. MOE allocates the quota, so entry is limited to new PhD students in the relevant intakes and can involve a waitlist.
scholarships.program_type: Government graduate scholarship for university lecturers from South, Southeast Asia and Africa to study in Taiwan (Ministry of Education, New Southbound Policy talent development)
scholarships.best_fit: University lecturers, assistant professors and professors from South and Southeast Asian or African countries who have secured an offer from a participating Taiwanese university, whose institution can place their post on hold, and who hold an up-to-date English Lecturer Certificate.
scholarships.notes: Critical money nuance: NT$25,000 per month is the TOTAL award, not the amount in the student's pocket. Participating universities deduct tuition and credit fees from that total first and split only the remainder into a monthly stipend. Taipei Tech publishes the resulting figures as around NT$14,000 per month in years 1 to 3 and NT$12,000 per month in year 4. Applicants should not budget on NT$25,000 of disposable income. Duration also varies by university: the standard MOE terms are 2 years for a master's and 3 years for a doctorate with annual review, while Taipei Tech runs the award for up to 4 years and restricts it to newly admitted PhD students. The scheme is quota-limited at 100 places per academic year, and waitlisted candidates approved by MOE must repay any previously disbursed stipends. Do not confuse this with MOE's Taiwan Scholarship Program, which pays tuition and miscellaneous expenses up to NT$40,000 per semester plus a monthly living allowance of NT$15,000 or NT$20,000.

scholarships.description: The University of Lausanne awards around ten excellence scholarships each year, exclusively to students who have graduated from a foreign university and whose academic results are of a very high standard. The scholarship is paid for the minimum statutory period of the Master's programme at CHF 1,600 per month, and recipients are exempt from the standard course registration fees, with only the CHF 80 semester fees remaining payable. UNIL states explicitly that the amount does not constitute full funding, since about CHF 2,000 per month is needed to live in Lausanne. Applications for the 2027/2028 academic year are open until 1 November 2026.

scholarships.description: The Alfred Werner Scholarship Program of the SCS Foundation, a partner organisation of the Swiss Chemical Society, supports highly talented international students who obtained their BSc outside Switzerland and wish to pursue an MSc in Chemistry, Biochemistry or the Pharmaceutical Sciences at a Swiss university or one of the Swiss Federal Institutes of Technology. Scholarships are awarded to candidates nominated by the academic institutions to which they have been admitted; the Foundation does not accept direct applications. The current call covers Master's Student Scholarships 2027-2029 with a submission deadline of 25 March 2027.

scholarships.deadline: Vacancies are published as recruitment rounds on the CERN careers site, with the deadline set on each individual vacancy. As of 2026-10-04 the Doctoral Studentship page lists live rounds under the reference TSC-2027-1/DOCT (Doctoral Student Programme 2027-1, 12 to 36 month contract).
scholarships.description: The CERN Doctoral Student Programme is a PhD-level employment contract in which doctoral students carry out cutting-edge research at CERN in collaboration with their university, in fields spanning physics, engineering, applied physics, electronics, electrical engineering, information technologies, chemical and process engineering, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, data science and AI, and technology transfer. The programme pays a monthly net allowance of CHF 3,907 together with CERN health insurance, a possible family supplement, possible travel to Geneva on joining, and 30 days of paid leave plus two weeks of annual closure. Contracts run six months and are renewable up to three years, with the possibility of spreading the total over a maximum of four consecutive years. Eligibility is limited to nationals of CERN Member or Associate Member States, and applicants from Pakistan, Lithuania, Latvia, Cyprus, Croatia and Turkey are currently excluded because the Article II.5 ceiling has been reached.

scholarships.notes: This is a paid employment contract, not a grant, so CERN does not pay tuition: the doctoral student remains enrolled at and pays fees to their own university. Funding figures on CERN programmes are periodically revised, so the CHF 3,907 net monthly allowance should be re-checked against the live page. The nationality exclusion list is time-limited and states that it reflects a ceiling under Article II.5 of the Associate Membership Agreement. Vacancies are published per round, so there is no single annual deadline.

scholarships.title: CERN Research Fellowship
scholarships.name: CERN Research Fellowship
scholarships.deadline: Vacancies are published as recruitment rounds on the CERN careers site, with the deadline set on each individual vacancy. As of 2026-10-04 the Research Fellowship page lists live vacancies including 'ATS Research Fellowship (Applied Physics and Engineering)', reference REF4103L, and 'Research Fellowship: Theoretical Physics', reference TH-2026-1/Cat1, both 24-month contracts.
scholarships.description: The CERN Research Fellowship Programme, part of CERN's broader Graduate Programme, is an opportunity for recent PhD graduates in physics and engineering to conduct advanced research in science, technology, engineering and mathematics at CERN. It pays a monthly net stipend of either CHF 7,004 or CHF 7,425 depending on the degree and years of post-graduation experience, together with CERN health insurance for the fellow, their partner and children, a contribution to the CERN Pension Fund, and depending on individual circumstances an installation grant, family, child and infant allowances and travel to Geneva on joining. Fellows receive 30 days of paid leave per year plus two weeks of CERN's annual closure, and on-the-job and formal training including language classes. Contracts run 6 to 24 months with the possibility of extension up to 36 months. Applicants must be nationals of a CERN Member or Associate Member State, must hold a PhD or obtain one within six months, must respect a research-experience cap of six years for Theoretical and Experimental Physics or three years for Applied Sciences and Engineering, and must never previously have held a CERN fellow or graduate contract.
scholarships.duration: 6 to 24 months, with the possibility of extension up to 36 months
scholarships.application_period: Continuous, round-based recruitment. Each published vacancy carries its own application deadline, and the page warns that vacancies under Experimental Physics, Applied Science and Engineering, and Theoretical Physics each correspond to distinct and separate recruitment processes.

scholarships.title: IMD MBA Scholarships
scholarships.name: IMD MBA Scholarships
scholarships.deadline: Most IMD MBA scholarships are open throughout 2026, available until allocated. The BackPack Scholarship for Women has a fixed deadline of 14 July. Bursary applications follow the admissions application deadline.
scholarships.description: IMD Business School offers a portfolio of scholarships and need-based bursaries for candidates applying to and entering its one-year full-time MBA in Lausanne. Six named scholarships were listed as open in October 2026: the MBA5 Scholarship of CHF 50,000, the Hilti STEM Scholars Program of CHF 50,000, the Nestle Scholarship for Women of CHF 40,000, the Forté Scholarship for Women of CHF 30,000, IMD MBA Merit Scholarships of up to CHF 40,000, and the BackPack Scholarship for Women with full funding. Most run throughout 2026 on an available-until-allocated basis, while the BackPack Scholarship closes on 14 July. Scholarships are applied for through the Program section of the MBA application form and are awarded to candidates who have applied for and accepted an offer, with selection based on academic and professional excellence, GMAT/GRE scores, career progression, international exposure and Assessment Day performance. Separate need-based bursaries are awarded on proven financial need and confirmed on an ongoing basis.

scholarships.application_period: Scholarships: throughout 2026 until allocated, except the BackPack Scholarship for Women which closes on 14 July. Bursaries: the same deadline as the admissions application.

scholarships.name: University of Basel Financial Aid and Scholarships
scholarships.deadline: The page publishes no central deadline. It links to a dedicated Submission Deadlines page under Advice and Support > Funding > Scholarships, and directs students to the scholarship office of their canton of residence, whose own deadlines apply.
scholarships.description: The University of Basel's scholarship page explains how study funding is structured in Switzerland: essentially, the parents and the scholarship office in the parents' canton of residence are responsible for funding studies, and scholarships from the university are granted by the scholarship committee of the Senate in addition to any cantonal education contributions. The university additionally awards specific scholarships to students in exchange programmes, advised by the Student Exchange Office, and its Social Services student welfare office offers advice. The page signposts the cantonal scholarship and student loan offices for Basel-Stadt and Basel-Landschaft as well as ausbildungsbeitraege.ch for all cantons, and advises international students to find out what scholarships they are eligible for in their home country.

scholarships.title: WIPO Fellowship Program
scholarships.name: WIPO Fellowship Program
scholarships.deadline: Fellowship positions may be advertised through calls for expressions of interest published on WIPO's career website, or via WIPO's LinkedIn or other social media channels. No fixed central deadline is published on the programme page.
scholarships.description: WIPO's Fellowship Program places professionals in specialized disciplines at the World Intellectual Property Organization in Geneva, Switzerland, for 12 to 36 months. Fellows are classified into four categories: translation fellows in the PCT Translation and Terminology Fellowship Program, legal case manager fellows in the WIPO Domain Name Fellowship Program, visiting and research fellows in the Research and Visiting Fellowship Program, and other specialized fellows. Applicants must hold at least a first-level university degree, with additional requirements such as professional experience, an advanced degree or specific competencies depending on the category. Fellows receive a monthly stipend of CHF 3,000 to CHF 8,000 depending on academic background and relevant experience, comprehensive medical and professional accident insurance largely paid by WIPO, relocation assistance covering travel at the start and end of the fellowship, assistance with visa formalities, 10 official holidays plus 2.5 days of annual leave per full month, and access to WIPO Academy training with up to six study leave days a year. Positions are advertised through calls for expressions of interest on WIPO's career website and LinkedIn.
scholarships.duration: 12 to 36 months; contracts run up to 12 months with the possibility of renewal for a total of up to three years
scholarships.application_period: Continuous, per vacancy. Positions are announced through calls for expressions of interest on WIPO's Taleo career site and on LinkedIn, so there is no single application window.

scholarships.description: The Leiden University Excellence Scholarship is a study scholarship for excellent students joining a full-time Leiden University master's programme starting in September, with the exception of the non-advanced LLM and MSc programmes of Leiden Law School. Applicants must normally hold a non-EEA/non-EFTA passport and not be eligible for Dutch student finance. scholarships.description: The University of Groningen's NL Scholarship is a one-time grant for international students from outside the EEA who wish to pursue a master's degree in the Netherlands, co-funded by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science and the university. scholarships.description: The Maastricht University NL-High Potential Scholarship programme awards 18 full scholarships each academic year, including a tuition fee waiver and a monthly stipend, to highly talented students from outside the EU who have been admitted to a Maastricht University master's programme. It combines the High Potential Scholarship, funded by the Maastricht University Scholarship Fund, with the ministry-funded NL Scholarship. For the 2027-2028 intake, scholarship applications run from 1 October 2026 to 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET), the participating master's application must be complete through Studielink before 10 December 2026, and applicants must be non-EU/EEA (also excluding Switzerland and Surinam), aged 35 or under on 1 September 2027, with a GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10 and no previous degree-seeking study in the Netherlands. Recipients receive a living-expense stipend of EUR 20,150 over 13 months or EUR 38,750 over 25 months, tuition fees, visa costs and EUR 700 of health and liability insurance paid at cost, a mandatory UM room until 16 July 2028 and a two-week Pre-Academic Training programme. Only about 2% of applicants are awarded.

Its value ranges from EUR 3,000 to EUR 22,000 for one year and is intended as compensation for study-related costs, with no costs such as tuition fees paid on the student's behalf; for two-year programmes a second-year award of an equal amount is possible if the student obtains an average grade of 7 out of 10 and at least 50 percent of the European Credits at the end of the third quartile of the first year. The official page states the VUFP 'covers the tuition fees only' and 'does not provide any additional allowance towards study or living costs, like rent, food, insurances'. scholarships.description: The LiU International Scholarship is a limited number of tuition-fee reductions awarded by Linköping University to fee-paying international master's students with significant academic potential; the tuition fee of an awardee is normally reduced by 50%. Applicants must have applied in the first admission round, ranked a LiU master's programme first, been admitted to that first choice in the first Notification of Selection Results, and met a minimum academic standard of GPA 3.5 on a 4.0 scale or equivalent. The application window opens on the day the Notification of Selection Results is published and closes a few days later - 26 to 30 March 2026 in the last published round - and no additional documents are required. Awards can cover 30 credits per semester, must be maintained by passing at least 75% of courses in the first academic year, and are rescinded if a Swedish Institute scholarship is awarded instead.

scholarships.title: Adelaide Academic Excellence Scholarship (50%)
scholarships.name: Adelaide Academic Excellence Scholarship (50%)
scholarships.deadline: Applications open from Monday 24 August 2026; applications are reviewed on a rolling basis with scholarship offers made throughout the recruitment cycle until all allocations have been exhausted.
scholarships.description: The Adelaide Academic Excellence Scholarship is a merit award for international students commencing an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree at Adelaide University, offering a 50% tuition fee reduction over the standard full-time duration of the degree. scholarships.title: Macquarie International Research Training Program (iRTP)
scholarships.name: Macquarie International Research Training Program (iRTP)
scholarships.deadline: Applications open 15 June 2026, close 31 July 2026 at 11pm for Session 1 2027. The next round's dates are not yet published.
scholarships.description: The International Research Training Program (iRTP) is the Australian Government's Research Training Program scholarship scheme for international graduate research students, administered by Macquarie University on behalf of the Department of Education. Successful PhD applicants receive a tuition fee offset for a maximum of three years plus a living allowance stipend of $40,900 per annum for up to three years and a travel concession on the local OPAL card. The award is open to international applicants commencing a full-time Master of Research or PhD at Macquarie in Session 1 2027, and those applying for an iRTP are automatically considered for the University-funded iMQRES. Applications for the 2027 round opened 15 June 2026 and closed 31 July 2026 at 11pm.

scholarships.application_period: Session 1 2027 international scholarship round: 15 June 2026 to 31 July 2026, 11pm.

Selection also considers the research environment, including project alignment with research strategy and priorities, the quality of the supervisory team, and the international standing of the research area. Outcomes for the 2027 round were due in early October 2026; applicants not notified by 15 November 2026 should consider the application unsuccessful.

scholarships.notes: Applicants to the iRTP are automatically considered for the University-funded iMQRES in the same round. The number of international places funded through the RTP varies from year to year.

scholarships.name: Western Australian Premier's University Scholarship
scholarships.deadline: Applications for Semester 2, 2026 closed at 3:00 PM (AWST) on Friday, 29 May 2026. The Department asks applicants to "check back soon for updates on when applications for Semester 1, 2027 will open"; no Semester 1, 2027 dates are published yet.
scholarships.description: The Western Australian Premier's University Scholarship is a Western Australian Government award that provides high-achieving international students with $50,000 towards their course fees and other university costs at one of Western Australia's five universities. Ten recipients are selected annually, with two awarded at each university. Applicants must be new offshore international students, citizens of one of 22 listed countries, and must apply directly to their chosen university, which assesses applications and selects the recipients. The Semester 2, 2026 round closed at 3:00pm AWST on 29 May 2026 and the Semester 1, 2027 round has not yet opened.

scholarships.title: La Trobe High Achiever Scholarship
scholarships.name: La Trobe High Achiever Scholarship
scholarships.deadline: Applications close 31/12/2027. The award was open from 10/02/2026 and the page status is Open, with automatic consideration rather than a separate scholarship form.
scholarships.description: The La Trobe High Achiever Scholarship rewards high-achieving international students with a reduction of up to 25% off annual tuition fees for the duration of their course. Applicants are automatically considered after submitting an application for a course on the University's list of eligible courses, and the percentage awarded is set by weighted average mark: 20% for a WAM of 60 to 74.9 and 25% for a WAM of 75 or above. The scholarship is open from 10 February 2026 to 31 December 2027 for full fee-paying, non-sponsored international students who are not humanitarian or permanent visa holders. Recipients must maintain full-time enrolment and satisfactory academic progress.

scholarships.name: SNU President Fellowship Program (SPF)
scholarships.deadline: Application Period: "During admission period for international students every semester". The scholarship application is submitted with the SNU online admission application, so the deadline is the SNU international graduate admission deadline for the semester applied for.
scholarships.description: The SNU President Fellowship Program is one of Seoul National University's most prestigious scholarship programmes, launched to provide opportunities for teaching and instructional staff members of universities in developing countries to pursue PhD degrees at SNU. Approximately 8 recipients are awarded each semester. Benefits include full tuition exemption for a maximum of 6 semesters, monthly living expenses of 1,500,000 to 2,000,000 KRW for 3 to 4 years, a round-trip economy airfare, Korean language training, and reimbursement of National Health Insurance fees. The application is made at the same time as the online application for admission to SNU, and the deadline falls during the international student admission period each semester.

scholarships.english_requirement: KAIST's official language of communication and instruction for international students is English. All applicants must provide at least one English proficiency test score, and the scores must be valid as of the online application deadline. Published minimums: TOEFL iBT 83 (taken before 21 Jan 2026) or 4.5 (taken on or after 21 Jan 2026); IELTS Academic 6.5 band; TOEIC 720 (Listening & Reading, TOEIC Public Testing Program); TEPS 326. TOEFL institutional code 0195, department code 99; Home Edition accepted; iBT MyBest Scores are NOT accepted; IELTS Online is accepted but IELTS One Skill Retake is NOT accepted; test scores from Institutional Testing Program (ITP) are NOT accepted. Exemption: no EPT score is required if you hold citizenship of, or have physically studied and completed a bachelor's-equivalent or higher qualification at an institution physically located in, Antigua and Barbuda, Australia, the Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Canada, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Ireland, Jamaica, Malta, New Zealand, St Kitts, St Lucia, St Vincent, Trinidad and Tobago, the U.K. or the U.S.A. A further exemption applies if you hold citizenship of one of a listed group of countries AND have physically studied and completed a qualification equivalent to a bachelor's degree or higher in English as the medium of instruction at an institution physically located in one of those countries, in which case a certificate from the school attended indicating English as the medium of instruction (e.g. English Lecture Certificate) must additionally be provided. Applicants expecting to graduate from regular KAIST degree programmes in the semester before the intended course also do not need to provide a score. Programs that do not require an EPT score: GDI-ITTP track, KINS-KAIST.

scholarships.description: The TU Graz High Potentials scholarship programme supports young talent from Austria and abroad with scholarships of up to EUR 8,800 for Bachelor's students and up to EUR 17,600 for Master's students over a period of up to two years. The programme is funded by partner companies, so individual scholarships carry their own sponsor requirements in addition to TU Graz's general criteria. TU Graz publishes separate application windows for the two degree levels: 15 October 2026 to 15 February 2027 for the Master's scholarships and 5 May 2027 to 7 July 2027 for the Bachelor's scholarships. Recipients also receive personal mentoring and access to a global alumni network, and TU Graz reports that it has supported around 200 students in total, with 13 scholarships awarded at the most recent ceremony in November 2025.
