scholarships.name: One World Scholarship (Afro-Asian Institute Salzburg)
scholarships.deadline: The Institute's apply page states: 'The call for applications for the October 2026 intake is closed. The next call is supposed to open in June 2027.' Its published multi-stage process closes the online form on 12 July and the full application on 15 July.
scholarships.description: The One World Scholarship of the Afro-Asian Institute Salzburg is a partial scholarship of EUR 500 per month during the semester (October through June) for students from Africa, Asia, the Near and Middle East, Oceania, the Caribbean and Latin America who study in Salzburg. Applicants must already be enrolled in Austria or admitted to a regular degree programme, hold a student residence permit or visa, and be admitted to a regular Master's or PhD programme in Salzburg. Selection is a multi-stage process - online form until 12 July, verification of formal criteria, full application until 15 July, online interview, then acceptance or rejection - and the Institute states that applying does not guarantee a scholarship place because positions are very limited. Successful applicants are expected to show financial need, good study progress, interest in development-related issues and a willingness to attend monthly meetings and actively contribute to the programme. Regarding equally qualified individuals, priority is given to female students.
scholarships.duration: Paid monthly during the semester, October through June

scholarships.title: Doctoral Scholarship from the University of Innsbruck
scholarships.name: Doctoral Scholarship from the University of Innsbruck
scholarships.deadline: The page carries the current call, labelled '3rd tranche 2026'. It states that 'Funding is expected to be awarded in December 2026 (i.e. earliest start of funding is December 2026 and latest start of funding is June 2027)', but the application deadline itself sits in a collapsible section ('When will the next call for tenders be issued?') that did not render readable text on 2026-10-04, so no deadline date can be stated.
scholarships.description: The University of Innsbruck awards a doctoral scholarship as start-up, interim, bridge or final financing for doctoral candidates, with a monthly allowance of EUR 1,120 for a maximum of 24 months. Funding is granted in six-month blocks confirmed by an interim progress report from the dissertation supervisor, and the 24-month period can be interrupted twice, each interruption not exceeding six months. Applicants must be enrolled as regular students and registered for continuation with a registered dissertation, and must evidence excellent academic success - an excellent grade point average plus normal duration of study - or scientific achievements; a maximum of two resubmissions is possible. The University states that at least 50 per cent of available funding is to be awarded to women in order to promote young female scientists, and that applicants of equal scientific quality are prioritised if they work in the University's main research areas or on project proposals. Payments are made exclusively by SEPA transfer.

scholarships.description: ESPRIT (Early-Stage Program: Research - Innovation - Training) is an Austrian Science Fund career programme that lets highly qualified postdoc-level researchers lead an independent research project at an Austrian research institution. The FWF states a funding period of 36 months, paying the principal investigator's salary at the current senior postdoc rate plus project-specific costs of EUR 45,000 as a flat rate, or up to EUR 75,000 with justification. Submissions are accepted on a rolling basis through the elane online application portal, and decisions are taken at five Scientific Board approval meetings per year.

scholarships.description: The FWF ASTRA Awards are a career funding programme launched in July 2024 for advanced postdocs in Austria who already have experience with independent research (R3 level). scholarships.description: The University of Vienna's SSH Call 2026 is a central recruitment call offering at least 40 fully funded four-year doctoral positions in the social sciences, humanities and cultural studies across nine participating doctoral schools, including the Vienna Doctoral School in Cognition, Behavior, and Neuroscience (CoBeNe). Positions are 30 hours per week under collective bargaining agreement §48 VwGr. B1, paid at a monthly gross salary of EUR 2,786.10 paid 14 times per year, and employees are exempt from tuition fees. Applications for the 2026 round ran from 7 January to 2 March 2026 at 14:00 CET through the University of Vienna PhD Selection Tool, with employment starting between 1 July and 1 October 2026. The University runs a central doctoral call annually, so the next cycle is expected but its dates were not yet published on the verification date.

scholarships.name: DAAD Research Grants in Germany (for doctoral candidates and early postdocs)
scholarships.deadline: "Application deadlines are updated annually in the second quarter. In most cases, they are in the same period as the previous year." scholarships.description: The DAAD Research Grants in Germany fund a research project at a state or state-recognised university or non-university research institute in Germany, carried out with a German scientific supervisor. Doctoral candidates may be funded for 2 to 12 months and early postdocs for 2 to 6 months; the grant cannot be extended and cannot be split within the funding period. The current DAAD announcement sets a monthly scholarship payment of EUR 1,400 plus insurance cover, a travel allowance, and for stays over six months a research allowance of EUR 460, a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly family allowance. Applications are submitted online through the DAAD Portal and are open annually, with deadlines updated in the second quarter of each year; on 2026-10-04 the DAAD stated that applications for the 2027 funding period were closed.

scholarships.description: The DAAD Helmut-Schmidt-Programme, also known as Public Policy and Good Governance, is funded by the German Federal Foreign Office and supports future leaders from developing and emerging countries who want to promote democracy and social justice in their home regions. It funds places on selected English-taught master's courses in public policy, good governance, international relations, public management, public administration, civil society, geo-governance, peace and conflict studies, and development and socio-economic policy at seven German higher education institutions. scholarships.description: Scholarship of the Heinrich Böll Foundation for international students who have completed their first degree abroad and intend to start a Master's degree in Germany, and for international PhD candidates who completed their graduate degree abroad. Applications are accepted in two rounds a year. Master's students funded by the Federal Foreign Office receive a base scholarship of EUR 992 per month plus a health insurance allowance of up to EUR 100 and optional components; PhD candidates funded by the Federal Foreign Office receive EUR 1,500 per month plus health insurance of up to EUR 200 per month. The funds come from the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) and the Federal Foreign Office (AA).

scholarships.title: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for Undergraduate Students (Embassy Recommendation)
scholarships.name: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for Undergraduate Students (Embassy Recommendation)
scholarships.deadline: No single central date: applicants must submit to the Japanese diplomatic mission in the country of their nationality by the deadline that mission sets, and that date is not published by MEXT. MEXT states applicants are informed of the final selection result by their diplomatic mission after February 2027, and that grantees must in principle arrive in Japan between 1 April 2027 and 7 April 2027.
scholarships.description: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for students from abroad who want to study as undergraduate students at Japanese national universities, selected through the recommendation of a Japanese embassy or consulate general. Applicants first pass a First Screening (documents, written academic examinations and interview) at the diplomatic mission in their country, are recommended to MEXT, and then pass MEXT's Second Screening. The scholarship pays a monthly allowance of JPY 117,000, waives entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees, and provides an economy-class airline ticket to Japan and, on return, back to the grantee's home country. The scholarship period is five years from April 2027 to March 2032 including one year of preparatory Japanese language education, or seven years for medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine and six-year pharmacy courses.
scholarships.duration: Five years from April 2027 to March 2032 including one year of preparatory Japanese language education; seven years for medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine or a six-year pharmacy course; four years for grantees placed directly at a university
scholarships.application_period: Annually; the 2027 cycle guidelines were published by MEXT in April 2026 and applications were made to Japanese diplomatic missions during the first half of the year
scholarships.official_source: MEXT (Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology)

scholarships.deadline: No applicant-facing deadline is published. Under the university-recommendation route the accepting university nominates the student to MEXT, so the application timetable is set between MEXT and each university and is not announced publicly.
scholarships.description: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for students from abroad who wish to pursue research study at a Japanese university under the university-recommendation route, meaning the accepting university nominates the student to MEXT. The monthly allowance depends on the course enrolled in: JPY 117,000 for regular students in bachelor degree courses, JPY 144,000 for master's or professional degree courses and JPY 145,000 for doctoral courses, with a supplemental regional allowance of JPY 2,000 or JPY 3,000 per month in specially designated regions. Entrance examination, matriculation and tuition fees must be paid by the accepting university, and MEXT stipulates the travel route and provides an economy-class airline ticket. The scholarship period is the necessary period for completion of the relevant regular course.

scholarships.application_period: Annual. MEXT publishes the guidelines for the coming year and calls universities for nominations; students apply through their prospective or current Japanese university rather than directly to MEXT

scholarships.title: Young Leaders Program (YLP) Students - Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship
scholarships.name: Young Leaders Program (YLP) Students - Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship
scholarships.deadline: No central MEXT or portal deadline is published. Recruitment is conducted through the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations, so the timetable is set country by country and by the recommending organisation. Applicants must check the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their own country.
scholarships.description: Young Leaders Program (YLP) Students is the seventh type of the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship. It funds a one-year master's course at a Japanese graduate school for university or college graduates with practical work experience and for young public administrators who are expected to play an active role in Asia and other countries. The scholarship pays JPY 242,000 per month, the tuition is exempted, and round-trip airfare to and from Japan is provided. Unlike the other six MEXT scholarship types, YLP is neither embassy-recommended nor university-recommended: recruitment is conducted by the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations, the initial selection is by document screening, interview and essay writing, and the final selection is made by the YLP Committee set in MEXT.
scholarships.duration: 1 year
scholarships.application_period: Not published centrally. Recruitment runs through the embassies of Japan in target countries upon the recommendation of official overseas recommending organisations, at timings that differ by country and region.

scholarships.description: JASSO's reservation programme for the Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students, for students who have already received pre-arrival admission to a Japanese institution and face financial difficulties. It pays a monthly stipend of JPY 48,000 for 12 months if the student enrols in April, or for 6 months if the student enrols in September or October. Applications are not made to JASSO directly; the applicant must apply through the school they plan to enrol in. There are three reservation categories: graduate level, EJU exam, and English courses.
scholarships.duration: 12 months for students enrolled in April (April of the year of enrolment to the following March); 6 months for students enrolled in September or October (October of the year of enrolment to the following March)
scholarships.application_period: School-by-school, twice a year, matching the Japanese enrolment cycles: spring enrolment (April) and autumn enrolment (September or October). JASSO publishes the eligible school and department lists for each cycle; for 2026 the autumn lists were published in June 2026 and the spring lists in January 2026.

Full CGS covers tuition, university accommodation or an accommodation subsidy, a stipend and comprehensive medical insurance, for one to three years of master's study or four to five years of doctoral study.

scholarships.name: Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship (GOI-IES)
scholarships.deadline: 2026 Application deadline: 5pm (Irish time) 12 March 2026. The 2026 call is closed.
scholarships.description: The Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship supports high-calibre international students who wish to study at NFQ levels 9 or 10 (master's, postgraduate diploma or PhD) in Ireland. The programme is funded by the Government of Ireland in partnership with Irish higher education institutions and managed by the Higher Education Authority, and 60 scholarships are awarded each year for one year of full-time study. scholarships.deadline: Opening date 1 May in year prior to study for offshore students, 1 July for onshore students. Closing dates 10 December for semester 1 (February) start, 30 April for semester 2 (July) start for offshore students, 15 August for onshore students.
scholarships.description: The Vice-Chancellor's Scholarships for International Students provide NZD $10,000 towards tuition fees to new international students entering full-time undergraduate study at the University of Otago. There is no separate scholarship application: applicants are automatically assessed during the admission process and agree in their eVision application for study to be considered for international scholarships. The award has a one-year tenure, is paid only as a credit towards tuition fees, cannot be deferred, and is forfeited if study does not commence by the enrolment date in the Offer of Place. Applicants must study on campus, and students sponsored by their home government or the New Zealand government are not eligible.
scholarships.duration: One year
scholarships.application_period: Applications open 1 May in the year prior to study for offshore students (1 July for onshore students) and close 10 December for a Semester 1 (February) start, or 30 April for a Semester 2 (July) start for offshore students.

scholarships.title: VUW Postgraduate International Scholarship
scholarships.name: VUW Postgraduate International Scholarship
scholarships.deadline: Closing date(s): Same as the programme application closing date. A scholarship application is not required; students are assessed for eligibility on application for their programme.
scholarships.description: The VUW Postgraduate International Scholarship is a partial fee-based scholarship of NZ$10,000 towards tuition fees for new international students entering a Master's degree programme of 120, 180 or 240 points, or a 120-point Postgraduate Diploma, at Te Herenga Waka — Victoria University of Wellington. No separate scholarship application is required: eligibility is assessed when the student applies for their programme, and the outcome is communicated in the Offer of Place. The scholarship applies for one year of study only, is credited directly against tuition fees upfront, and is awarded formally once the student enrols in first-year courses. It may be held alongside other scholarships where their regulations allow, and deferral is possible within the same calendar year but not to a later year.
scholarships.duration: One year of study only, for a student's first enrolment in the programme

scholarships.description: The VUW Undergraduate International Scholarship is a partial fee-based scholarship of NZ$15,000 towards tuition fees for one year of study, for new international students entering their first year of a Bachelor's degree programme at Te Herenga Waka — Victoria University of Wellington and studying full-time on campus. No separate scholarship application is required: eligibility is assessed when the student applies for their programme, and the outcome is communicated in the Offer of Place. The scholarship is credited directly against tuition fees upfront, is awarded formally once the student enrols in first-year courses, and covers one year of study only. Students completing Victoria's EAP or Foundation Studies programmes remain eligible, but returning students, Study Abroad or Exchange students, students with credit transfer, government sponsored students and holders of domestic status are not. Withdrawal after award can trigger repayment, and a change in fee or residency status from international to domestic can cause the scholarship to be withdrawn, suspended or repaid.

scholarships.description: Since the 2026 intake the University of Turku no longer offers a scholarship that covers the first year of tuition. Instead it offers an automatic EUR 2,000 Early Bird discount to newly admitted master's students who accept the offer and pay within 28 days of the admission decision, and the University of Turku Merit Scholarship, which covers 50% of the tuition fee for the following study year. The merit scholarship is based on studies completed at the University of Turku and requires 55 ECTS in the first study year, an average score of at least 3.0, and at least 4 ECTS of Finnish, with a separate application opened in spring.

scholarships.title: LUT Scholarship and Early Bird Discount (master's studies)
scholarships.name: LUT Scholarship and Early Bird Discount (master's studies)
scholarships.deadline: No scholarship application deadline exists: the awards are automatic. The early bird discount requires that you 'accept your study place and pay the remaining first-year tuition fee of EUR 10,000 within 21 days of your official admission email'. The LUT scholarship requires 60 ECTS recorded on your Transcript of Records by 31 July. LUT's own homepage states applications to English-language master's programmes are open until 31 March 2027 under rolling admission.
scholarships.description: LUT University reduces tuition for fee-paying students of its two-year master's programmes in two automatic steps. In the first academic year every tuition-liable student who accepts the study place and pays the remaining EUR 10,000 of the first-year fee within 21 days of the official admission email receives an early bird discount of EUR 5,000. In the second academic year every tuition-liable student who has completed at least 60 ECTS credits in accordance with their personal study plan, with those credits recorded on the Transcript of Records by 31 July, and who pays the second-year fee on time receives a LUT scholarship of EUR 5,000. Neither award requires a separate application and neither covers living costs.
scholarships.duration: The early bird discount applies to the first academic year and the LUT scholarship to the second academic year of a two-year master's programme

scholarships.title: Danish Government Scholarship for Non-EU/EEA Full-Degree Students
scholarships.name: Danish Government Scholarship for Non-EU/EEA Full-Degree Students
scholarships.deadline: The ministry publishes no deadline: 'The scholarships are administered by the Danish universities, who each select the students, who are awarded with a scholarship. For further information about the government scholarship, please consult the admission details of the higher education institution of your choice.' The deadline is therefore the admission deadline of the individual university.
scholarships.description: Danish universities receive a limited number of government scholarships each year to fund highly qualified full-degree students from countries outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland. Applicants must be citizens of a non-EU/EEA/non-Swiss country, enrolled in a full degree programme and hold a time-limited residence permit for education, and they are excluded if they seek admission to an artistic higher education institution, have a legal claim to Danish citizens' rights, or are eligible for SU. The scholarship consists of two parts and may be a full or partial tuition fee waiver, a grant towards living costs, or both. The individual university administers the award and selects the students.

scholarships.deadline: Positions are advertised individually and applications are assessed continuously: 'Acceptance to a PhD-programme at NTNU is done continuously throughout the academic year and is not restricted to the beginning of term.' Each vacancy carries its own application deadline.
scholarships.description: NTNU's PhD positions are salaried employment rather than scholarships: Norwegian PhD candidates are not treated as students and are normally employees of the institution that funds them. Most PhD candidates at NTNU are employed as PhD research fellows (stipendiat) at NTNU or a university college, with individual positions advertised on NTNU's vacancy pages and on jobbnorge.no. Admission requires at least five years of higher education including a master's degree, a weighted average of at least B over the last two master's years on NTNU's scale, and a funding plan for the whole PhD period. Acceptance is done continuously throughout the academic year rather than at fixed deadlines, and the standard PhD is three years full-time, sometimes extended by a fourth year of teaching duties.

scholarships.description: The Stipendium Hungaricum is a Hungarian Government scholarship programme, implemented by Tempus Public Foundation, to promote the internationalisation of Hungarian higher education and to attract international students. Applicants must be nominated by the responsible Sending Partner in their own country or region and apply through the Tempus Public Foundation online system, which lists 30 Hungarian universities and colleges and more than 900 study programmes, with a maximum of two programme choices. Holders have their tuition fees covered and receive a monthly stipend plus an accommodation contribution, and must reside in Hungary during the study period. The programme runs a single annual application round, and for 2026/2027 the deadline was 15 January 2026, 2 p.m. CET.

scholarships.title: Jagiellonian University Rector's Scholarship (stypendium rektora)
scholarships.name: Jagiellonian University Rector's Scholarship (stypendium rektora)
scholarships.deadline: Official wording: "The deadline for submitting the application for the Rector's scholarship is October 20 of the academic year for which the scholarship is to be awarded." The last published schedule (2025/2026) showed applications open from 1 to 20 October.
scholarships.description: Jagiellonian University's Rector's Scholarship is a merit-based cash benefit from the university Scholarship Fund for first-cycle (bachelor), second-cycle (master) and long-cycle master's students, awarded on request for outstanding academic performance, scientific, artistic or sports achievements. In the first year of first-cycle or long-cycle master's studies it goes to students admitted in the year of the matura exam who won an international olympiad or were laureates/finalists of a central-level olympiad, or who medalled in at least a Polish Championship competition; in higher years it is capped at 10% of students in a given programme. Foreign students admitted from the 2019/2020 academic year onward may apply regardless of citizenship. The award runs for nine months (October to June), paid monthly into a Polish zloty (PLN) bank account held at a bank in Poland.
scholarships.application_period: Annual. Published 2025/2026 schedule: rector's scholarship applications from 1 October to 20 October, submitted electronically in USOSweb.

scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are assessed with a points-based system awarding points for grade average plus academic, artistic and sports achievements; the scholarship goes to students with the highest number of points and is capped at 10% of students per programme/specialisation. scholarships.description: The International Visegrad Fund runs regional mobility programmes for Czechia, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Ukraine. The Visegrad Fellowship Program funds individual short-term in-person stays of 2 to 10 weeks for full-time doctoral students and PhD holders to conduct a research project, give lectures or seminars, or study archival material at an institution in a V4 country other than their country of citizenship and residence; it pays a lump-sum scholarship of EUR 500 per week in two instalments (80% and 20%). The separate Visegrad Scholarship Program supports Master's and post-Master's students and researchers for up to two semesters at institutions in Central and Eastern Europe and its next cycle opens on 1 January 2027. Other Fund programmes include the Visegrad-Taiwan Scholarships for doctoral and post-doctoral researchers, the Western Balkans-Visegrad Fellowships, research grants at the Historical Archives of the EU, and a scholarship at the Open Society Archives in Budapest.

scholarships.description: The Foundation for Science and Technology runs an annual call for PhD studentships under its Regulation for Studentships and Fellowships (RBI) and Research Fellowship Holder Statute (EBI). The regular line of application covers all scientific areas and funds research carried out in scientific and academic institutions, including public and private higher education institutions, R&D units, Associated Laboratories and other private non-profit R&D bodies, at home or abroad. scholarships.description: Nova SBE funds its master's students through an institutional portfolio of tuition-fee scholarships and awards. The Nova SBE Merit Scholarship is open to all candidates regardless of country of origin and covers 20% or 50% of the master's tuition fee value. Alongside it sit the Nova SBE Social Mobility Scholarship (20%, 50% or 100% of tuition, for candidates with proven financial need), the Nova SBE Continuity Scholarship (50% or 100%, for Nova SBE bachelor's graduates within a widened income threshold), and a series of partner-funded awards including Accenture (100%), Antonio Serrenho (100%), Banco Primus (100%), Deloitte (100%), Andre Sousa Bessa (100%), Women in Finance (20% or 50%), plus CEMS-specific awards. Scholarships are awarded on a rolling basis, so the available budget can be exhausted before the end of the master's admission cycle, and combined Nova SBE funding is normally capped at 70% of total tuition.

scholarships.title: Ontario Graduate Scholarship (OGS) - University of Toronto
scholarships.name: Ontario Graduate Scholarship (OGS) - University of Toronto
scholarships.deadline: Student Deadline: date set by graduate unit. Application Dates: determined by graduate unit. Graduate Unit Deadline: refer to SGS Memo. Results: mid-July.
scholarships.description: The Ontario Graduate Scholarship program encourages excellence in graduate studies at publicly-assisted universities in Ontario and has provided merit-based scholarships to Ontario's best graduate students in all disciplines since 1975. At the University of Toronto the program is jointly funded by the Province of Ontario and the University of Toronto, and the Province allocates OGS awards to universities specifying how many each may offer annually. The OGS is worth $5,000 per session at U of T, and the awarding graduate unit contributes one-third of the total award cost. Deadlines and application dates are set by each graduate unit, with results in mid-July.
scholarships.duration: Each scholarship is tenable for one year, i.e. two consecutive or three academic sessions.
scholarships.application_period: University-specific internal deadlines; provincial competition annually
scholarships.official_source: School of Graduate Studies, University of Toronto / Ontario Ministry of Colleges, Universities, Research Excellence and Security

scholarships.description: The Alberta Graduate Excellence Scholarship recognizes outstanding academic achievement of students pursuing graduate studies in Alberta. It was established to incent the best and the brightest students, including international students, to study in Alberta, and is funded through the Alberta Heritage Scholarship Fund. The award is between $11,000 and $15,000. Applicants must be enrolled full-time in a master's, doctoral or ladderable graduate programme at an eligible Alberta post-secondary institution while living in Alberta, and eligible statuses include Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents, Protected Persons, international students and Indigenous students. Alberta Student Aid publishes no application deadline; selection is carried out by schools.

scholarships.title: Merit Scholarship Program for Foreign Students (PBEEE) - Fonds de recherche du Quebec
scholarships.name: Merit Scholarship Program for Foreign Students (PBEEE) - Fonds de recherche du Quebec
scholarships.deadline: Deadline (application): December 2nd, 2025 at 16:00 (EST) for the 2026-2027 competition. University and CCTT Network preselection of applications to FRQ: October 23, 2025, 4 p.m. Candidates preselected by the China Scholarship Council: before March 31, 2026. The 2026-2027 rules are marked out of competition and no next-cycle date was published as at 2026-10-04.
scholarships.description: In support of the Quebec government's science policy, the Merit Scholarship for Foreign Students (PBEEE) supports the internationalization of research activities in Quebec higher education institutions, attracts top foreign researchers and students, and creates cultural links for joint research projects. It is managed by the Fonds de recherche du Quebec - secteur Nature et technologies, which was commissioned by the Ministere de l'Enseignement superieur du Quebec, which provides the funding. The programme has four component types - master's research, doctoral research, postdoctoral and short-term research or professional development - available both to students of all countries and, through five bilateral components, to students from Brazil, China, India, Israel and Wallonia. Recipients must be preselected by a Quebec university or the CCTT network, and scholarship payments begin only after FRQ receives a copy of the study permit (doctoral) or work permit (postdoctoral).
scholarships.duration: Master's: maximum 6 instalments (6 semesters). Doctoral: maximum 12 sessions (12 instalments), with $25,000 for the first 9 sessions and $12,000 for the last 3 if an extension is requested. Postdoctoral: maximum 12 months, not renewable. Short-term research or professional development: 4 months, not renewable.

scholarships.description: The Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development - Phase 2 (SEED-2) program is offered by Global Affairs Canada as a key initiative under Canada's Indo-Pacific Strategy, funded under that strategy. It expands the Canada-ASEAN Scholarships and Educational Exchanges for Development (SEED) programme to students from ASEAN Member States, Pacific Island Countries and Mongolia, who conduct short-term study or research at Canadian post-secondary institutions in areas contributing to the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Canadian institutions must apply on behalf of eligible candidates, must be Designated Learning Institutions, and must waive tuition fees for recipients. Four award components are offered, from $10,200 to $15,900, with durations of four to eight months.

scholarships.description: The Embassy of the People's Republic of China in the Commonwealth of The Bahamas opened the 2026/2027 Chinese Government Scholarship, comprising one bilateral place and three unilateral places for undergraduate, master's, doctoral, advanced general studies and advanced higher studies programmes in China. scholarships.deadline: Applications are submitted twice a year, by 31 March and 31 October of the calendar year. The next still-applicable round closes on 31 October 2026.
scholarships.description: The Václav Havel Bursary is Charles University's own financial support for international students whose studies are hindered or prevented by repression under totalitarian, authoritarian or other non-democratic regimes anywhere in the world. Students from countries where humanitarian organisations report violated human rights and freedoms and where discriminatory measures restrict access to education may apply, provided they have already been admitted and enrolled in a degree programme at a Charles University faculty through the standard admissions procedure. Students submit the application to the Student Affairs Office of their faculty, which forwards it digitally through the Dean to the Chair of the Václav Havel Bursary Board. As part of the preparation for studies in the Czech language, applicants may also request a contribution towards living expenses.

scholarships.description: The Visegrad Scholarship Program supports full-time Master's and post-Master's students and researchers in all disciplines and in any language for one to two semesters at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe. It is funded by the International Visegrad Fund, founded by the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia. The award is EUR 3,500 per semester for the scholar plus EUR 2,000 per semester for the host institution, and it does not cover tuition. Applicants must already hold a bachelor's or master's degree, and their country of citizenship or residence must differ from the host institution's country.

scholarships.title: CTU Scholarship for Foreign Students - Czech Technical University in Prague
scholarships.name: CTU Scholarship for Foreign Students - Czech Technical University in Prague
scholarships.deadline: No application deadline is published on the CTU Scholarships page. Applications are submitted to the Department of International Relations at the rectorate of CTU via the faculty International Office, with no published closing date or intake calendar.
scholarships.description: CTU awards a scholarship to foreign students who wish to take a Master study programme at the Czech Technical University in Prague and display qualities that entitle them to the award, and to foreign doctoral students capable of doing scientific work who study on a doctoral programme in English at CTU in Prague. The Master's award is a contribution towards the costs of a stay in the Czech Republic of up to CZK 10,000 per month for one to two semesters; the doctoral award covers the basic doctoral-study scholarship plus living costs of up to CZK 16,000 per month for six to twelve months. Both are financed equally from the rectorate's scholarship fund and the relevant faculty's fund, and are awarded under Act No. 111/1998 Sb. on Universities, section 91(3)(b). The award is a living-cost contribution and does not cover tuition fees.
scholarships.duration: 1-2 semesters initially, extendable to full Master's programme duration
scholarships.application_period: No intake calendar or deadline is published. The page describes a standing procedure: obtain the faculty's agreement, then apply through the faculty International Office to the Department of International Relations at the rectorate.

scholarships.description: Aalborg University grants a small number (approximately 15 per year) of tuition-fee-waiver-plus-stipend scholarships to individually selected applicants from non-EU/EEA countries applying to fee-paying master's programmes for the September intake. scholarships.title: RESDOC Doctoral Researcher Positions - Resilient and Just Systems Doctoral Project (MSCA COFUND)
scholarships.name: RESDOC Doctoral Researcher Positions - Resilient and Just Systems Doctoral Project (MSCA COFUND)
scholarships.deadline: Applications for the 2026 RESDOC call had to be submitted "by 31 August 2026 at latest 11:59 PM (Finnish time EET)". The call is now closed and no date for the next RESDOC call has been published.
scholarships.description: RESDOC (Resilient and Just Systems Doctoral Project) is an international doctoral training project at the University of Helsinki, co-funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions COFUND scheme under Horizon Europe and the University itself. It recruits 30 doctoral researchers for four-year, 100% employment contracts running 2027-2030, at a gross salary of approximately EUR 2,900 per month including a mobility allowance, plus an annual travel allowance for conferences and secondments. Research must fit one of four interdisciplinary themes: Infectious Diseases and Antimicrobial Resistance in Changing Environment; Biodiversity and Nature's Resilience; Secure and Sustainable Food and Water Systems; and Just Socio-Ecological Transition. The 2026 call closed on 31 August 2026 with 2,159 applications, and evaluation by external evaluators was under way in September 2026.

scholarships.deadline: No fixed application deadline is published; nominations are submitted year-round through the ANRF online portal and selections are made periodically by an empowered Selection Committee.
scholarships.description: The Ramanujan Fellowship, operated by the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, is a reverse brain drain scheme that brings brilliant Indian and Indian-origin scientists and engineers from abroad to take up scientific research positions in India. It is scientist-specific and highly selective, restricted to candidates below 40 years of age who hold a higher degree such as a PhD in science or engineering, a master's in engineering or technology, or an MD, with adequate professional experience and a proven track record evidenced by publications and recognition. Fellows must not already hold any permanent, tenure-track or contractual position in an Indian institution or university, and must be working abroad at the time of nomination. The fellowship pays Rs 1,35,000 per month consolidated including HRA, plus a research grant of Rs 7.00 lakh per annum and Rs 60,000 per annum in overhead charges to the host institute.

Scholarships run for a maximum of two years on master's courses and three years on bachelor's or single-cycle courses, paid in two instalments and conditional on earning at least 20 CFU by 30 November each year. Eligibility follows automatically from the degree course application.

(Taiwan and Palestine are treated in this manner.) Persons of Japanese nationality are eligible to apply if they have resided at the time of application in a foreign country for 10 years or longer and are judged at a host research institution to have played an active role in that country's scientific community. scholarships.selection_notes: Selection of the applicant (host researcher) and the candidate (invited overseas researcher) is done by the JSPS International Program Committee, made up of Japan's frontline researchers. Selection is carried out through a document review in the first stage and a panel review in the second. Reviewers with a potential conflict of interest are removed, and all Review Committee Members must comply with confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements. Document reviews are conducted by three examiners per application, using a graduated 1-5 scale (5 superlative, 4 excellent, 3 good, 2 fair, 1 poor), taking into account research achievements, the research plan, estimated research capacity and future potential; the averaged document-review score is the primary screening criterion for panel review. Two selection judgements are made: Selected and Not-selected.

scholarships.best_fit: Established overseas researchers holding a position equivalent to a Japanese professor, associate professor or assistant professor (or researchers more than six years past a doctorate who have continuously conducted research), who already have an agreed collaboration plan with a Japanese host researcher and can spend 14 to 60 days in Japan.
scholarships.notes: The pages read publish no deferral, renewal, return-home or clinical-restriction term, so those fields are left null. Published exclusions: for a candidate who has been living in Japan (and has a mailing address) before the fellowship starting date, the outbound 'airfare' and a 'settling-in allowance' will not be paid. JSPS states the number of selectees with Japanese nationality must be no more than about 3% of all selectees under one recruitment for an application deadline. Selection policy also states that, as much as possible, unbalance should be avoided in the selectees' nationalities, host institutions and areas of specialization. The host institution, not the fellow, applies for the research support allowance.

scholarships.description: The NL Scholarship is the Dutch national scholarship programme for bachelor and master students from outside the European Economic Area. It is financed by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science together with Dutch research universities and universities of applied sciences. Study in NL states the scholarship amounts to € 5,000 and is paid in the first year of studies, and explicitly notes that it is not a full-tuition scholarship. Institutions set their own application deadlines and their own amount tiers, so the value and the deadline both depend on the institution you apply to.

scholarships.description: The KITLV Visiting Fellowship is a three month funded research stay at the Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies (KITLV) in Leiden for researchers who hold a PhD in the social sciences and/or humanities and are not tax residents of the Netherlands. Fellows work on a publication or research project of their own choice in Southeast Asian or Caribbean Studies and do not need a university or research institute affiliation. The offer covers a return economy air or train fare, reimbursement of accommodation costs in Leiden up to EUR 2,000 per month against proof of payment, and a case-by-case monthly compensation for higher living costs. It is explicitly not a salaried position and fellows are expected to have a steady income during the stay.

scholarships.description: The Tilburg University Waiver halves the institutional tuition fee for up to 21 non-EEA international applicants each year, as part of the university's Diversity, Equity and Inclusion commitment. It applies to all regular one-year Master's programmes starting in September 2027, with the two-year Master in Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence as an explicit exception; Research Master's and Pre-Master's students are not eligible. Applicants must have completed their most recent degree in a designated country and must not already hold any other tuition-fee waiver. If more eligible applicants apply than there are waivers, recipients are chosen by random lottery, and outcomes are notified by 1 June 2027.

Awards can be made for either vocational or academic study and can run for one, two or three years. scholarships.description: The New Zealand Space Scholarship gives postgraduate STEM students a fully supported three-month internship at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, working alongside scientists and engineers on space missions and research. The scholarship covers return economy flights to the United States, accommodation, a daily living allowance and reasonable travel-related expenses including insurance support where applicable. Applicants must be New Zealand citizens aged 18 or over, enrolled in a postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution in a field relevant to NASA's mission priorities, and hold at least a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale.

scholarships.description: The University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship is the University's main doctoral award, funding PhD and professional doctorate (DClinDent, DMA, DBA, EDd) candidates at the University of Otago in Dunedin, New Zealand. It pays a NZ$34,128 per annum stipend plus a tuition fee waiver for 36 months at the domestic rate, and excludes student services fee and insurance. Up to 153 awards are offered annually to both domestic and international applicants who are seeking their first doctoral qualification. Applications can be submitted at any time and are considered at quarterly rounds in March, June, September and November.

scholarships.description: The Ulam NAWA Programme is an institutional programme of the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange that lets Polish higher education and research institutions employ outstanding scientists from abroad for 6 to 24 months, with projects starting between 1 February and 1 December 2027. The funding covers remuneration of the invited Principal Investigator up to PLN 17,000 per month including employer costs and an allowance of up to PLN 1,200 per month for the Inviting Person, with a maximum of PLN 436,800 per project. Invited scientists conduct research, postdoctoral training, publication work and grant preparation, with teaching as a complementary activity, and the programme is open to all disciplines. Applications are submitted by the Polish host institution in English through NAWA's ICT system; the 2026 call closed on 15 May 2026 at 3:00 p.m. CET with results due by 30 November 2026.

scholarships.description: TOP200 NAWA is an initiative of the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange that attracts outstanding research talent from universities ranked in the global top 200 to Polish universities and research institutes, offering stable full-time employment for two to four years so that the researcher can build their own research team. It runs two tracks, Junior Fellow for early-stage researchers whose doctorate is no more than seven years old and Senior Fellow for researchers experienced in leading research teams, is open to all scientific fields, and is funded from a call budget of PLN 17 million. The pilot call closed on 27 February 2026 with results due by 31 July 2026 and projects running from 2026 to 2032.

scholarships.description: The Bekker NAWA Programme supports the international mobility of PhD students, scientists and academic teachers from Polish scientific and academic units by funding research fellowships of 3 to 24 months at recognised research centres abroad. It covers the scholarship holder's living expenses during the stay together with a mobility allowance, and the amount may be increased for a spouse, underage children, or an assistant with a severe or moderate disability. The programme is open to all scientific and artistic disciplines with no restriction on host countries, and can serve as a postdoctoral fellowship for young scientists or as part of doctoral education for PhD students. The 2026 call closed on 29 May 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Polish time, for projects starting between 1 March and 1 October 2027, with applications in English through NAWA's ICT system.

scholarships.description: The Walczak NAWA Programme funds international mobility for researchers in medical, pharmaceutical and health sciences connected with Polish institutions, letting them carry out research and work alongside leading specialists in the best medical centres worldwide. Participants choose a teaching, research or clinical track for a stay of one to six months. Eligible applicants are PhD students and doctoral-school participants, doctors with at least a doctorate working in hospitals and other medical institutions, and academic teachers in the medical, pharmaceutical and health sciences. The support, described by NAWA as covering a stipend, living and accommodation costs and travel expenses, amounts to up to PLN 32,000 for each month of stay, with a one-off PLN 20,000 for doctoral students and researchers on the scientific path whose stay exceeds three months. NAWA's call page still shows the December 2024 edition as the most recent announcement.

scholarships.deadline: No application deadline is published for the 2027/28 edition as of 2026-10-04. The programme runs on an annual cycle: kirkland.edu.pl reports 'Uroczyste zakończenie XXVI edycji Programu Kirklanda' (graduation of the 26th edition) and 'Inauguracja roku stypendialnego 2026/27' in September/October 2026, and the recruitment calendar is published on the Polish candidates page.
scholarships.description: The Lane Kirkland Scholarship Program is a nine-month non-degree professional development scholarship for graduates from Ukraine, Belarus, Russia, Moldova, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan who already have at least two years of professional experience. Grantees attend two semesters of classes at one of about fifteen affiliated Polish universities, take part in an introductory course, trainings and grantees' conventions, and complete at least two weeks of professional internship. The programme provides support valued at PLN 6,000 per month, free access to university classes, accommodation, health insurance and a return ticket to Poland. It was founded by the Polish-American Freedom Foundation and is financially supported by the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange (NAWA).

scholarships.description: Poland My First Choice NAWA is a Polish government scholarship that funds the statutory period of full-time second-cycle (master's) studies at academic higher education institutions supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education. Beneficiaries receive the NAWA Director's scholarship of PLN 1,800 per month, an exemption from tuition fees at public universities and a one-time travel lump sum. Applicants choose the university and field of study themselves and must apply for university admission independently of the NAWA application. The 2026 call (no 19/2026 of 30 April 2026) is closed and its results were published in August 2026.

scholarships.description: Erasmus+ is the European Union programme supporting projects, partnerships, events and mobility in education, training, youth and sport. Its higher education strand is mainly a student exchange programme that also covers placements in companies abroad and academic staff mobility. Students can spend part of their studies in another country without additional tuition, registration or examination costs and receive a scholarship covering living costs, with the period and courses recognised by their home institution. In Poland the programme is implemented by the Foundation for the Development of the Education System, appointed as the Polish National Agency.

scholarships.description: The Temasek Undergraduate Overseas Scholarship is awarded to exceptional polytechnic graduates who show academic excellence, outstanding extracurricular involvement and a strong passion for STEM, to study a STEM undergraduate degree at an overseas university, with Medicine and Dentistry excluded. Eligibility is capped by a Gross Monthly Household Income of S$15,000 or less at the point of admission, and graduates must serve a 4-year bond in a STEM-related role in Singapore or with a Singapore-headquartered company.

scholarships.title: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window #1 (Developing Country Nationals)
scholarships.name: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window #1 (Developing Country Nationals)
scholarships.deadline: Application Window #1 from January 18 to February 26, 2027. The programme also runs Application Window #2 from March 29 to May 21, 2027. The link to the JJ/WBGSP application form is only communicated to candidates admitted unconditionally (except for funding) to a participating master's programme and shortlisted as eligible by that university.
scholarships.description: The JJ/WBGSP is a fully funded master's scholarship for mid-career professionals from listed World Bank developing countries who are already admitted to one of a fixed set of participating development-related master's programmes. For the 2027 cycle the World Bank states that a scholarship provides tuition, a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus, economy class round-trip airfare, basic medical insurance obtained through the university, and a US$600 travel allowance for each trip. The amount of the monthly subsistence allowance varies depending on the host country and is not published on the programme page. The Government of Japan solely funds the scholarship on an annual basis, and scholars commit to return to their home country after earning their degree.
scholarships.duration: The duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
scholarships.application_period: Two application rounds per cycle, organised to match the academic calendars of the participating programmes. For the 2027 cycle: Application Window #1 January 18 - February 26, 2027; Application Window #2 March 29 - May 21, 2027. Each participating university sets its own admission deadlines, which fall before the JJ/WBGSP window closes.
scholarships.official_source: World Bank, Development Economics Vice Presidency (programme funded by the Government of Japan)

scholarships.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it from 1 to 10 on four factors: quality of professional experience (30% weight), quality of professional recommendations (30% weight), quality of commitment to the applicant's home country (30% weight), and quality of education background (10% weight). The Secretariat uses the average of the two assessors plus a reasonably wide geographical distribution of awards, a reasonable distribution across gender, unusual circumstances or hardships, and giving scholarships to applicants who otherwise have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists go to the JJ/WBGSP Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.

scholarships.notes: Not eligible if admitted to a non-participating programme: the World Bank states explicitly that if you are not admitted to one of the participating master's programs you are not eligible to apply for a JJ/WBGSP scholarship in 2027. The scholarship does NOT cover visa application costs, expenses to bring and/or support family members, extra-curricular courses or training, courses below the minimum credits required for the degree, language training not provided by the graduate program, additional travel during the study program, research or supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars or internships, educational equipment such as computers, and the resident permit fee. The scholarship may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support; if you hold another award you must send those documents to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat. Scholars commit to return to their home country after earning their degree. Declining an earlier offer, or receiving the scholarship and failing to graduate, permanently bars reapplication. The 2026 window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026, so only the 2027 developing-country-national cycle is live.

scholarships.description: The Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship Program is a program of the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs that provides up to $5,000 in merit-based scholarships to outstanding American undergraduate students with high financial need to pursue credit-bearing academic studies and career-oriented internships abroad. It is congressionally funded, established by the U.S. Congress in 2001, and administered by the Institute of International Education since its inception. Applicants must be receiving a Federal Pell Grant during the time of application or be able to prove they will receive one during their term abroad. The programme has funded American students to study and intern abroad in more than 170 countries, with recipients from all 50 U.S. states and D.C.

scholarships.description: The Boren Awards fund intensive overseas language study for U.S. undergraduate students (Boren Scholarships) and research or language study for U.S. graduate students (Boren Fellowships). scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated by IIE-organized regional merit review panels made up of faculty members and administrators from colleges and universities across the United States, representing a wide array of fields of study. The panels make recommendations on each submitted, eligible application, with final decision-making authority held by the program's federal sponsor, DLNSEO. scholarships.notes: Non-deferrable in practice: recipients must remain matriculated at their U.S. institution for the whole funded period and may not graduate until the award is complete, and overseas programmes must be approved by a Boren Program Advisor before travel. No return-home obligation is published; instead recipients must complete at least one year of federal service in support of U.S. national security after graduation, with preference given to a longer-term commitment. Internships conducted during a Boren-funded period may not be remunerated nor conducted with the U.S. or a foreign government, and Boren Fellows may not work as journalists while abroad, even freelance or unpaid. Funding for programme expenses incurred after May 31, 2028 is contingent upon availability and cannot be guaranteed at the time of award.

scholarships.deadline: Reference letters due October 16, 2026 by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time. Application deadlines: October 19, 2026 (Life Sciences); October 20, 2026 (Computer and Information Science and Engineering; Materials Research; Psychology; Social Sciences); October 22, 2026 (Engineering); October 23, 2026 (Chemistry; Geosciences; Mathematical Sciences; Physics and Astronomy). All applications must be received by 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the deadline date for the Major Field of Study selected. November 15, 2026 is the last day to withdraw an application without it counting towards the number of times an individual may apply.
scholarships.description: The NSF GRFP funds full-time graduate students pursuing research-based master's or doctoral degrees in NSF-supported STEM fields at accredited, nonprofit U.S. institutions. Each fellowship provides three years of financial support over a five-year fellowship period: a $37,000 annual stipend paid to the fellow and a $16,000 annual cost-of-education allowance paid to the institution in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees, so there is no tuition or mandatory-fee cost to the student. There is no post-graduate study service requirement, and fellows may transfer to a different institution after completion of the first fellowship year. Estimated 1,500 awards for the 2027 solicitation (NSF 26-526), pending availability of funds.
scholarships.duration: Five-year fellowship period with three years of financial support
scholarships.application_period: The GRFP Application Module usually opens in July or August; applications for the 2027 competition close between October 19 and October 23, 2026 depending on Major Field of Study, with reference letters due October 16, 2026. scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are reviewed by disciplinary and interdisciplinary scientists, engineers and STEM experts selected by NSF Program Officers, with care taken to ensure no conflicts of interest. Applications are reviewed in broad areas of related disciplines based on the Major Field of Study selected by the applicant, using the two NSF Merit Review Criteria: Intellectual Merit (potential to advance knowledge) and Broader Impacts (potential to benefit society and contribute to specific, desired societal outcomes). Intellectual Merit factors include the ability to plan and conduct research, work independently, work as part of a team, interpret and communicate research, take initiative, think creatively, solve problems, persist and overcome challenges, and demonstrated intellectual ability as indicated by grades, coursework and awards. Broader Impacts factors include increasing participation in STEM, improving STEM education through outreach and mentoring, increasing public scientific literacy, increasing collaboration among academia and industry, improving educator development, improving societal well-being, developing a globally competitive STEM workforce, improving national security, increasing U.S. economic competitiveness, and enhancing research and education infrastructure. GRFP was established to recruit and support individuals who demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions in STEM.
scholarships.program_type: Government fellowship
scholarships.best_fit: Final-year undergraduates, bachelor's degree holders with no prior graduate degree enrollment, joint bachelor's-master's students in their final undergraduate or first graduate year, and first-year graduate students in their first research-based graduate degree program, who are U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals or permanent residents.
scholarships.notes: No post-graduate study service requirement. Fellowship funds are awarded to the institution of higher education at which the fellow is enrolled, and the institution is responsible for disbursing the stipend to the fellow; the fellowship is therefore only usable at an eligible accredited nonprofit U.S. institution. The fellowship period is five years with three years of financial support, so fellows must plan for two unfunded years. Fellows may transfer to another institution after completing the first fellowship year. Practice-oriented professional degree programs (medical, dental, law, public health, MBA, MPH, MSW, JD, MD, DVM, DDS) are excluded at any time during the fellowship, as are joint science-professional degree programs. Applicants may submit only one application per annual competition, and only in the first year of their first graduate degree program (joint bachelor's-master's students are limited to one application). No clinical or medical-school pathway is eligible.

scholarships.title: SA-TIED Request for Research Proposals: Public revenue mobilization; Poverty, inequality, and labour markets
scholarships.name: SA-TIED Request for Research Proposals: Public revenue mobilization; Poverty, inequality, and labour markets
scholarships.deadline: Closing date: 15 October 2026, 23:59 (UTC+2). Submit questions by 8 October 2026.
scholarships.description: UNU-WIDER and the South African National Treasury invite proposals under the third phase of the Southern Africa - Towards Inclusive Economic Development (SA-TIED) programme for research using South African tax administrative data. Accepted proposals are paid a research honorarium in the range of US$3,000-10,000 on delivery of a working paper of 10,000 words or fewer, and the resulting papers are published in the SA-TIED research paper series. This is research funding rather than a degree scholarship: the deliverable is a policy paper, and the honorarium is expected to cover all expenses of the research.
scholarships.duration: Milestone-driven: first draft of papers due 8 June 2027 and final draft due 8 September 2027, with a work-in-progress workshop in June or July 2027
scholarships.application_period: Launched 17 September 2026; proposals close 15 October 2026 at 23:59 UTC+2. Questions on the proposal process were due by 8 October 2026, with queries and responses published on the RfRP announcement page and updated on a rolling basis.

scholarships.selection_notes: Each proposal is reviewed for scientific merit and feasibility and selected on three criteria: relevance to the research project, strength of empirical and policy contributions, and qualifications and experience of the research team. Preference is given to applications from early-career and female scholars and researchers from South Africa. Only the final decision on whether the proposal is accepted is communicated; applicants must not expect feedback on their proposals. Funding decisions are targeted for 9 November 2026.

scholarships.title: Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship (AEF) Program
scholarships.name: Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship (AEF) Program
scholarships.degree: Not a degree programme - professional fellowship for K-12 STEM educators
scholarships.degree_levels: Not a degree programme - professional fellowship for K-12 STEM educators
scholarships.deadline: Application deadline 8:00pm Eastern, November 5, 2026. Online application opened August 3, 2026. The application period typically opens in mid-August, with applications due in mid-November.
scholarships.description: The AEF Programme places accomplished K-12 STEM educators for eleven months in federal agencies or U.S. Congressional offices, working on national education programmes and policy. Each fellow receives a monthly living stipend of $8,200, a travel allowance of up to $5,000 for approved travel requested by the host agency, an education allowance of up to $1,000 for approved professional development expenses, relocation reimbursement of up to $3,500 for fellows relocating from outside the Washington, DC area, and a health insurance stipend of up to $550 per month on an individual plan or $1,300 per month on a family plan. The DOE sponsors up to five congressional office placements. The programme is a single eleven-month appointment; it is not a degree award and involves no tuition.

scholarships.application_period: Online application opens August 3, 2026 and closes 8:00pm Eastern on November 5, 2026 for the 2027-2028 programme. Semi-finalist notifications with travel arrangements are made by February 24, 2027; interviews in Washington, DC February 27 - March 1, 2027; finalist notifications March 9, 2027; congressional fellows placement interviews mid-June 2027; fellows arrive in Washington, DC mid-August 2027.

scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review conducted by the AEF Programme to verify applicant eligibility and ensure all required materials have been provided; only applications meeting all requirements are advanced for merit-based evaluation. Merit review is a thorough, consistent and objective examination by evaluators who must be independent of the applicants and of the sponsoring agencies, applying pre-established criteria in four areas: the applicant's teaching experience, professional accomplishments, demonstrated leadership qualities, and interests as they relate to participating in the AEF Programme. Sponsoring federal agencies then review the highly reviewed applications on overall professional experience and demonstrated leadership qualities, the applicant's interest in and preparedness for the fellowship, alignment of the applicant's experience and subject matter expertise with the interests of the host office, and quality of recommendations, and select the top candidates as semi-finalists to interview in Washington, DC. Semi-finalists are invited to Washington, DC for three days of individual interviews and information sessions. Following interviews, final selections are made at the discretion of the sponsoring federal agencies; finalists are contacted by ORISE regarding offers. DOE selects the finalists for Congressional office placements. Recruitment and selection is done without regard to race, gender, age, colour, religion, national origin, mental or physical disability, or status as a veteran.
scholarships.program_type: Government fellowship
scholarships.best_fit: Experienced, currently employed U.S. K-12 STEM teachers or district officials who have at least five complete years of full-time classroom STEM teaching, can secure an eleven-month leave of absence, and can relocate to the Washington, DC area.
scholarships.notes: Not deferrable and not renewable: the fellowship is for a single eleven-month period from mid-August with initial programme Orientation, and there is no flexibility in start and end dates. There is no return-home requirement, but relocation to the Washington, DC area is a programme requirement if the Fellow does not already live there. The Fellow cannot maintain a teaching position while serving; a leave of absence must be secured or employment terminated. The AEF Programme does not arrange housing. Fellows receive a monthly stipend and are not considered employees of the hosting office, so they do not earn sick or annual leave, although up to ten personal days and ten sick days are allowed without stipend reduction. All stipends are reportable to the Internal Revenue Service and the AEF Programme does not withhold taxes; fellows may need to file Form 1040-ES and pay estimated income tax. Current and former AEF Fellows are not eligible to apply for a second fellowship. No clinical restriction is published.

scholarships.title: Office of Science Graduate Student Research (SCGSR) Program

scholarships.deadline: Applications are due November 4, 2026, at 5:00PM ET. This is 2026 Solicitation 2. The online application system closes at 5:00 PM Eastern Time and no additional materials will be accepted after it. 2027 Solicitation 1 dates are published but all tentative: application opens February 2027, applications due May 2027.
scholarships.description: SCGSR provides supplemental awards to thesis-based doctoral students to conduct part of their dissertation research at a DOE national laboratory or facility, in collaboration with a DOE laboratory scientist, in a DOE Office of Science priority research area. Awardees receive a monthly living stipend of up to $3,600 while at the host laboratory, plus up to $3,000 total for inbound and outbound transportation if the host laboratory is more than 50 miles from their home graduate institution. The award does not pay tuition or fees, does not cover supplies and materials, and does not cover travel during the project; the student must remain enrolled full-time at their home institution and keep paying their own tuition. Successful applicants are considered guest scientists at the host laboratory, not employees.
scholarships.duration: 3 to 12 consecutive months of research at a DOE laboratory/facility, within a project period bounded by published earliest and latest start dates
scholarships.application_period: 2026 Solicitation 2: online application opened August 12, 2026 and closes 5:00 PM ET on November 4, 2026. Offer notifications April 1 - 16, 2027. Proposed project periods may start as early as June 7, 2027 and must start no later than October 4, 2027. 2027 Solicitation 1 (tentative): application opens February 2027, applications due May 2027, offers September 2027, project periods starting November 2027 and ending no later than March 2028.

scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are first subject to an eligibility and compliance review. All eligible and compliant applications are then reviewed externally by subject matter experts in the field of the proposed research, using the DOE Office of Science's standard merit review processes. Two merit review criteria apply: (1) Scientific and/or Technical Merit of the Proposed Research, asking whether the research is well-conceived with a clear understanding of the scientific and technical challenges, whether the method and approach are appropriate, whether the graduate student is sufficiently well prepared, and whether DOE laboratory resources are adequate, including whether necessary access to a scientific user facility has been secured by the collaborating scientist; and (2) Relevance of the Proposed Research to Graduate Thesis Research and Training, asking whether the proposed research can make a significant contribution to the applicant's thesis project and whether it will enhance the applicant's graduate training and research skills. Applications are selected for award based on the results of peer review and other program policy factors, including availability of funds and balance of portfolio. The application materials received, including the research proposal, provide the sole basis for evaluation. Participation in other DOE programmes is collected for internal purposes only and does not affect selection.
scholarships.program_type: Government research fellowship
scholarships.best_fit: Full-time U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents who have already obtained Ph.D. candidacy with an approved thesis topic, are enrolled in a thesis-based research Ph.D. in a DOE-supported STEM field at an accredited U.S. institution, and can arrange a 3 to 12 month in-person research residency with a collaborating DOE laboratory scientist at a participating laboratory.
scholarships.notes: Not deferrable in the ordinary sense, but the award period may be changed under exceptional circumstances, such as unexpected schedule changes at scientific user facilities, with the support of both the collaborating DOE laboratory scientist and the primary graduate thesis advisor; such requests must reach the SCGSR Program Manager at least 20 business days in advance with signed consent letters from both, and the overall project period must remain the same length as proposed. Cumulative SCGSR award periods across all awards may not exceed 12 months. The award is not an internship and not a full graduate fellowship: the SCGF programme, which provided a stipend and tuition support for up to three years, is no longer accepting applications. Awardees are not employees of the host laboratory or DOE and are not entitled to employee benefits. Regular travel between the host laboratory and the university during the award period violates the terms and conditions, because a full-time schedule at the host is required during normal laboratory business hours; awardees may observe the host's holidays but must report any expected interruption to the collaborating scientist and the SCGSR Program Manager. Awardees become ineligible if, after applying, they accept a separate non-SCGSR appointment from the host laboratory, such as an hourly paid intern or a full-time or temporary position. Medical research, or biological research on model systems for the purpose of understanding disease or pathogens, is not eligible, which excludes clinical and medical-degree routes; joint MD/PhD, joint JD/PhD, DVM, MBA, MD, JD and joint BS/MS programmes are all ineligible. Published work based on the research should carry the SCGSR acknowledgement statement, including contract number DE-SC0014664.

scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are sifted against the eligibility criteria from October 2026, then independent reading committees assess all eligible applications from mid-October 2026 to January 2027. British embassies and high commissions produce shortlists and interview candidates in March to April 2027; results are announced from mid-June 2027. Applicants are assessed on leadership and influencing skills, the ability to build professional relationships to achieve positive outcomes, the reasons for the course and university choice (linked to UK priorities such as promoting growth and prosperity, building climate resilience, strengthening security and stability, and supporting development for more inclusive and effective societies), and a realistic short, mid and long-term career plan. Chevening states: 'The use of AI software to generate answers in Chevening applications is strictly prohibited.' The official page does not publish a separate SIDS selection weighting, so the SIDS element appears to be applied alongside the standard Chevening assessment.

Opting in for the SIDS element does not affect your chances of a standard Chevening Scholarship.
scholarships.notes: Applicants must commit to returning to their home country (country of award) for at least two years after the scholarship ends. SIDS scholars must study on a course addressing a national development priority or capacity shortage. The award is a one-year master's degree; Chevening publishes no deferral or renewal provisions. Reference letters must be uploaded at least seven working days before the interview - 'Failure to do so will result in your application no longer being considered for a Chevening award.' Applicants must not have previously studied in the UK on a UK government-funded scholarship. No clinical or medical restriction is published.
