scholarships.selection_notes: Chevening publishes the four general Fellowship objectives - supporting mid-career professionals in positions of leadership and influence, offering dynamic training/professional development/research relevant to professional interests and UK international strategic priorities, increasing the breadth and diversity of Chevening awards, and supporting FCDO foreign policy priorities by creating lasting relationships with future leaders, influencers and decision-makers. For this programme the assessment is against the general Chevening Fellowship criteria plus the published programme-specific requirements, and against the needs of a cohort drawn from the listed European countries. Chevening Fellowships are 'an important element of Britain's public diplomacy effort', and fellows are active in their field or subject. Chevening does not publish a separate scoring framework or interview format for this programme; applications for Chevening Scholarships follow the published sifting, reading committee, embassy shortlist and interview stages, while Chevening states that 'Application timelines for Chevening Fellowships vary.'
scholarships.program_type: Government fellowship
scholarships.best_fit: Mid-career professionals who are citizens AND residents of one of the 35 listed European countries, hold a postgraduate qualification or equivalent professional training, have at least five years' relevant professional experience (7,200 hours) in defence, security, government, diplomacy, policing, intelligence, civil protection, resilience, academia, media, energy/infrastructure or international organisations, and can show leadership potential and a commitment to applying what they learn on return.
scholarships.notes: Deferral: 'Applications to defer awards will only be granted in the case of pregnancy.' Extensions: 'Extensions to the original fellowship duration may be permitted in exceptional circumstances, but the total duration must not exceed 12 months. All extensions are subject to the availability of funds and assessed on a case-by-case basis. Extensions are not automatic and should not be assumed.' Return home: 'You are expected to return to your home country for at least one year on completion of your fellowship.' Dependants: 'All Chevening Awards are calculated to support fellow costs only. There are no financial or welfare provisions for dependants of Chevening Fellows. It is strongly advised that Fellows do not bring dependants to the UK', and 'The Chevening Programme will not endorse the visa applications of, nor provide travel for, dependants.' Other conditions: no transfer to any course other than that confirmed in the Final Award Letter; no other publicly funded award during the fellowship period; approval required before any part-time employment or internship outside the approved programme; cannot serve as an official government representative during the fellowship; must not be outside the UK for more than 30 days in total (pro-rata: 3-month tenure up to 7 days outside the UK), and absences without prior notice may suspend the stipend or end the award; must cite Chevening Fellowships in publications; breach may result in withdrawal of the award. Stipend suspension may occur if fellowship terms and conditions are not complied with, if compulsory documentation is not returned, or if the Fellow elects to return home early and submit work from overseas.

scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are assessed on academic excellence, the clear alignment of the research project with the Foundation's mission and four founding themes, the rigour of the research proposal, and the ability to share knowledge for the benefit of society. Only applications meeting the programme's eligibility criteria are assessed. Applicants who pass review are notified by email; all other applicants are informed at the end of the application review period. Applicants shortlisted in the selection process are invited to group meetings and individual interviews, conducted in French or English depending on the applicant's preference. Final decisions are approved by the Board of Directors. The application form is removed from the portal once the competition ends; the confirmation email is the only proof of receipt.
scholarships.program_type: Foundation scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: First- or second-year PhD students in the humanities and social sciences whose research maps onto one of the Foundation's four themes (Human Rights and Dignity; Responsible Citizenship; Canada and the World; People and their Natural Environment), who already have an outstanding academic record and who want mentorship and a non-academic network alongside funding.
scholarships.notes: The Scholarship is a three-year program. It is not deferrable in the sense that the value is adjusted: Scholars may accept other awards, but the value of the Trudeau Scholarship is adjusted based on amounts received from other organizations, institutions or universities, and all additional sources of income must be declared annually. Regardless of other funding, every Scholar receives the full annual $20,000 research, travel and networking allowance and a minimum of $25,000 from the annual stipend. For Scholars studying outside Canada who receive external funding in foreign currency, the Foundation converts that amount into Canadian dollars; the location of study does not affect the Scholarship amount. Scholars may work part-time (up to 20 hours per week) while continuing to receive full benefits, including university or campus-based roles such as research assistant, teaching assistant or lecturer. Scholars may suspend the Scholarship for up to one year for parental, medical, personal or professional leave; the Foundation states Scholars are not employees of the Foundation and it does not provide paid parental leave, and payments are paused until the Scholar re-enrols full-time. Funds begin only after Board of Directors approval, signature of the funding agreement and submission of required documentation. The annual Scholarship is disbursed in three instalments per year. There is no return-home requirement for Canadian students studying abroad or for international students.

scholarships.title: Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarships
scholarships.name: Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarships
scholarships.deadline: No single calendar deadline is published. The Alberta Innovates programme page gives the due date as "Continuous" and states "This program is accepting applications on a seasonal basis. Intake Open Date is specific to each individual university; please contact your university of choice for deadline information." At the University of Calgary, "The Graduate Award Competition opens November 1 of each year" and "Deadlines vary by program"; the Faculty of Graduate Studies reference deadline is February 1.
scholarships.duration: Terms vary from one to four years, depending on the recipient's time in the program. At the University of Calgary the published terms are $26,000 for master's students for up to two years and $31,000 for doctoral students for up to four years.
scholarships.application_period: Continuous at the funder level, with a seasonal intake at each institution. Alberta Innovates publishes the due date as "Continuous". At the University of Calgary the Graduate Award Competition opens November 1 each year, program deadlines vary and must be confirmed with Graduate Program Staff, and results for the Alberta Innovates competition are announced September to December. Awards are paid in the following academic year, with the majority starting in September.

scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is institution-specific. Each of the participating Alberta institutions has its own scholarship application and evaluation processes for students in full-time programmes, and Alberta Innovates directs students to their faculty of graduate studies for that information. At the University of Calgary the competition is merit-based and the applicant must be able to clearly articulate alignment with Alberta Innovates' Applied Digital & Emerging Technology Areas and the potential impacts of the work for Alberta. For the Killam and Open Doctoral categories a first-class average is required, which at the University of Calgary is a grade point average of 3.5 or higher in the last two years of study, though that published indicator is stated for those categories rather than for the Alberta Innovates category. Successful students may normally hold one GAC scholarship per year across the Open Doctoral and Special Awards categories and will be awarded the highest-value scholarship for which they are eligible.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: Master's or doctoral students, including international students, enrolled full time in a thesis-based research programme at the University of Alberta, University of Calgary, University of Lethbridge, Athabasca University or Concordia University of Edmonton, whose research develops an Applied Digital or Emerging Technology in natural sciences or engineering and can produce potential environmental, health, economic and social impacts for Alberta.
scholarships.notes: Multi-year scholarships are renewed annually after the first year upon satisfactory reporting by the student. Students who have been awarded an Alberta Innovates Graduate Student Scholarship must complete annual and final reports through the term of their award, and post-award reports after the end of the award. No deferral rule, no return-home obligation and no clinical or practice-location restriction are published. You may create only one application per competition each year. At the University of Calgary, students in course-based and professional degree programs are NOT eligible for the Graduate Award Competition through which this award is applied for.

scholarships.title: Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen (FES doctoral scholarship for international doctoral candidates)
scholarships.name: Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen (FES doctoral scholarship for international doctoral candidates)
scholarships.deadline: No fixed calendar deadline is published. The programme page states the right time to apply is up to about two years before submission of the dissertation ('bis circa zwei Jahre vor Abgabe der Dissertation'), and the application page directs applicants to the individual scholarship programme for the deadlines. The online application form for Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen is published and open.
scholarships.description: The Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung funds doctoral candidates from abroad who are admitted to a German university, paying 1,500 euros a month plus a supplement for statutory health insurance, together with an extensive political education programme. Applicants must have very good German skills (B2 accepted, also without a certificate, and required even when the dissertation is written in English), socio-political engagement, identification with the values of social democracy, an above-average and fast degree result, and a research project that makes a significant contribution to research. The scholarship does not have to be repaid.
scholarships.duration: As a rule three and a half years; in justified exceptional cases it can be granted for longer, but at the latest until the final examination
scholarships.application_period: Continuous/rolling: applications are accepted while the doctoral thesis can still be completed within the funding period, in principle from about two years before submission of the dissertation. The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year and the final decision is communicated at the latest one week after the relevant meeting.

scholarships.selection_notes: The FES checks the online application for formal and content criteria. In selecting, it particularly considers applications from people who are the first in their family to study and/or have a migration background, as well as from women and from students at universities of applied sciences and in MINT subjects. Suitable applicants are passed to a trust lecturer for a specialist interview that produces an opinion; shortlisted applicants then have a second interview with a member of the selection committee, whose opinion goes to the committee's meeting. The selection committee meets eight to ten times a year and decides on admission; the applicant is informed at the latest one week after the meeting. All applicants are informed by email at each stage. 'Above average' refers to the average grade in the subject at the university location or in the training occupation.

scholarships.notes: The scholarship does not have to be repaid. Applications for the Promotionsförderung für Ausländer:innen require German language skills even where the dissertation is written in English. Medicine is excluded.

scholarships.selection_notes: Only proposals satisfying the eligibility criteria (critères de recevabilité) are transmitted to the evaluation committee and can in no case be funded. Eligible projects are assessed by an independent international-dimension committee convened by the ANR, which may call on external experts and may hear project leaders (with project representatives) after sending questions in advance. The committee produces (1) a list of projects it recommends for funding on the published criteria and (2) a list it proposes not to fund because quality is insufficient on at least one criterion, with a written justification for each project, and may give an opinion on the amount requested. Uninvolved PEPR GFM programme directors then propose to the SGPI which projects could be financed and at what amount; the Prime Minister, after opinion of the CPMo and the SGPI, decides beneficiaries and amounts, and each project is covered by a contract between the ANR and the coordinating institution. Evaluation criteria fall into three groups: (a) scientific ambition and excellence (research question going beyond the documented state of the art, discipline combination justified by the question, dialogue of conceptual frameworks, ethical questions treated as integral to ambition); (b) quality of the consortium, resources mobilised and governance (recognised complementary expertise, adequacy of staff with objectives including a precise role and career benefit for each contractual worker, structured maturation phase, mechanisms for shared appropriation of questions, inventory/acquisition/management strategy for data and samples, recurrent ethical monitoring mechanisms, explicit choices to minimise the environmental footprint, coherent sizing with an argued 0.8-3 M€ budget); (c) fit with the PEPR GFM challenges and impact (clear fit with at least one challenge and the programme's strategic priorities, described scientific/economic/environmental/societal impacts, described sharing of data and results, open-access data strategy with FAIR and CARE and Opidor PGD links, dissemination to academic and non-academic audiences).
scholarships.program_type: Research grant
scholarships.best_fit: A permanent staff member (enseignant-chercheur or chercheur) at a French higher education or research institution who can lead a 36-54 month consortium and needs to build a genuinely new, wide-interdisciplinary or transdisciplinary deep-sea research consortium, typically with 800 k€-3 M€ of ANR money and with doctoral students to hire on the project budget.
scholarships.notes: Aid is awarded as a one-off exceptional grant, distinct from recurrent institutional funding, intended for new actions. It is a grant to an institution, not a personal scholarship: no tuition, living-cost or travel allowance is paid to individual students, and the individuals hired on a project are salaried employees of the host institution. Consortiums without companies are not obliged to conclude and transmit a consortium agreement; where required, the coordinating institution must supply it to the ANR within a maximum of 12 months from signature of the aid contract, and its absence can lead to cessation of funding and repayment under article 6.6 of the Financial Regulation. Beneficiaries must guarantee immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL, deliver a first PGD within 6 months of project start, deposit data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv, and must mention the France 2030 support and logos in communications. Annual indicator reporting to the State and the ANR is mandatory for ex-post evaluation. Financial aid may constitute State aid under TFEU Article 107(1) and is subject to the French research State-aid framework 2022/C 414/01, the RDI exemption regime SA.111723, the de-minimis Regulation 2023/2831 and the 2011/20/EU decision.

scholarships.selection_notes: Only proposals meeting the eligibility criteria (critères de recevabilité) are transmitted to the evaluation committee and can in no case be funded. Eligible projects are evaluated by an independent international-dimension committee, which may use external experts and may hear project leaders (with project representatives) after transmitting questions in advance. The committee delivers to the PEPR PROPSY scientific directors a report with a list of projects recommended for funding, a list of projects it proposes not to fund for insufficient quality on at least one criterion, a written justification for every project, and possibly an opinion on the amounts requested. The PEPR PROPSY scientific directors then propose to the SGPI which projects could be financed and at what amount; the Prime Minister, after SGPI opinion, decides beneficiaries and amounts, and each project is covered by a contract between the ANR and the coordinating institution. Evaluation criteria fall into three groups: (1) excellence and scientific ambition in precision psychiatry - clarity of objectives and hypotheses, innovativeness, ambition, originality, methodological or conceptual rupture against the state of the art, methodological relevance, preliminary data, project feasibility; (2) quality of the consortium, project management, resources mobilised and governance - competence, expertise and involvement of the project leader including capacity to coordinate ambitious multidisciplinary projects or consortia, academic track record, international recognition, quality and complementarity of the scientific consortium, adequacy between human and financial means and the objectives, relevance of the schedule and management of scientific risks with alternative solutions and credible milestones, relevance and efficiency of governance including patient associations and links with industrial partners or other programmes; (3) impact and outcomes - capacity to address precision-psychiatry development issues, active strategy to measure economic and/or societal impact, contribution to solutions for pathophysiological, diagnostic or therapeutic issues, dissemination and valorization strategy in itinere and ex post, adherence to FAIR and Open Science principles and promotion of scientific culture. Committee members and external experts commit to ANR deontology and integrity rules, strict confidentiality, declaration of conflicts of interest, and a ban on AI tools in the evaluation.

It is institutional research funding, not a personal scholarship: nothing is paid to individual students, and tuition, living costs or individual travel allowances are not covered. Consortiums without companies are not obliged to conclude and transmit a consortium agreement; where it is required (mandatory when companies are involved, otherwise when exigé), the coordinating institution must supply it to the ANR within a maximum of 12 months of contract signature, and its absence can lead to cessation of funding and repayment under article 6.6 of the Financial Regulation. Beneficiaries must guarantee immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL, deliver a first PGD within 6 months of project start, deposit data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv, and must mention the France 2030 support with the Plan France 2030 and PEPR PROPSY logos in communications. Funded projects must send accepted publications to the PEPR PROPSY direction team for diffusion and archiving, and annual indicator reporting to the State and the ANR is required. Financial aid may constitute State aid under TFEU Article 107(1) and is subject to the French research State-aid framework 2022/C 414/01, the RDI exemption regime SA.111723, the de-minimis Regulation 2023/2831 and the 2011/20/EU decision. Projects mainly on addictions are out of scope unless addictions appear as secondary phenomena or comorbidities of one of the four targeted disorders.

scholarships.english_requirement: Pre-proposals and detailed proposals, and Annexe 1, must be written in English (rédigées en langue anglaise). The ANR also states that, on request, a translation of the evaluation criteria may be provided.

scholarships.selection_notes: Evaluation and selection are centralised at M-ERA.NET level and take place in two steps: step 1 central evaluation of pre-proposals by independent international experts convened by the M-ERA.NET Call Secretariat, with invitations to step 2 issued in ranking order and taking account of the participating agencies' budget capacity; step 2 central evaluation of detailed proposals by independent international experts convened by the same secretariat. Proposals are ranked on the evaluation results and selection follows the ranking. The list of projects recommended for funding is drawn up by the group of participating funders taking account of their respective budget capacities, and the final funding decision is then taken individually by the funders concerned. Results are sent by the call secretariat to the project coordinators. Evaluation modalities and criteria are those of the call text (Guide for proposers) available on the ANR call page and the M-ERA.NET call site; the ANR adds its own horizontal objectives, which are that projects show significant French participation (in coordination or in charge of a substantial part of the work), generate significant opening and diversification of French collaboration networks, and are ambitious with a clear intention of continuity and evolution of the collaboration. During discussions to separate projects of similar scientific quality within the funder group, projects involving a wider and/or more diverse consortium may be favoured.
scholarships.program_type: Research grant
scholarships.best_fit: A researcher or institution in France leading or joining a materials or battery-technology consortium of at least three funded partners from at least three different countries, whose pre-proposal was recommended in step 1 and who need French ANR co-funding for a maximum 36-month project in one of the four ANR-eligible topics.
scholarships.notes: This is institutional research funding, not a personal scholarship: nothing is paid to individual students and no tuition, living-cost or travel allowance is established for individuals. The aid is paid to each partner's own national or regional organisation, not centrally. Amounts may not be increased between the two steps: increases are not authorised, and projects that do not respect the aid limits or that do not conform to any budgetary adjustments requested by the ANR are declared ineligible. The 20 000 € European-preparation supplement is conditional on adequate planning and activities within the M-ERA.NET project (a dedicated Work Package and budget under the responsibility of an ANR-funded partner), on the activities actually leading to a research proposal involving consortium members in continuity with the M-ERA.NET work, and on the follow-up proposal targeting clearly identified FP10 calls (not co-funded by the ANR) coordinated by the ANR-funded French partner; it is a subject of a final assessment and a supplementary deliverable to the ANR. Beneficiaries commit to immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit of the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL, a FAIR approach to research data, a PGD within 6 months of the scientific start, deposit of data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv, and free-licence release and Software Heritage archiving of software. Any change affecting the whole project (extensions, consortium modifications) must be approved by all partners, their funding agencies and M-ERA.NET. Proposals may be transmitted to other administrations, control bodies and partner funders, and certain national funders are obliged to publish submitted pre-proposals/proposals, which may disclose intellectual-property or business-secret content; applicants are warned to be careful with what they include. The ANR applies the PPST protection of the scientific and technical potential of the nation to projects with foreign public or private partners, and a negative SHFDS/MESR opinion prevents selection without reasons being given.

scholarships.deadline: First call: 'a deadline on Wednesday, 25 November 2026 at 14:00 CET'. From 2027 there will be two calls per year: the first call launched mid-February closes on the last Wednesday of April at 14:00 CET, and the second call launched mid-September closes on the last Wednesday of November at 14:00 CET.
scholarships.duration: Funding may cover up to four years of doctoral training.
scholarships.application_period: The very first call was launched mid-September 2026 with a deadline on Wednesday, 25 November 2026 at 14:00 CET, so the scheme is open on 2026-10-01. From 2027 there will be two calls per year: the first call launched mid-February closes on the last Wednesday of April at 14:00 CET, funding decisions are communicated in July and funded projects must start no later than 1 February of the following year; the second call launched mid-September closes on the last Wednesday of November at 14:00 CET, decisions are communicated in March of the following year and funded projects must start no later than 1 October.

The 2026 call is a pilot for a self-assessment on potential research security aspects.

Because funding goes to the Host Institution and the candidate is employed, the award is a salary rather than a stipend; the beneficiary has an employment relationship with the host, not with the FNR.

scholarships.title: Flanders Trainee Programme (Flanders Traineeship Programme)
scholarships.name: Flanders Trainee Programme (Flanders Traineeship Programme)
scholarships.deadline: No more grants for 2026: 'You can no longer apply for a grant for internships continuing into 2026. There is no more budget available for 2026. A budget will be available again in 2027. You can reapply for internships taking place in 2027 as from January 2027.' Within a funded budget year: 'You can submit your grant application up to six months in advance until one day before the start of your internship.'
scholarships.description: The Flanders Trainee Programme gives young people who hold a secondary or higher education diploma obtained in Flanders financial support for an internship with a multilateral organisation. The grant is made up of a one-off travel allowance and a monthly lump-sum amount for accommodation and living expenses, both set in advance; the monthly amount depends on the host city. Nationality and official place of residence are irrelevant, and the programme targets people interested in global challenges such as climate change, food security or human rights. The 2026 budget is exhausted; a budget is available again for 2027, with applications reopenable from January 2027.
scholarships.duration: The grant covers an internship of at least two and up to six months. The internship can be extended to a total duration of six months, or nine months where the internship concerns a project funded by the Government of Flanders.
scholarships.application_period: The 2026 budget is exhausted and applications for 2026 are closed. The 2027 budget reopens for applications in January 2027 for internships taking place in 2027, and new internship vacancies will be published on the programme's internships page from late 2026 onwards. Inside a funded budget year the published rule is that you may apply at any time of the year until one day before your internship starts, up to six months in advance, but a grant is only granted while budget remains.

scholarships.selection_notes: No competitive jury or published ranking is described for this programme. The published route is a budget-limited reimbursement scheme: in principle you can apply at any time of the year, but you only get a grant if budget is still available, and if a budget is no longer available for the current year that is announced clearly on the programme website; an application submitted after the budget is gone is not processed and is not kept until a new budget is available. The average administrative turnaround time is three weeks. The grant is reduced by any remuneration or financial allowance you receive for the same internship from another Belgian or foreign government or from the multilateral organisation itself.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: Anyone under 35 with a secondary or higher education diploma earned at a Flemish institution, of any nationality, who has already secured or is about to secure an internship at a qualifying multilateral organisation such as the UN, NATO-adjacent bodies, the OECD, the WHO family, the Council of Europe, the Benelux Union or an EU institution.
scholarships.notes: The grant is explicitly not a salary but a lump-sum reimbursement of expenses actually borne, made up of a one-off travel allowance and an expense allowance for accommodation and living expenses. Coverage is partial: it does not pay tuition or course fees, there is no travel payment for an internship in Belgium, and the amounts are capped at a fixed 200 or 500 EUR travel payment plus a city-based monthly living amount. The internship can be extended to a total of six months, or nine months for internships linked to a project funded by the Government of Flanders. If you end the internship early you must inform the programme and may have to repay part of the grant, the amount being determined by the number of days you actually worked. There is no clinical or professional restriction published beyond the requirement that the host be a qualifying multilateral organisation.

scholarships.description: A monthly stipend for foreign students who already hold an admission confirmation from an Estonian higher education institution for the 2026/2027 academic year. The rate is EUR 350 per month for first-cycle (BA) and master's studies and EUR 660 per month for doctoral studies. The Board pays the scholarship to the host university, which then disburses it. The scheme is funded under bilateral intergovernmental or inter-ministerial agreements and is run through the Estonian Scholarship Programme.

scholarships.name: UC Doctoral Scholarship (UCDS)
scholarships.deadline: Applications for the October round close 15 October 2026. The round opened 20 August 2026 and is for students who intend to start their doctoral studies before 1 July 2027.
scholarships.description: The UC Doctoral Scholarship is a centrally funded Te Whare WÄnanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury award that supports study towards a first research doctoral degree in any discipline at UC. Its published value is financial assistance of $32,650 per 120 points of thesis-only enrolment, plus tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment, for up to a total of 360 points. The same round can add recognition-only or top-up Prestige awards, but applicants who hold one of the Core scholarships are also automatically considered for Prestige awards with no separate application, and the Prestige value is added on top of the Core value (for example a $32,650 p.a. stipend becomes $37,650 p.a. with a $5,000 top-up). It is not a New Zealand Government scholarship; it is a university award and subject to funding availability and annual review.
scholarships.duration: Up to a total of 360 points of thesis-only doctoral enrolment (three years of full-time study)
scholarships.application_period: Two rounds a year. October round: opens 20 August 2026, closes 15 October 2026, for doctoral study starting before 1 July 2027. May round: opens 20 March, closes 15 May, for students starting in the second half of 2027. UC states applications generally open approximately eight weeks before the closing date.

scholarships.title: Vice-Chancellor's International High Achievers Scholarship (VCIHAS)
scholarships.name: Vice-Chancellor's International High Achievers Scholarship (VCIHAS)
scholarships.deadline: Applications close 31 January 2027 for Semester 1, 2027 intake, and 4 July 2027 for Semester 2, 2027 intake.
scholarships.description: The Vice-Chancellor's International High Achievers Scholarship is a Charles Darwin University award for international students with a record of academic excellence. CDU publishes that it covers 50% of the tuition fee for an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree, for the full duration of the course, and that it is neither transferable for cash nor refundable and cannot be transferred to another person, semester, course or year. Applicants must have a minimum overall score of 95% in their highest completed qualification, must be paying international student fees, and must not hold another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency. Results are announced during Orientation Week.

scholarships.english_requirement: CDU requires all higher education applicants to satisfy the English Language Proficiency Requirements for their chosen course and to supply evidence of this at the time of application. CDU's published minimum English test scores are: IELTS Academic overall minimum 6.5 with no band below 6.0 for postgraduate and overall minimum 6.0 with no band below 6.0 for undergraduate; PTE Academic overall minimum 58 with no score below 50 for postgraduate and overall minimum 50 with no score below 50 for undergraduate; TOEFL overall minimum 79 with a minimum writing score of 21 for postgraduate and overall minimum 60 with a minimum writing score of 21 for undergraduate; Cambridge English Advanced overall minimum 176 with no skill below 169 for postgraduate and overall minimum 169 with no skill below 169 for undergraduate; CDU ELICOS EAP004 for postgraduate and EAP003 for undergraduate; and an approved English test completed within two years of commencement. IELTS One Skill Retake is accepted, allowing a single skill to be retaken within 60 days. Alternative evidence routes published on the same page include Year 12 in an approved English-speaking country, 0.5 FTE of higher education study in an approved country completed within the past five years where relevant, an enabling course, a TAFE qualification at Certificate III or higher, current AHPRA registration, two years of full-time equivalent employment in English-medium roles within the last five years in a recognised English-speaking country, or a primary language pathway declaration.

scholarships.selection_notes: CDU publishes the selection criteria as the overall score in your highest completed qualification plus a supporting statement. The application form adds that the decision of the University selection panel is final, and the declaration confirms the process is competitive. CDU publishes no interview requirement, no weighting for the two criteria, no offer round structure and no appeal process for VCIHAS; other CDU International College scholarships on the same page do publish an interview requirement, so confirm whether an interview applies to VCIHAS.
scholarships.program_type: University scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: International applicants with a 95% or higher overall score in their highest completed qualification who are applying to commence study at CDU in Semester 1 or Semester 2 2027 in an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree and who can fund the remaining 50% of their tuition fees themselves.
scholarships.notes: This is not full funding: it covers 50% of the tuition fee only, and the recipient must pay their portion of tuition on or before the first day of teaching of each semester. The scholarship is neither transferable for cash nor refundable, and cannot be transferred to another person, semester, course or year. It is conditional rather than open-ended: it ends at the earliest of course completion, exhaustion of the maximum scholarship value, or loss of ongoing eligibility, and retaining it requires a minimum GPA of 5.3 with no fail grade in any unit and a full-time enrolment of 40 credit points (0.5 EFTSL) each semester unless a reduced load or leave of absence is approved. Only one CDU tuition fee scholarship may be held at a time, and holding another scholarship from an Australian or foreign sponsoring agency disqualifies the applicant. No deferral, return-home, clinical restriction, tax treatment or award renewal terms are published on the pages read. Official pages disagree on the statement length: the scholarship page says up to 600 words, the application form says 500 words or less.

scholarships.description: The ANU Vice-Chancellor's International Achievement Award is an Australian National University award whose stated objective is to attract a diverse range of academically capable overseas students to enrol in undergraduate and postgraduate coursework programs at ANU, funded by the University. ANU publishes the value as 20% off first-year tuition fees, with the tuition scholarship applied towards tuition at the start of each semester for the one year of the award. It is restricted to residents of China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, and excludes the Doctor of Medicine and Surgery (MChD) and the Master of Digital Transformation and Entrepreneurship (MDTE). scholarships.selection_notes: ANU states that selection is based on academic merit, that only applicants who meet all the eligibility criteria will be considered, that qualifications submitted for admission will be converted to the common scale which determines whether an applicant is eligible, and that eligible applicants with multiple qualifications will be ranked according to the qualification used as the basis of admission. scholarships.program_type: University scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: International students resident in China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea or the Democratic People's Republic of Korea who are applying for admission to an eligible ANU undergraduate, honours, graduate certificate or postgraduate coursework program, meet a Selection Rank of 85 or equivalent (undergraduate) or a GPA of 5.5 or equivalent (postgraduate), and are not already covered by external sponsorship of their tuition fees.
scholarships.notes: This is not full funding and should not be budgeted as such: the published value is 20% off first-year tuition fees for one year only, and recipients pay the balance of all tuition fees by the prescribed date each session. ANU states recipients are responsible for the costs of books, study materials, accommodation and all other costs of study. The award can be offered only once at each level of study, with two published exceptions: progression from an undergraduate degree (AQF Level 7) to a one-year Honours program (AQF Level 8), and packaged offers such as a Graduate Certificate leading to a Master's degree. Eligibility is by residential status, not citizenship, and is restricted to China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea; residents of all other countries apply to the separate ANU International Achievement Award. Holding external sponsorship covering all or part of your ANU tuition fees disqualifies you. Deferral, renewal, return-home obligations, clinical restrictions and tax treatment are not published on the page read; the Conditions of Award (63/2026) PDF is the document that governs them and could not be read.

scholarships.title: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 - Research Students (Embassy Recommendation)
scholarships.name: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship for 2027 - Research Students (Embassy Recommendation)
scholarships.deadline: No central deadline is published. MEXT states that all procedures for the Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarships are conducted through Japanese embassies, consulates in your countries, or institutions of higher education in Japan; candidates should contact the Japanese embassy (or consulate general) in their own country for the application date, and the Study in Japan page states that the type and field of application may vary from country to country and that applicants should check with the Japanese embassy or other Japanese diplomatic mission for any openings.
scholarships.description: The MEXT Scholarship research-student route funds postgraduate research study at a Japanese graduate school: it exempts tuition, pays a monthly scholarship of ¥143,000-¥145,000, and provides round-trip travel expenses (airfare). Recipients are selected by the Japanese embassy or consulate general in their country after sitting that mission's Japanese and English qualifying examinations, and are then placed at a graduate school. This record covers the Embassy Recommendation route for the 2027 cohort; the separate University Recommendation route is administered by individual Japanese universities.
scholarships.duration: Embassy Recommendation: irregular course within 2 years; regular course: standard school year (when necessary, 6 months preliminary education will be added)
scholarships.application_period: Applications for the 2027 cycle are handled at embassy/consulate level. MEXT lists the 2027 Embassy Recommendation Research Student recruitment under "募集中のプログラム" (programmes currently being recruited). No central opening or closing date is published; embassies set and publish their own deadlines and sit their own qualifying examinations.

scholarships.title: GKS (Global Korea Scholarship) Program - Undergraduate Degree Programs
scholarships.name: GKS (Global Korea Scholarship) Program - Undergraduate Degree Programs
scholarships.deadline: Announcement by NIIED in September. Application submission: Embassy Track in September; University Track September - November. Screening and selection October - December. Final results announced by NIIED in December. The page publishes month-level timing only; no day-level deadline is published on this page.
scholarships.description: The Korean government-invited scholarship degree programme that funds a year of Korean language training followed by an associate degree (2-3 years) or bachelor's degree (4-6 years) at a designated GKS university in Korea. The published benefits list is airfare, Korean language training fees, tuition and monthly allowances. Selection runs through two routes: an Embassy Track that applies through the Korean embassy/consulate, and a University Track in which the student applies directly to a GKS-designated university (UIC specialisation and Associate Degree).
scholarships.duration: Korean language training (1 year) + associate degree programs (2-3 years), bachelor's degree programs (4-6 years)
scholarships.application_period: Embassy Track: applications accepted in September. University Track: applications accepted September to November. On 2026-10-01 the University Track falls inside the published September-November window; the Embassy Track submission month published is September.
scholarships.official_source: National Institute for International Education (NIIED), Ministry of Education, Republic of Korea

scholarships.notes: Separate track from the GKS Graduate Degree Programs: different quota, different university lists (undergraduate lists 28 Type A and 42 Type B/R-GKS universities), a compulsory one-year Korean language training year, and a different application route. The University's University Information File carries the department-level detail. The 'Apply for the GKS(Global Korea Scholarship)' control on the page returned the on-page message 'It is not the application period.' on 2026-10-01, which relates to the Study in Korea online route used by the Embassy Track; the University Track route is a direct application to the university.

scholarships.degree: Doctoral, Postdoctoral, Research (faculty and doctoral/postdoctoral scholars)
scholarships.degree_levels: Doctoral, Postdoctoral, Research (faculty and doctoral/postdoctoral scholars)
scholarships.deadline: Applications can be submitted online throughout the year. The applications should be uploaded at least three months before the due date of the Conference.
scholarships.description: This scheme gives partial financial assistance to Indian social science scholars who have been formally invited to present a paper at an international conference abroad. Assistance covers air travel, visa fee, travel insurance, local conveyance, maintenance for the stay, and registration fee up to US$200. Regular faculty receive up to 50 percent of the total cost of the visit, while SC/ST faculty, persons with benchmark disability, and postgraduate/doctoral/postdoctoral researchers without salary protection may be considered for the full cost of the visit.
scholarships.duration: Period of stay abroad not exceeding the actual days of the conference plus travel dates
scholarships.application_period: Rolling - applications are submitted online throughout the year, and must be uploaded at least three months before the due date of the Conference.
scholarships.official_source: Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), Ministry of Education, Government of India

scholarships.eligibility_summary: Indian social science scholars in regular service at a UGC-recognized university/deemed university/college, an Institute of National Importance, or an ICSSR research or recognised institute, holding a PhD, or post-graduate/PhD/post-doctoral scholars at an advanced stage of study, or certain independent senior professionals.

The Council reserves the right to reject any application without assigning any reason and is not responsible for postal delays or loss.
scholarships.program_type: Government research travel grant
scholarships.best_fit: Indian social science scholars (faculty, PhD scholars, postdocs, and some independent senior professionals) with a formally accepted oral paper at a high-value international conference outside India, who need help with the cost of attending.
scholarships.notes: Not deferrable: the application will not be entertained or considered in any case after participation and presentation of the paper in the Conference. Not renewable in the sense that a scholar can avail of the award only twice in his/her lifetime, and a second application is considered only after a gap of three years. No must-return-home rule is published because this is a travel grant, not a degree award. Post-award: expenditure is reimbursed on submission of the original boarding pass, attendance certificate, statement of expenditure and a report on participation; ICSSR may ask for a copy of the tickets booked and the visa obtained before departure. Publication is expected in high valued journals/edited books/impactful reports with due acknowledgement of ICSSR, and the paper presentation should clearly display the ICSSR logo and its support. A second time application is not considered for poster presentations, session chairs, conveners, rapporteurs, or workshop/training/refresher/summer/winter course attendance.

scholarships.description: The ICSSR provides financial assistance to Indian social science scholars who need to travel abroad for data collection or to consult archival material in connection with their research. It is aimed at scholars who proposed fieldwork abroad in their original approved ICSSR fellowship or project proposal and have made substantial progress, or at independent scholars for whom data collection abroad is academically justified and the research is at an advance stage. The total expenditure on the foreign visit, including economy class airfare, visa fee, travel insurance, local conveyance and maintenance, is supported within the prescribed norms of Government notifications.
scholarships.duration: The visit under this Scheme should be realistic and not more than of two weeks duration

scholarships.notes: Not deferrable and not renewable: this is a single research visit capped at two weeks, not a tenure. scholarships.title: University of Sharjah Research Assistant (RA) and Teaching Assistant (TA) Scholarship for Master's Students
scholarships.name: University of Sharjah Research Assistant (RA) and Teaching Assistant (TA) Scholarship for Master's Students
scholarships.deadline: Applications for Master's programs will be open from 5 October 2026 to 12 November 2026.
scholarships.description: The University of Sharjah offers work-based Research Assistant and Teaching Assistant scholarships to eligible master's students, who must commit 20 hours per week at the University and may not be employed elsewhere during the scholarship period. The award is awarded by the concerned academic department based on its academic and research needs and available opportunities. The official page read does not publish the benefit amount, whether tuition is waived, or any list of expenses the scholarship covers, so this record is deliberately left unquantified rather than assumed to be full funding.
scholarships.duration: Tied to enrolment in a full master's degree programme; continuation is subject to the bylaws and regulations of the University of Sharjah. No scholarship duration is published.
scholarships.application_period: Master's applications are open 5 October 2026 to 12 November 2026 for the published 2026/2027 intake. The University publishes no separate RA/TA scholarship application window; it states that meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not guarantee a scholarship and that selection is subject to departmental evaluation, availability and approval.

English language proficiency test results are valid for two years from the date of the examination. scholarships.title: Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) Program
scholarships.name: Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) Program
scholarships.deadline: The African Development Bank publishes no central JADS call opening or closing date, so there is no central deadline to quote. Applications go only through the partner universities, and the AfDB's own "List of Universities" page publishes each partner's intake and application window: Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University - "Application Deadlines are as following: April Enrollment: October / September Enrollment: April"; Hiroshima University Graduate School of Advanced Science and Engineering - "Month of Intake: April - Preliminary Survey: Oct 18-29 - Application period: Nov 8-19 - Exam. Period: Nov 29-Dec 8" and, for its second course, "Preliminary Evaluation for Apr. Oct 4-8, Preliminary Evaluation for Oct.: Mar. 7-11, Application Period for Apr.: Nov 4-15, Application Period for Oct.: Apr. 4-22"; The University of Tokyo Graduate School of Frontier Sciences - "Month of Intake: April or October / Examination: Schedule A (application period: mid June) Schedule B (application period: mid November)"; Sophia University - "Month of Intake: September / Deadline of Application: Web entry: Mid of March ~ Early April; Application: Mid of April". Kyoto University and Kogakuin University are listed with "Please refer to the program website".
scholarships.description: The Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) is a capacity building programme of the African Development Bank and the Government of Japan that offers high-achieving African students a two-year scholarship to pursue post-graduate study at master's level in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability and engineering. AfDB states it covers tuition for the 24-month study programme, a monthly living stipend, air travel between the scholar's home country and the host university at the start and end of the scholarship period, and health insurance usually obtained through the university, plus an additional six months for advance preparatory study or internships after graduation. It is not complete funding in AfDB's own terms: the Bank publishes an explicit exclusion list covering visa application costs, family members, extra-curricular courses, additional travel during the study programme, supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars, internships and educational equipment such as computers. AfDB publishes no stipend figure and no central call date, so the amount and the closing date must both be confirmed with the chosen partner university and the JADS Secretariat.
scholarships.duration: Two-year scholarship; "the scholarship only covers the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less"
scholarships.application_period: Annual partner-university admissions cycle. As published by AfDB on 2026-10-01, the next windows relative to that date are: Ritsumeikan Asia Pacific University April-intake deadline in October 2026; Hiroshima University preliminary survey 18-29 October 2026 and application period 8-19 November 2026; Hiroshima University second course preliminary evaluation 4-8 October 2026; The University of Tokyo Schedule B application period in mid November 2026. AfDB states there is no separate application to the Bank and no central JADS window.
scholarships.official_source: African Development Bank Group, with the Government of Japan

scholarships.selection_notes: All eligible applications are comparatively evaluated by the Program Implementation Unit hired by the African Development Bank, and the final selection is approved by the JADS Secretariat. Evaluation focuses on educational and professional excellence, commitment to home country development priorities, the quality of the statement of purpose, financial status and geographic diversity of awardees. The Bank's management decision and approval of the finalist also takes into consideration geographical diversity, gender balance, equity and inclusiveness (unusual circumstances or hardships when assessing employment experience), financial needs (applicants are financially constrained), and special consideration for applicants with special needs.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship (multilateral - African Development Bank and the Government of Japan)
scholarships.best_fit: Citizens of an African Development Bank regional member country who are 35 or younger and in good health, hold a bachelor's degree or equivalent in energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering or a related field with an excellent academic record, and have at least one year of paid employment in their home country or another African country obtained within the past three years of completing that degree. Applicants must already be able to apply to an approved master's course at a JADS partner university, must not be enrolled in another graduate degree programme, and cannot be AfDB Group staff or a close relative of AfDB Group staff.
scholarships.notes: There is no separate application to the African Development Bank - "Only candidates who have been offered admission and endorsed by the university will be considered for the JADS Program", and a university admission offer alone is not a scholarship award. The scholarship "may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support/fellowship you might have"; finalists and awardees must inform the JADS Secretariat of other funding, and "The JADS stipend may be withdrawn completely or partially if during the scholarship period the program has evidence of additional sources of support." Deferral and renewal are not addressed on the AfDB pages. Scholars "are expected to return to their home countries and contribute to national and continental socio-economic development, using the newly acquired knowledge and skills." No clinical or field-of-practice restriction is published, but the approved master's courses are limited to energy, agriculture, health, environmental sustainability, engineering and related areas. "The scholarship only covers the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less."

scholarships.english_requirement: Published and mandatory. Applicants must be "proficient in reading, writing, and speaking English" and the instructions state "High-level proficiency in written and spoken English is required for the Fellowship", because "All activities - including academic sessions, discussions, meetings, cultural activities, and social interactions - will be in English." Applicants complete a self-assessment against the levels Absolute Beginner, Novice, Intermediate, Advanced, or Very Advanced; no standardized English test score is required. Applicants who are deaf should indicate proficiency in reading and writing standard English and proficiency in American Sign Language, and are told that "interpretation in the United States may only be available in ASL, so selected Fellows who are deaf should be proficient in, or be prepared to learn, ASL prior to arrival in the United States."

All submitted applications are final and cannot be changed by any means."]
scholarships.selection_notes: "The Fellowship selection process is a merit-based open competition." After the deadline, all eligible applications are reviewed and scored against the published criteria: proficiency speaking, reading and writing in English; a proven record of accomplishment in business, trade, emerging technologies, governance and/or security; a demonstrated and clear interest in building and maintaining partnerships with American organizations and businesses that advance shared goals; a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa and contribute skills and talents; the ability to work cooperatively in groups and to respect others; strong social and communication skills; and demonstrated adaptability and the ability to lead effectively in varying and changing environments. Applicants who do not meet the technical eligibility requirements "will not be forwarded to the selection committee." Semi-finalists are then interviewed in person by the U.S. embassy or consulate in their home country between October 2026 and January 2027. Selected finalists must participate in mandatory Pre-Fellowship Orientation activities and a visa interview within Sub-Saharan Africa. The U.S. Department of State and IREX "reserve the right to verify all information included in the application", requiring documentation of age, citizenship and residency at the interview stage; any discrepancy or false information means "the application will be immediately declared invalid and the applicant ineligible." PDE applicants are assessed separately on the ability to work professionally in a U.S. organization, articulation of clear and specific learning goals, flexibility, alignment between professional background, institute track and potential U.S. organizations, interest in sustaining engagement with U.S. professionals, and strong English proficiency.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship (U.S. Department of State educational and cultural exchange programme, administered by IREX)
scholarships.best_fit: Citizens and permanent residents of any of the 49 listed Sub-Saharan African countries, aged 25 to 35 on the application deadline of 13 October 2026 (exceptional applicants aged 21-24 may be considered), proficient in reading, writing and speaking English, with a proven record of accomplishment in business and trade, emerging technologies, governance and/or security, and with a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa. Applicants must not be U.S. citizens or permanent residents, must be eligible for a U.S. J-1 visa, must not be U.S. Government employees or their immediate family, and must not be alumni or prior participants of the Fellowship.
scholarships.notes: This is a non-degree exchange programme, so no tuition is charged or funded and no degree is awarded. It is not deferrable, not renewable, and a Fellow cannot re-apply: the technical eligibility rules exclude "alumni or prior participants of the Mandela Washington Fellowship". The programme requires a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa, and applicants must be residents of an eligible country as of February 1, 2027 and at the start of the Fellowship in June 2027. "Fellows are not allowed to have dependents, including spouses and children, accompany them during the Fellowship." There is no clinical or field-of-practice restriction. Selected Fellows must complete a detailed Medical History Form and, if applicable, an Accommodations Form, and the programme "strongly encourages all eligible applicants to apply regardless of your medical history or accommodations you may require." Fellows with disabilities and chronic health conditions receive reasonable accommodations and support at no cost. Fellows must attend and fully participate in all required sessions and program activities, and housing may be shared: "Every effort will be made to provide single-occupancy housing; however, Fellows may share a double-occupancy bedroom with another Fellow of the same sex and a bathroom with one or more Fellows of the same sex." The U.S. Department of State and IREX reserve the right to alter or suspend Fellowship activities at any time, and selection of finalists may be reviewed case by case for nationals of countries subject to a U.S. entry or visa suspension.

scholarships.deadline: No single global deadline is published. Deadlines are set per country operation and published on the UNHCR country help pages (published 2026/2027 examples: Rwanda 7 August 2026; Kyrgyzstan 21 August 2026; Slovakia 31 August 2026). scholarships.description: DAFI is UNHCR's dedicated tertiary scholarship programme for refugees and returnees, founded in 1992 and funded principally by the Government of Germany. The published scholarship package covers a range of costs including tuition and study materials, food, transportation and accommodation, and depending on the needs and capacity of the individual country operation or programme partner may also cover academic preparatory, language and ICT courses as well as psychosocial support. It funds ISCED 6 bachelor's or equivalent programmes and ISCED 5 short-cycle tertiary and TVET programmes of two years or more, and it explicitly does not cover master's studies. Applications are made through the DAFI Programme Management Platform, which was live and accepting registrations and submissions on 2026-10-01.
scholarships.duration: Duration follows the degree programme enrolled in: ISCED 6 bachelor's or equivalent, or ISCED 5 short-cycle tertiary / TVET of two years or more
scholarships.application_period: Country-specific. The 2026/2027 cycle ran on country-published windows in July-August 2026 (Rwanda 15 July-7 August 2026; Kyrgyzstan 7 July-21 August 2026; Slovakia 1 July-31 August 2026). New country calls for the next cycle are announced on the relevant UNHCR country help page and applications are submitted through the DAFI Programme Management Platform.

scholarships.notes: The scholarship does not cover master's degree programmes (published: 'DAFI does NOT cover Masters studies.' / 'Please note that the scholarship does not cover master's degree programs.'). Awards are not deferrable, renewable or multi-year by default: funding follows admission to an ISCED 5 or ISCED 6 programme in the cycle applied for. No return-home obligation is published, and because studies take place in the country of asylum or home country no relocation is required. No clinical or field-of-study restriction is published beyond the general rule that the programme targets undergraduate and short-cycle tertiary/TVET study. The 2024 cycle was the first since 2020 with a decrease in the number of scholars supported, reflecting reduced global funding. As this is a multi-country programme with no published global deadline, the applicable deadline is the one published by the applicant's own UNHCR country operation; the published 2026/2027 country windows had all closed by 31 August 2026 at the time of verification, and the platform itself remained live and accepting registrations on 2026-10-01.

Applicants must have interrupted any stay in Austria for at least six months before taking up the grant. Gainful employment is not allowed, with a marginal employment exemption of EUR 551.10 per month in 2026. A final report is obligatory at the end of the stay. The grant contract (Letter of Award and Letter of Acceptance) defines start and end date, grant amount, payment modalities, compulsory attendance at the guest institution, performance report and final report, data protection and repayment obligations. The grant cannot be used to enrol in a Master or PhD programme in Austria. Without written proof of accommodation in Austria, a residence permit is not granted. scholarships.description: The Programa Portugal-Berkeley is an FCT call, run with FLAD and UC Berkeley, that supports doctoral students to spend a research stay as Visiting Student Researchers at UC Berkeley for up to six months. FCT launches the call to promote the internationalisation of Portuguese science and to foster research exchange between Portuguese universities and UC Berkeley in areas of mutual scientific interest. The selected candidate's home institution (CPS) is responsible for the administrative procedures to acquire the Visiting Student Researcher status and pays the University Services Fee, the DS-2019 visa processing fee and the Institute of European Studies administrative fees at UC Berkeley. The selected candidate must arrange and financially cover their own travel, accommodation and health insurance, and the call publishes no direct stipend or award figure.

scholarships.selection_notes: Assessment is carried out by an academic committee appointed by FCT and FLAD. Criterion A: candidate's curriculum, considering academic grades, track record and scientific achievements including peer-reviewed publications, scholarships, prizes, conferences and project participation (40%). Criterion C: motivation letter explaining the relevance of the stay and the work to be developed for the scientific ambition of the doctoral work plan, and the expected impact of the stay on the candidate's career (30%). scholarships.name: Programa RESTART — 4ª Edição (FCT research funding after parental leave)
scholarships.deadline: Applications open 01 October 2026 at 14h and close 13 November 2026 at 17h (Portuguese time)
scholarships.description: RESTART is an FCT funding instrument that competitively finances individual R&D projects in all scientific domains for researchers who have recently taken a parental leave, including adoption leave. The award is a project grant of up to EUR 50,000 per project for a maximum of 18 months, drawn from a total budget allocation of EUR 1.6 million, and it is held by the beneficiary R&D unit rather than paid as a personal living stipend. Candidates must hold a doctorate, be an integrated doctoral member of an R&D unit or hold a contract with a State laboratory, and have taken a parental leave of at least 120 days (or at least 72 days in a shared leave, whether exclusive or shared) between 3 June 2025 and 1 October 2026 inclusive.

scholarships.description: The Rufford Small Grants Programme funds fieldwork costs for small-scale, pilot nature conservation projects run by early-career conservationists in developing and emerging economy countries. Funding is staged across four levels - 1st Rufford Small Grant up to GBP 7,000, 2nd Rufford Small Grant up to GBP 8,000, Booster Grant up to GBP 12,000 and Completion Grant up to GBP 18,000 - and the Foundation aims to provide between 50% and 100% of project costs, requiring evidence of co-funding where it is not the only funder. Only fieldwork costs are considered, and award holders must provide project updates and a final report that are posted on their Rufford webpage. There are no deadlines, so the programme was open on the verification date.

Selected participants complete training modules on TEFConnect, submit a business plan, financial projection and pitch video, and then provide business registration, tax and banking documents before the seed capital is paid into their business account. scholarships.description: The DAAD EPOS programme funds individual scholarships for graduates from developing and newly industrialised countries to take a development-oriented postgraduate (mostly Master's) course at a state or state-recognised German university, and in exceptional cases a doctoral degree. The award is a monthly payment of EUR 992 for graduates or EUR 1,300 for doctoral candidates (EUR 1,400 from February 2026), plus payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance and a flat-rate travel allowance. Under certain circumstances scholarship holders may additionally receive a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying family members. Scholarships are awarded subject to funding being provided by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).
scholarships.duration: 12 to 42 months (dependent on study programme)
scholarships.application_period: Cycle-based: applicants apply directly to a listed EPOS postgraduate course for the published intake year (the current DAAD programme list is headed 'List of Application Deadlines for Intake 2027/2028'); the course's own committee then nominates candidates, who are invited to upload to the DAAD portal for the final selection.

scholarships.description: MOPGA is a French Government visiting fellowship that pays a monthly allowance to early-career foreign researchers to carry out a 12-month research project in a French host laboratory on climate and environmental themes. Each fellowship covers a monthly allowance of EUR 2,500, a EUR 500 settling-in allowance, and health, civil liability and repatriation coverage. Host laboratories receive no funding under the programme; the money is intended solely to cover the invited researcher's living expenses, and international travel costs are not covered.

scholarships.notes: The fellowship is not renewable and lasts exactly 12 months. International travel costs to France are not covered by the programme; the host laboratory may be able to help but is not funded to do so. scholarships.title: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard Program)
scholarships.name: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship for Research in Japan (Standard Program)
scholarships.deadline: FY2027 2nd recruitment: April 23, 2027, 5 p.m. JST, submission from the Japanese host institution to JSPS. FY2027 1st recruitment closed on August 28, 2026.
scholarships.description: JSPS funds postdoctoral researchers from overseas to conduct collaborative research in Japan under the guidance of a Japanese host researcher at a university or other eligible research institution. Financial support is a maintenance allowance of JPY362,000 per month, a round-trip air ticket, a settling-in allowance of JPY200,000, and overseas travel insurance. A Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research for JSPS Research Fellows can also be applied for through the host institution to cover cooperative research-related expenses. Because this is a research appointment rather than a degree programme, there is no tuition to pay and the award is not presented as tuition funding.
scholarships.duration: 12 to 24 months
scholarships.application_period: Two open calls per year. FY2027 1st: application deadline August 28, 2026 (5 p.m. JST), results late December 2026, arrival windows April 1 - September 30, 2027, 120 fellowships. FY2027 2nd: application deadline April 23, 2027 (5 p.m. JST), results early August 2027, arrival windows September 1 - November 30, 2027, 120 fellowships.

scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship

scholarships.notes: This is NOT an award first-time applicants can enter into. As of the 2026-10-01 verification date the selection, notification and formalisation steps in the published calendar had already run (3-18 September 2026); the published process close date is 30 November 2026, so what remains open is the finalisation of the process and the documentation/disbursement steps, not fresh selection. Applicants who are not existing Secihti national scholarship holders should treat this record as not applicable to them. Tuition is not covered by anything published here, Secihti does not handle immigration procedures for the beneficiary or their economic dependents, support can be cancelled if a restriction or incompatibility is found, names of beneficiaries are published in the Secihti register, and the award can be audited during the award and for 5 years after it ends.

scholarships.title: Convocatoria de Becas OEA - UNIR, EP NEWMAN y UNIR Mexico (Curso Academico 2026, 2a convocatoria)
scholarships.name: Convocatoria de Becas OEA - UNIR, EP NEWMAN y UNIR Mexico (Curso Academico 2026, 2a convocatoria)
scholarships.deadline: 2a convocatoria: 19 de octubre de 2026 (UNIR Maestrías Oficiales y Grados Oficiales, and EP NEWMAN); 26 de octubre de 2026 (UNIR Mexico); 30 de octubre de 2026 (UNIR Formacion Permanente)
scholarships.description: The SG/OAS awards tuition discounts for online postgraduate study with UNIR (Spain), the Escuela de Posgrado Peruana de NEWMAN (Peru) and UNIR Mexico. Up to 885 places are offered, with a 60% discount on total tuition for official master's programmes and official degrees, and a 50% discount for UNIR Formación Permanente programmes, applicable only to the value of the study programme. Admission fees, translation and notarisation, study materials, titulation and degree-awarding procedures, and any other cost not listed are explicitly excluded, and recipients must personally demonstrate the financial capacity to cover the uncovered programme costs, so this is not full funding.
scholarships.duration: UNIR Maestrías Oficiales 12 months; UNIR Grados Oficiales 4 years, with the scholarship applying only to the first teaching year of the degree scholarship; UNIR Formación Permanente 21 to 34 weeks; EP NEWMAN maestrías 12 months; UNIR México maestrías 18 or 24 months
scholarships.application_period: Two calls in the 2026 academic course. 1a convocatoria (Primavera 2026) deadlines ran 16 March to 10 April 2026 and are closed. 2a convocatoria (Otono 2026) is open with deadlines of 19, 26 and 30 October 2026 depending on the institution and programme; selected candidates are announced in November 2026 and programmes start in October/November 2026 depending on the programme.

scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: Citizens or permanent legal residents of OAS Member States other than Nicaragua, from a country other than the one they plan to study in, who have already been admitted to a participating online programme and can fund the non-discounted portion of the tuition themselves.
