Excluded from eligibility: SG/OAS officials, persons under contract by results with the SG/OAS, Permanent Mission staff, and relatives of all of the above. Nicaraguan nationals and permanent legal residents are excluded. Applicants cannot study in their own country of origin. The call states programme costs shown in the document are orientative and may be lower in some countries, and it repeatedly warns that neither the OAS nor the institutions take responsibility for recognition, legalisation, homologation or convalidacion of the resulting title in the applicant's country of country of origin. The scholarship is conditional on academic performance, and it applies only to the value of the study programme. The SG/OAS reserves the right to cancel this announcement at any point in the process. The document's benefits section refers to a 'Responsabilidades del Becario' section on page 27, but the official PDF available at this URL contains only 10 pages, so that section could not be read.

scholarships.title: KAUST Fellowship (Master's, Ph.D. and M.S./Ph.D. Pathway)
scholarships.name: KAUST Fellowship (Master's, Ph.D. and M.S./Ph.D. Pathway)
scholarships.deadline: Fall 2027 Round 2 application deadline 3 January 2027 (Round 2 opened 28 September 2026); decisions released 14 February 2027
scholarships.description: The KAUST Fellowship is awarded automatically to admitted graduate students at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia. The published package covers full tuition and bench fees (stated as worth up to USD $35,000 per year), a monthly stipend (stated as worth USD $20,000 per year for M.S. students and USD $25,000 to $30,000 per year for Ph.D. students depending on qualifications and academic progress), base on-campus accommodation, health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus, and relocation support covering visa, relocation and travel costs. KAUST states the total value of the Fellowship at between $70k and $80k per year depending on the student's situation.
scholarships.duration: M.S. is a 36-credit program expected to be completed in three semesters and one summer session; the M.S./Ph.D. pathway typically takes five to six years
scholarships.application_period: Fall 2027 Round 2 applications open 28 September 2026 and close 3 January 2027; Spring 2027 entry (PhD only) had a Round 1 deadline of 27 September 2026 with decisions on 8 November 2026
scholarships.official_source: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST)
eligibility: ["Bachelors degree in a subject relevant to the program being applied to, from a recognized higher education institution, for entry into Master's programs", "Masters degree in a subject relevant to the program being applied to, from a recognized higher education institution, for entry into Ph.D. programs; Professional Master's degrees are not regarded as directly equivalent and must be declared", "At least 18 years of age on entry", "Minimum permitted GPA of 3.0 on a 4-point scale (or equivalent); typically 90% of admitted applicants have a GPA above 3.3 and 75% above 3.5", "Evidence of proficiency in the English language"]
scholarships.eligibility_summary: Applicants need a bachelor's degree in a relevant subject for Master's entry or a relevant master's degree for Ph.D. entry, be at least 18 years old on entry, hold a minimum 3.0/4.0 GPA, and demonstrate English proficiency.
benefits: ["Eligible students can request a housing upgrade, which will be subject to an additional fee", "Relocation assistance covers each student's initial move to KAUST and their return home upon graduation", "Over 90% of admitted students receive full tuition support, a monthly stipend, housing, medical coverage and relocation assistance"]
coverage: ["Full tuition and bench fee coverage (stated as worth up to USD $35,000 per year)", "Monthly stipend (stated as worth USD $20,000 per year for M.S. students and USD $25,000 to $30,000 for Ph.D. students)", "Base accommodation (shared accommodation for single students; 2-bed accommodation for married students)", "Health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus", "Relocation support covering visa, relocation and travel costs"]

required_documents: ["Official university transcripts (complete academic record showing courses, credits where applicable, grades, final grade or award, and the grading scale used)", "Curriculum Vitae (CV)", "Statement of purpose (approximately 750 words)", "Contact details of 3 referees", "Official English language test score (if available)", "Clear, unobscured copy of the passport page (or national ID card for Saudi applicants)", "Certified English translation of non-English transcripts", "Final official transcript sent directly by the awarding institution before arrival, if admitted"]
scholarships.english_requirement: IELTS 7.0 overall with at least 6.5 in all individual sections (IELTS Online accepted), or TOEFL iBT 5.0 overall with at least 4.5 in all individual sections (KAUST Admissions code 4107; TOEFL Home Edition accepted), or PTE Academic 71 overall with at least 67 in all individual sections, or Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency 185 overall with at least 176 in all individual sections. Scores valid for two years from the test date.
application_method: ["Log into the KAUST application portal and submit the application before the published round deadline", "Upload transcripts, CV, statement of purpose, English test score and passport page as part of the online application", "Enter 3 referees' contact details, which sends reference requests to them automatically", "Respond to any invitation for an online interview with KAUST faculty from your subject area", "Await the decision notification by email within the published notification window for the round"]
scholarships.selection_notes: Five-stage process: submission, Admissions team document review, faculty review committee evaluation and ranking against other applicants with shortlisting for interviews, academic interview and/or test, then decision. Admission review is holistic, considering academic achievements and personal qualities such as motivation and potential impact in the scientific community. All admission decisions are final and will not be reconsidered, and KAUST states it cannot provide individual feedback on specific applications.
scholarships.program_type: University scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: Graduate students in science, engineering, mathematics and related fields who hold a relevant bachelor's (Master's entry) or relevant master's (Ph.D. entry) degree with a minimum GPA of 3.0/4.0 and clear research interests.
scholarships.notes: Relocation assistance is only for each student's initial move to KAUST and their return home upon graduation. Some students with external sponsorship or funding may not be eligible for the KAUST Fellowship. Eligible students who request a housing upgrade pay an additional fee. An English proficiency score is not required if the applicant's degree was completed by in-person study at an accredited institution in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand, or if the applicant previously completed a degree taken at KAUST's campus in Thuwal; distance learning, satellite campuses, joint programs and branch institutions outside those countries do not qualify for the exemption. Applicants may submit without an English score but must meet the minimum before enrolment. Saudi nationals and PhD students scoring IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 4.5 / PTE 64 / Cambridge 176 may be admitted on condition of taking the Academic English Language Communication Course in their first year. KAUST does not accept Medium of Instruction certificates, the Duolingo English Test (except for Visiting Student applicants), TOEFL MyBest superscores, or IELTS One Skill Retake results. If accepted, there is a limited time to respond to secure the place or the decision may be withdrawn.

scholarships.title: MBZUAI Graduate Funding for M.Sc. and Ph.D. Students
scholarships.name: MBZUAI Graduate Funding for M.Sc. and Ph.D. Students
scholarships.deadline: Final application deadline 15 December 2026, 5p.m. GST for all graduate programs except the Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence (28 February 2027 for MAAI); decision notification 31 March 2027; offer response deadline 15 April 2027
scholarships.description: MBZUAI's graduate funding is not a single named scholarship but a University-and-faculty funding model under which funded M.Sc. and Ph.D. students receive free tuition fees, a monthly stipend, one return airfare each year to their home country, health insurance for the approved funding period, and a University-sponsored UAE residence visa and Emirates ID where eligible. Ph.D. Year 1 funding is centrally funded by the University while the student is matched with a faculty advisor, and funding moves to the faculty advisor's funding no later than the start of Year 2. M.Sc. students are fee-paying by default and funding is secured through a faculty advisor-sponsored research or teaching assistantship, or an approved government scholarship for UAE nationals, with merit-based funding considered during the admissions review process. The Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence is a fee-based programme and is not eligible for University or faculty-sponsored funding.
scholarships.application_period: Application portal opened 7 September 2026, 8a.m. GST for all graduate programs except M.Sc. and Ph.D. Computational Biology, which opened 30 September 2026, 8a.m. GST. Portal closes 15 December 2026, 5p.m. GST (MAAI: 28 February 2027).

scholarships.selection_notes: Applicants are evaluated on academic excellence, technical preparation, research potential, and alignment with their chosen program. Admission to MBZUAI is highly competitive with limited places available in each incoming cohort; MBZUAI states that forty-three percent of its incoming graduate students for the 2026-2027 academic year came from the world's top computer science universities. Funding decisions for M.Sc. students depend on whether a faculty advisor sponsors a research or teaching assistantship or, for UAE nationals, an approved government scholarship, with merit-based funding considered during the admissions review process.
scholarships.program_type: University scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: Graduate applicants to MBZUAI's M.Sc. or Ph.D. programmes in computer science, electrical or computer engineering, mathematics, physics or another relevant science or engineering major who hold a STEM degree with a minimum CGPA of 3.0 or 3.5 on a 4.0 scale depending on the programme.
scholarships.notes: M.Sc. students are fee-paying by default and funding is NOT guaranteed for all admitted students; students without a funding source are classified as fee-paying. Ph.D. funding is subject to a confirmed advisor match and satisfactory progress, and transitions to the faculty advisor's funding no later than the start of Year 2. Funded students are expected to maintain an in-person presence on campus throughout their funded period and to obtain approval before being away. Students receiving external scholarships or fellowships must disclose this funding to the University; external funding normally replaces the University stipend rather than being paid in addition to it. The Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence (MAAI) is fee-based at AED 5,000 per credit, 34 credit hours, total tuition AED 170,000 (approx. USD 46,291), and is not eligible for University or faculty-sponsored funding. Cost of Attendance figures for Fall 2027 for unfunded M.Sc. students are currently being finalized and were not published on the page at the time of verification. An English language waiver exists and is described on the MBZUAI admissions FAQ, but the minimum score thresholds are published only on programme-specific pages, so no score is recorded here.

scholarships.title: HBKU Graduate Tuition Waiver and Stipend
scholarships.name: HBKU Graduate Tuition Waiver and Stipend
scholarships.deadline: Online graduate admission application opens to the public 1 October 2026; admission application deadline for international graduate applicants 1 February 2027; admission application deadline for Qatari and resident applicants who wish to apply for funding 15 March 2027
scholarships.description: HBKU graduate scholarships may include a tuition waiver applied to reduce tuition costs and a stipend paid directly to the student, and HBKU states that graduate students receiving a stipend would generally also be provided with a tuition waiver. Tuition waivers are standardised across HBKU and range from 100% for PhD STEM and PhD SHAPE and S.J.D. programmes down to 0% for LL.M. programmes, MS Economics and certificate programmes. Stipends are awarded to selected graduate students, with published monthly and annual rates for Qatari, international and local PhD and Master's students, over durations of 45 months for PhD and 21 months for Master's. Awards depend on the availability of funds, are not guaranteed, and are made on a merit or need basis only.

scholarships.application_period: Online applications open to the public on 1 October 2026 and close on 1 February 2027 for international graduate applicants. Qatari and resident applicants who wish to apply for funding have a later deadline of 15 March 2027. scholarships.notes: Students are responsible for covering the cost of their housing, whether in Qatar Foundation dormitory facilities or external accommodation; this expense is paid from the monthly stipend or personal funds, and HBKU does not provide direct payment for student housing. Meal plans are not separately included; the stipend is a fixed amount meant to cover general living expenses including meals. Stipend awards do not depend on the student's marital status or the number of family dependents. Stipends for local students are limited. Stipends funded from external sources, including research grants, are excluded from the published rates. Self-sponsored graduate students are only eligible for a discounted tuition rate of 2,000 QAR per credit hour based on financial need, and these scholarship guidelines do not apply to students funded by external sources. Receipt of external funding may affect eligibility. Deferral of admission may affect scholarship eligibility. LL.M. programmes, MS Economics and certificate programmes carry a 0% tuition waiver.

scholarships.title: MOFA Scholarship Program
scholarships.name: MOFA Scholarship Program
scholarships.deadline: No application deadline is published on the program page; applications are registered through the online service and the review and final approval process typically takes between 3 to 5 months, with updates communicated by email or SMS
scholarships.description: The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs runs a scholarship programme for Emirati students to study a Bachelor's degree at one of the world's top universities approved by MOFA, specialising in fields that meet the needs of the UAE diplomatic corps. MOFA states in its FAQ that the programme covers all tuition costs in accordance with the programme's policies, and the applicant must already hold an unconditional direct academic acceptance from an approved university indicating the programme start and end dates and the total cost. The programme is not a general study-abroad scholarship: it carries a service obligation, requiring the holder to join the MOFA diplomatic corps for a period equivalent to the number of academic years covered by the scholarship and to join the Anwar Gargash Diplomatic Academy upon graduation.
scholarships.application_period: No published opening or closing dates. Applicants register through the MOFA scholarship service form and are notified of results by email or SMS; amendments after submission are handled through the call centre at +971 80044444.

scholarships.title: Wellcome Early-Career Award
scholarships.name: Wellcome Early-Career Award
scholarships.deadline: There are no deadlines for applications to this scheme. Applications can be submitted at any time. Apply anytime - Applications are accepted year-round.
scholarships.description: The Wellcome Early-Career Award funds early-career researchers from any discipline who are ready to develop their research identity and lead their own independent research programme. The award provides the total cost of the grantholder's salary for the entire grant period, determined by the administering organisation, plus up to £400,000 for research expenses. Certain costs sit outside the £400,000 limit, including overheads, overseas allowances, adjustment support, and the cost of macaques purchased from the MRC Centre for Macaques. Staff salaries are funded up to the equivalent of a 36-month full-time post, and no studentships are provided on this award.
scholarships.duration: Usually 5 years, but may be less for some disciplines, and may only be longer if held on a part-time basis
scholarships.application_period: Rolling, applications accepted year-round. Location eligibility changes on 29 October 2026: from that date applications are only accepted from lead applicants based at eligible administering organisations in the UK and low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia. Applications submitted on or before 28 October 2026 are assessed under the current location eligibility requirements.

scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are assessed through Wellcome's shortlisting Advisory Groups and then peer review. If your application scores in the lowest levels at the shortlisting meeting you will not be permitted to resubmit. If unsuccessful with an Early-Career Award, you may submit one further application for the same project to any Wellcome scheme, provided you still meet the eligibility criteria.
scholarships.program_type: Foundation research grant
scholarships.best_fit: Researchers with a completed PhD (or equivalent) and no more than three years of postdoctoral experience, from any discipline, based at an eligible UK, Republic of Ireland or eligible LMIC organisation, whose work has potential to improve human life, health and wellbeing.
scholarships.notes: Location eligibility is changing on 29 October 2026: from that date Wellcome will only accept applications from lead applicants based at eligible administering organisations in the UK and low- and middle-income countries in Africa, South Asia and South-East Asia, so an application submitted in October 2026 from a Republic of Ireland or a Latin American organisation would not be accepted under the new rule. You can only hold one of these awards and Wellcome does not offer renewals. No studentships are provided on this award. You cannot apply if you hold or have accepted an equivalent award at this career stage, or if you have an existing tenured salaried post for the duration of the award (unless based in a low- or middle-income country). You cannot apply if you intend to carry out activities that involve the transfer of grant funds into mainland China. Total resubmission of the same project is capped at two times across all Wellcome schemes. Overheads are not paid to UK research organisations that already receive core funding for overheads.

scholarships.title: UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers' Fellowships Programme (UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme) - Cycle 2026
scholarships.name: UNESCO/Japan Young Researchers' Fellowships Programme (UNESCO/Keizo Obuchi Research Fellowships Programme) - Cycle 2026
scholarships.deadline: Deadline for candidate submission is now extended to 15 October 2026, midnight Paris time. Letters of nomination and all application documents must reach UNESCO from the National Commissions no later than 15 October 2026, and candidates must submit to their own National Commission at least 2 weeks before the required deadline.
scholarships.description: Under the 2026 cycle UNESCO and the Government of Japan award 10 fellowships to young researchers from Africa, Small Island Developing States, Ukraine and Turkiye to carry out postgraduate research in a Japanese university or research institution. Selected fellows may receive a fellowship grant of up to US$10,000, provided as a lump-sum contribution intended to cover costs directly related to the approved research stay in Japan. The grant may cover international and domestic travel for the approved itinerary, accommodation, medical insurance, personal subsistence in Japan including meals, local transportation and incidental expenses, and other research-related expenses where applicable. It is a research fellowship, not a degree programme: the grant does not cover tuition fees, and the page publishes no award figures beyond the US$10,000 ceiling.
scholarships.duration: No less than 3 months and no more than 9 months
scholarships.application_period: Cycle 2026 call is open (page last updated 28 September 2026, stating the application for the Cycle 2026 is open and the deadline is now extended to 15 October 2026). Because the National Commission needs at least two weeks, the practical national deadline falls around 1 October 2026. Fellowship period in Japan from February 2027 onwards, to be completed no later than December 2027.

scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated by a Selection Committee composed of experts from UNESCO and the Government of Japan in the relevant fields, taking into account the merits of the candidates and the quality, relevance and originality of their proposed research. The final selection decision is made by the Japanese authorities based on the recommendation of the Committee, with due consideration to gender equality and diversity.
scholarships.program_type: UN agency research fellowship (UN and government co-sponsored)
scholarships.best_fit: Researchers aged 40 or under who hold at least a Master's degree (or equivalent) in a field relevant to the proposed research, come from an invited Member State or Associate Member, already have acceptance from an academic supervisor at a Japanese university or research institution, and are applying in one of the five listed research areas on heritage conservation, AI for natural resources and climate action, ethical and human-centred AI, AI for sustainable cities and infrastructure, or AI and education.
scholarships.notes: Only 10 fellowships are awarded in the 2026 cycle, and only applications nominated by your National Commission are accepted, so the national shortlist is the binding gate. The fellowship grant is a lump sum capped at US$10,000, not a line-itemed scholarship, and the cost of the mandatory medical insurance is deducted from the total before disbursement, so the amount actually received is below the ceiling. The grant does NOT cover tuition fees, the purchase of equipment including computers, publication costs, or participation in conferences, unless such participation can be clearly justified as an integral part of the research and makes a direct and significant contribution to the project. Candidates who submit incomplete applications, or who submit the online applications beyond the deadline, will not be considered. The practical deadline is at least two weeks earlier than 15 October 2026 because your National Commission must forward the file.

scholarships.title: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window for Japanese Nationals
scholarships.name: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program (JJ/WBGSP) 2027 - Application Window for Japanese Nationals
scholarships.deadline: The 2027 application window for Japanese nationals will open from February 15 to April 16, 2027. As from February 15, 2027, prospective candidates are invited to express their interest to the JJ/WBGSP Secretariat with an email to scholarshipapplicants@worldbank.org. Winners are informed by mid-July, after the JJ/WBGSC approval. The 2026 application window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026.
scholarships.description: This is the Japanese-nationals track of the Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program, which the World Bank states is fully funded by the Government of Japan. It funds up to two years for a limited number of Japanese mid-career professionals dedicated to the alleviation of poverty and enhanced shared prosperity in developing countries who have been admitted to or are currently enrolled in a master's or PhD programme outside Japan in a development-related field. Benefits include one economy class air travel to the host university and a $600 travel allowance at the start, one economy class return travel and a $600 travel allowance at the end, tuition, basic medical insurance obtainable through the university, and a monthly subsistence allowance to cover all living expenses while on campus. The amount of the monthly subsistence allowance varies by host country and is not published on the page.
scholarships.duration: Up to two years; all JJ/WBGSP scholarships cover the duration of the graduate program or two years, whichever is less
scholarships.application_period: A single application window for the 2027 cycle for Japanese nationals, from February 15 to April 16, 2027. From the opening date, prospective candidates are invited to register interest with the Secretariat by email. Results are communicated by mid-July 2027.
scholarships.official_source: World Bank, Development Economics Vice Presidency, JJ/WBGSP Secretariat (scholarship fully funded by the Government of Japan)
eligibility: ["Be a Japanese national", "On or after the date the call for scholarship applications opens, not be an Executive Director, his/her alternate, and/or staff of any type of appointment (including temporary and consultant) of the World Bank Group (The World Bank, International Development Association, International Finance Corporation, Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, and International Center for Settlements of Investment Disputes), and not be a close relative of any of the aforementioned by blood or adoption (close relative defined as Mother, Father, Sister, Half-sister, Brother, Half-brother, Son, Daughter, Aunt, Uncle, Niece, or Nephew)", "Hold a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) earned at least three years before the date of the Application Deadline", "On or after the date the JJ/WBGSP scholarship application process opens, not be employed (as a staff or any type of employment) by the Government of Japan or its related agencies, including JICA, local governments and the Central Bank", "Have at least 3 years of paid development-related employment acquired since earning a bachelor's degree (or equivalent university degree) and acquired within the past six years from the date of the Application Deadline", "At the time of the application submission, be either admitted unconditionally (except for financing) or currently enrolled full-time in a graduate program outside of Japan in an area of study related to development, or be currently employed full-time in development-related work pertaining directly to developing countries"]

scholarships.selection_notes: Two qualified assessors independently review each eligible application and score it on a scale of 1 to 10 on four factors: Quality of Academic Experience and Recommendation (20% weight), Quality of Professional Recommendations (20% weight), Quality of Professional Experience (20%), and Commitment to International Development Career (40% weight). The Secretariat uses the average score of the two assessors plus maintaining a reasonable distribution of awards across gender and giving scholarships to those applicants who, other things being equal, have limited access to financial resources for graduate studies abroad. Finalists are presented to the JJ/WBG Steering Committee, composed of members of the World Bank Board of Directors and World Bank management, for approval.
scholarships.program_type: Development bank scholarship (bilateral government-funded graduate scholarship)
scholarships.best_fit: Japanese nationals with a bachelor's degree earned at least three years before the deadline and at least three years of paid development-related employment acquired within the past six years, who are admitted unconditionally (except financing) to, or already enrolled full-time in, a development-related master's or PhD programme outside Japan.
scholarships.notes: The scholarship does NOT cover visa application costs, expenses to bring and/or support family members, extra-curricular courses or training, courses below the minimum credits required for the degree, language training not provided by the graduate program, additional travel during the study program, research or supplementary educational materials, field trips, workshops, seminars or internships, educational equipment such as computers, and the resident permit fee. The scholarship may only supplement, and does not duplicate, any other source of financial support; if you are notified of being a semi-finalist or are awarded, you must inform and document other scholarship funds to the Secretariat. After earning their degree, Japanese national scholars are expected to advance their professional career with a keen focus on the alleviation of poverty and enhanced shared prosperity in developing countries. The air travel benefit at the end of the scholarship period is conditional on having completed all requirements to earn the graduate degree, and the return ticket is to Japan or to a developing country where the scholar has secured employment. The published US$600 is a per-trip travel allowance, not the award total. The 2026 window for Japanese nationals closed on Friday 17 April 2026, so only the 2027 window is live.

scholarships.title: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships (ESKAS)
scholarships.name: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships (ESKAS)
scholarships.deadline: Applications are open from 20 August 2026. Applications are submitted to the applicant's Swiss diplomatic representation, and the deadline is set country by country: information on application deadlines and scholarship opportunities by country of origin is published by the Federal Commission in August each year.
scholarships.description: The Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships are awarded annually by the Swiss Confederation to encourage international exchange and research cooperation between Switzerland and more than 180 other countries. Recipients are selected by the Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS, also known as ESKAS), an independent decentralised federal body that is not bound by directives. The programme has two components: research scholarships for talented early career researchers from abroad who have already completed a Master's degree, and art scholarships for students from a limited number of countries wishing to pursue an initial Master's degree in an artistic field in Switzerland. Applicants are aged 35 or less and the scholarship pays CHF 2,450 per month.
scholarships.duration: Research fellowships: maximum 12 months (minimum 6 months), no extension possible, start 1 September 2027. PhD scholarships: 12 months, renewable twice for up to 36 months subject to academic progress, start 1 September 2027.
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle. Applications open on 20 August 2026, country-specific deadlines apply between August and December 2026, and the Federal Commission announces its award decisions by the end of May at the latest for the following academic year.
scholarships.official_source: State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI) - Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS / ESKAS), Switzerland

scholarships.eligibility_summary: Open to applicants from 183 countries who are aged 35 or less and already hold a Master's degree or equivalent. Applicants must not have been living, studying or working in Switzerland for more than 13 months before the scholarship start, must not already have held a Swiss Government Excellence Scholarship, and every research scholarship application must be backed by an academic supervisor at a Swiss higher education institution.

scholarships.selection_notes: Applications are submitted to the applicant's Swiss diplomatic representation. The Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students assesses applications against three criteria: candidate profile, quality of the research project or artistic work, and synergies and potential for future research cooperation. Art scholarships are reviewed in consultation with the Federal Office of Culture.
scholarships.program_type: Government research scholarship (Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students, FCS/ESKAS)
scholarships.notes: Host institutions for research scholarships are Swiss cantonal universities, universities of applied sciences, ETH Zurich or EPFL, and the four research institutes within the ETH Domain (PSI, WSL, Empa, Eawag). Official phishing warning: the State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation warns against fake Swiss Government scholarship offers sent by e-mail or published on social media, and the application for a Swiss Government Scholarship is free of charge.

scholarships.title: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP)
scholarships.name: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP)
scholarships.deadline: There is no central student deadline. Participants apply through their home institution's International Relations Office and the deadline is set by that institution. For institutions, accreditation and funding applications can be submitted annually at the beginning of March and the funding period starts on 1 June of the year of application. Movetia currently states that the next application deadline is spring 2027, likely under Erasmus+.
scholarships.description: The Swiss-European Mobility Programme is Switzerland's national mobility programme for higher education and forms part of the Swiss solution to the EU's Erasmus+ programme. Funded by SERI and implemented by the Swiss agency Movetia, it enables officially accredited Swiss higher education institutions and colleges of higher education to send their students and staff abroad (outgoing) and to host students and staff from abroad (incoming). Students, including PhD students, spend one or two semesters at a partner higher education institution and keep their enrolment at home, earning ECTS credits; they do not pay study fees abroad and receive financial support for travelling and accommodation.
scholarships.duration: 2 to 12 months per mobility (a stay must last between 60 days and 12 months); one or two semesters for study mobility
scholarships.application_period: Annual institutional cycle: applications from accredited institutions each March, funding period from 1 June. Student-level applications run year-round through the home institution's own deadlines. Movetia expects the next call to be launched under Erasmus+ following Switzerland's planned association from 2027.
scholarships.official_source: State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI), Switzerland - implemented by Movetia
eligibility: ["Enrolled at a higher education institution (university, university of applied sciences, university of teacher education) or college of higher education in Switzerland or abroad; PhD students included", "Stay lasting between 60 days and 12 months", "Interinstitutional agreement between the home and host institutions", "Follow courses at the host institution that count towards the student's degree (ECTS credits or equivalent)", "For funding applicants: an officially recognised Swiss higher education institution, or a college of higher education with federally recognised courses at higher education level", "Accreditation under the SEMP Charter or a European Charter for Higher Education (ECHE); partner institutions abroad must hold an ECHE or formally accept the SEMP quality principles"]
scholarships.eligibility_summary: Participants must be enrolled at a higher education institution (university, university of applied sciences, university of teacher education) or a college of higher education in Switzerland or abroad, their stay must last between 60 days and 12 months, the home and host institutions must have an interinstitutional agreement, and they must follow courses at the host institution that count towards their degree. Funding applicants are officially recognised Swiss higher education institutions, or colleges of higher education with federally recognised courses, holding a SEMP Charter or an ECHE.

required_documents: ["Learning agreement for study mobility, validated in advance by the sending and receiving institutions and the participant", "Mobility agreement for staff mobility, or Grant Agreement for staff mobility, finalised before the mobility starts", "Declaration of Honour (student mobility), prepared and finalised by the Swiss institution before the mobility period", "Evidence of the interinstitutional agreement between home and host institutions", "Completed application for the special-needs grant via the International Relations Office, ideally two months before the mobility starts and in any case before departure"]
scholarships.selection_notes: Participants are selected by their home institution through fair and transparent selection procedures and criteria; each institution sets its own participation criteria, and some award SEMP grants only for mobilities within Europe. Institutions may also apply internal restrictions, for example no mobility to the applicant's country of origin for foreign nationals, language skills, or mobility duration.
scholarships.program_type: Government mobility programme (higher education), Swiss solution to Erasmus+
scholarships.notes: SEMP funds four mobility types under one annual application: semesters abroad for students (Student Mobility for Studies), traineeships abroad for students (Student Mobility for Traineeships), training activities for staff in higher education, and teaching assignments for staff in higher education. Grants are always paid out by the Swiss home or host institution, never directly to the participant. In 2024 the Swiss solution enabled more than 17,000 participants from Switzerland and Europe to supplement their education or training with a stay abroad.

scholarships.title: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP) - Incoming Mobility to Switzerland
scholarships.name: Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP) - Incoming Mobility to Switzerland
scholarships.deadline: There is no central deadline for individual students: applications are handled by the international relations office of the Swiss host institution, which sets its own dates. At institutional level, accreditation and funding applications go to Movetia annually in early March for a funding period starting 1 June. Movetia currently states that the next application deadline is spring 2027, likely under Erasmus+.
scholarships.description: Incoming mobility to Switzerland is funded under the Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP), the higher education part of the Swiss Programme for Erasmus+ that Switzerland operates in place of Erasmus+ association. Students from abroad, including PhD students, can spend one or two semesters at a Swiss university or college of higher education, or do a traineeship in Switzerland, while remaining enrolled at their home institution and earning ECTS credits. They do not pay study fees at the Swiss host institution and receive a financial contribution towards travel and accommodation. Applications are coordinated by the international relations office of the Swiss host institution, which is the only party that can receive and pay out the grant.
scholarships.duration: 2 to 12 months per mobility (minimum 60 days); one or two semesters for study mobility; traineeships of at least 60 days
scholarships.application_period: Annual institutional cycle with applications each March and a funding period from 1 June; student-level applications run through the Swiss host institution's own deadlines. Movetia expects the next call to be launched under Erasmus+ following Switzerland's planned participation from 2027.
scholarships.official_source: Movetia (Swiss agency for exchange and mobility), implementing the Swiss Programme for Erasmus+ on behalf of SERI

Students from abroad apply for the grant directly with the Swiss higher education institution where they plan to study or train; if the placement is at a Swiss company or NGO, they must still find a Swiss institution willing to coordinate the application and pay out the grant.

scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is carried out by the home institution abroad (which runs the application and nominates the student) and then by the Swiss host institution, which coordinates the SEMP application and pays out the grant. Swiss SEMP institutions apply their own transparent selection criteria and may restrict SEMP grants to certain destinations.
scholarships.program_type: Government mobility programme (higher education), Swiss solution to Erasmus+ - incoming mobility
scholarships.notes: Switzerland is not associated to the Erasmus+ 2021-2027 programme; the funding for incoming mobility comes from the Swiss solution to Erasmus+, administered by Movetia on behalf of SERI. The European Union Programme Agreement was signed on 10 November 2025 and the Federal Council plans to request funding for association to Erasmus+ in 2027, so the programme framework may change.

scholarships.title: Türkiye Bursları (Türkiye Scholarships) - Turkish Government Scholarship
scholarships.name: Türkiye Bursları (Türkiye Scholarships) - Turkish Government Scholarship
scholarships.deadline: Applications for the full-time programmes (associate, bachelor's, master's, PhD and art scholarships) are received through the Türkiye Scholarships Application System (TBBS) between 10 January and 20 February, which is the application period every year. Research Scholarships have different application periods, announced regularly on the official website. For the 2026 cycle the window was 10 January to 20 February 2026, so the next cycle is expected in the same annual window.
scholarships.description: Türkiye Bursları is the Republic of Türkiye's government-funded, competitive scholarship programme for international students, run under the coordination of the Presidency of Turks Abroad and Relatives of Overseas Citizens (YTB). It funds associate, bachelor's, master's, PhD and research places at the most prestigious Turkish universities and is distinctive in providing university and department placement rather than a fellowship to be spent at a chosen institution. The package covers tuition, a monthly stipend, health insurance, accommodation, a one-year Turkish language course, a once-off return flight ticket and free academic and cultural programmes. Applications are submitted online, free of charge, through the Türkiye Scholarships Application System (TBBS).
scholarships.duration: One year of free Turkish language education before or alongside the degree programme; associate degree is a two-year programme, with bachelor's, master's and PhD programmes of standard length. Research Scholarships have their own application periods.
scholarships.application_period: One annual period each year: 10 January to 20 February for international applicants, for associate, bachelor's, master's and doctoral scholarships. Research Scholarships run on separate, individually announced periods.
scholarships.official_source: Presidency of Turks Abroad and Relatives of Overseas Citizens (YTB) - Türkiye Scholarships

scholarships.notes: The Art Scholarship Programme funds undergraduate, graduate and PhD study in performing arts, music and fine arts at Ankara Music and Fine Arts University, Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli University and İstanbul Technical University. scholarships.title: Invest Your Talent in Italy (IYT) — MAECI / ICE / Uni-Italia scholarship programme
scholarships.name: Invest Your Talent in Italy (IYT) — MAECI / ICE / Uni-Italia scholarship programme
scholarships.deadline: The 11th edition (academic year 2026-2027) call was open from 20 April 2026 and closed at 6:00pm Italian time on 11 May 2026. The official programme site announces that the new call opens in 2027 (the 12th edition).
scholarships.description: Invest Your Talent in Italy is a MAECI scholarship programme run with the ICE Agency and Uni-Italia that pays a nine-month scholarship to foreign students from 22 partner countries to attend a Master's or Postgraduate course at a participating Italian university, combined with a compulsory internship at an Italian company or professional association. Courses are taught entirely in English, and the programme includes study of Italian language and culture plus a mandatory gender-equality and anti-gender-violence seminar or module. The winner receives an annual scholarship of EUR 10,800, paid quarterly into an Italian bank account in the holder's name, and is exempt from enrolment fees and university contributions, but must still pay the regional right-to-education tax, stamp duty, accident and civil liability insurance and health insurance. The scholarship explicitly does not cover travel expenses and does not include accommodation, and the recipient must independently arrange health insurance.
scholarships.duration: 9 months of study, starting 1 October 2026 for the 2026-2027 academic year
scholarships.application_period: The 11th edition ran 20 April 2026 to 11 May 2026 at 6:00pm Italian time and is closed, with 1634 applications received, 982 eligible and 211 scholarships awarded. The official site carries the banner 'NEW APPLICATION OPENS 2027!' / 'IL NUOVO BANDO APRE NEL 2027!', so the next edition is announced but no opening date, closing date or application window has been published.

scholarships.english_requirement: Courses are taught entirely in English. Applicants must attach certification of English language proficiency from level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference (Cambridge, IELTS, TOEFL iBT, ISE Digital – Trinity College, ISE Paper – Trinity College, PTE, Linguaskill, ESOL, TOEIC covering listening, reading, speaking, writing). Candidates who obtained a university degree at the end of a degree course taught in English may submit a university certificate attesting that English was the language of instruction, accepted as proof of level C1. A separate requirement exists for Italian: certification issued by the institution where the training was undertaken, or a declaration of commitment to attend a classroom or self-study Italian course before departure; Italian certification is not mandatory but contributes to the evaluation score.

scholarships.selection_notes: Examination and evaluation of applications is carried out by the Technical Committee of the IYT Program (MAECI, ICE and Uni-Italia), which may use an ad hoc commission. Scholarships are allocated in quotas defined for each country and awarded on the basis of a comparative evaluation of the applications against the requirements in Articles 3 and 5 of the call. The Design Scholarship quota is allocated using specially drawn-up rankings that take into account the order of preference for courses given by the student, as is the Borse Ateneo quota.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: Students aged 25 or under (born on or after 1 January 2000) who hold a qualification valid for enrolment in a participating Italian Master's or Postgraduate course, permanently resident in one of the 22 listed partner countries, and not already studying at or graduated from an Italian university.
scholarships.notes: Renewable: IYT scholarship holders may apply to continue the second year of the Master's by uploading a university certificate of exams taken (CFU), a certificate of attendance for an Italian language course (and, for the 11th edition holders, an internship project) by 20 July 2027; renewal and fee exemption for the second year are conditional on achieving 30 credits by 20 July 2027 and verified regular attendance of the university's Italian language course. All scholarship recipients must complete the paperwork for the start of their internship by 20 January 2027. Incompatible: the IYT scholarship cannot be combined with any other scholarship or financial benefit from the Italian Government or any public institution (e.g. Erasmus+), including scholarships offered by Italian regions under regional education programmes. Must fund separately: the scholarship does not cover travel expenses and does not include accommodation, and the recipient must independently arrange health insurance covering illness and accidents in Italy. Not covered even after fee waiver: regional tax for the Right to Education, stamp duty, accident and/or civil liability insurance costs, and health insurance. Restrictions on mobility: the scholarship only covers attendance at courses in Italy. Award is conditional on the positive outcome of the Court of Auditors legality review.

scholarships.title: ARES Scholarships - Bourses de formations internationales (scholarships for study in Belgium)
scholarships.name: ARES Scholarships - Bourses de formations internationales (scholarships for study in Belgium)
scholarships.deadline: For the 2027-2028 call, applications had to be submitted through the GIRAF platform by Friday 18 September 2026 at 12h (Belgian time). The call is now closed and the next call is announced for August 2027.
scholarships.description: ARES, the Walloon agency for international cooperation and education, awards scholarships so that professionals from its partner countries can study in Wallonia, in institutions of the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles. The 'bourses de formations internationales' cover a one-year bachelor of specialisation (bachelier de spécialisation), a specialised master's degree (master de spécialisation) or a short continuing-education course of up to six months, with study programmes that address development-related issues. The scholarship is aimed at people who are permanent residents and working in one of ARES's partner countries and who already hold a higher education diploma. For the 2026-2027 call 200 scholarships were available; for 2027-2028 the call offered one bachelor of specialisation, eight specialised master's degrees and one continuing-education certificate. Applications are submitted through the GIRAF platform and the selection is run by a jury for each programme.
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle: the call opens in early August and applications close in mid-September, with preselection and selection running from October to May and results in June
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship of the Walloon government, administered by ARES
scholarships.notes: Applying to an ARES scholarship is free of charge: "Postuler à une bourse de l'ARES est gratuit. L'ARES ne demande donc aucun frais à quelque étape du processus de candidature ou de sélection que ce soit." ARES warns against anyone claiming to act for ARES and requesting payment by email; report such cases to bourses-cooperation@ares-ac.be. Award holders are expected to return to their country of origin or another country and to apply the training acquired in Belgium to development, for example through a work contract or a formal commitment, with a multiplier effect. ARES guarantees the possibility of deferring the scholarship in case of pregnancy.

scholarships.title: Boren Scholarships and Fellowships (National Security Education Program)
scholarships.name: Boren Scholarships and Fellowships (National Security Education Program)
scholarships.deadline: National deadlines for the 2027 Boren Awards: Boren Fellowships January 20, 2027; Boren Scholarships January 27, 2027. 2027-28 Boren Awards funding may be applied to programs starting as early as June 2027 or as late as March 1, 2028. Applicants are notified of selection in mid-to-late April.
scholarships.description: The National Security Education Program awards Boren Scholarships and Fellowships to U.S. undergraduate and graduate students committed to long-term overseas study and to federal service. Boren Scholarships fund study abroad by U.S. undergraduates and Boren Fellowships fund research and language study proposals by U.S. graduate students, in world regions critical to U.S. interests. Maximum awards are determined by duration abroad: $25,000 for 25-52 weeks (preferred), $12,500 for 12-24 weeks, and $8,000 for 8-11 weeks for STEM majors under the Scholarships programme. There are no minimum language requirements except French and Spanish, which require intermediate high [1+] proficiency for advanced study programs in Africa and Latin America. The Boren Awards are an initiative of the Defense Language and National Security Education Office.
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle tied to the academic year. 2027-28 funding may be applied to programs starting as early as June 2027 or as late as March 1, 2028.

scholarships.title: Kyushu University Friendship Scholarship
scholarships.name: Kyushu University Friendship Scholarship
scholarships.degree: Undergraduate, Master's, PhD (exchange, special auditing, special research or double degree enrolment at Kyushu University)
scholarships.degree_levels: Undergraduate, Master's, PhD (exchange, special auditing, special research or double degree enrolment at Kyushu University)
scholarships.deadline: No exact date is published. There are two recruitment periods in each fiscal year: Period I is recruited around February for grantees starting between April and September, and Period II is recruited around May for grantees starting between October and March. Applications are made through the applicant's prospective host department at Kyushu University, so the department sets its own internal date within the period.
scholarships.description: Kyushu University's own support programme for privately financed international students who come to Kyushu University on exchange, special auditing, special research or double degree status and who cannot afford to study in Japan solely at their own expense. It pays a monthly stipend of JPY 80,000, and the total of all scholarships held by the grantee may not exceed that amount. Applicants apply through their prospective host department at Kyushu University, not directly to the university centre. There are two recruitment periods per fiscal year: Period I around February for students who will study from April to September, and Period II around May for students who will study from October to March. The period of stay must be 3 months, 5 months (one semester) or 11 months (two semesters).
scholarships.duration: 3 months, 5 months (one semester) or 11 months (two semesters) at Kyushu University; the period of stay must begin within the academic year
scholarships.application_period: Two recruitment periods a year. Period I: around February, for study starting between April and September. Period II: around May, for study starting between October and the following March.

scholarships.title: Programa de Becas de Cooperación Sur Sur - República de Chile, Convocatoria Año 2027 (AGCID)
scholarships.name: Programa de Becas de Cooperación Sur Sur - República de Chile, Convocatoria Año 2027 (AGCID)
scholarships.description: AGCID, Chile's international cooperation agency, runs a South-South cooperation scholarship programme under which professionals from Latin America and the Caribbean study a master's degree at accredited Chilean universities with a high level of excellence. The 2027 call is aimed at degree-holding professionals working in government programmes or ministries and public services, as well as university academic staff, teachers and researchers, and also at professionals working in civil society across the invited countries. Applications go through the national focal point in each candidate's country, and the scholarship takes place in person in Chile. The official Panamanian focal-point page for this call states a closing date of 30 October 2026.
scholarships.application_period: Applications are submitted through each country's national focal point; the official IFARHU page for this call gives a closing date of 30 October 2026. Individual countries set earlier national deadlines, so the focal point in your own country governs.

scholarships.eligibility_summary: Degree-holding professionals from the invited Latin American and Caribbean countries who work in government programmes or public services, or are academics, teachers or researchers at recognised universities, or work in civil society, and who have been admitted to an eligible Chilean master's programme.

scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship
scholarships.best_fit: A mid-career professional from an invited Latin American or Caribbean country working in the public sector, at a university, or in civil society, who already holds unconditional admission to an accredited Chilean master's programme listed in the call's annex.
scholarships.notes: The programme is organised by AGCID under South-South cooperation and each invited country runs its own national selection through its focal point, so deadlines differ by country and the national window closes before the international one. AGCID's own 'Ofertas Vigentes' page loads its list of scholarships with JavaScript and did not render any entries when read in a browser on 2026-10-04, so the call's own PDF convocatoria could not be read as text; the priority thematic areas, the maximum 24-month duration, the 1 March to 30 September 2027 start window and the benefit breakdown sit in that PDF and are recorded as unverified rather than asserted here.

scholarships.title: PEC-PG - Brazilian Program for Exchange Students, Postgraduate Level (PEC-PG 2027)
scholarships.name: PEC-PG - Brazilian Program for Exchange Students, Postgraduate Level (PEC-PG 2027)
scholarships.description: PEC-PG is the Brazilian postgraduate exchange programme funded by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and administered through CNPq, open to nationals of participating countries who are not Brazilian and do not hold Brazilian permanent residence. For the 2027 cycle the Call Notice was released on 29 June 2026 and CNPq publishes the list of eligible Brazilian institutions in December 2026, after which each institution runs its own candidate selection. Scholarships are paid from March 2027 to March 2028 at R$ 2,100 per month for a master's and R$ 3,100 per month for a doctorate, with access to the SUS public health system and possible MRE-funded return travel aid.
scholarships.duration: 24 months for a master's; 48 months for a doctorate
scholarships.application_period: Call Notice released 29 June 2026; list of eligible institutions published December 2026; institution-level candidate selection runs from December 2026; scholarships paid March 2027 to March 2028
scholarships.official_source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Brazil (Itamaraty) with Conselho Nacional de Desenvolvimento Cientifico e Tecnologico (CNPq)
eligibility: ["Be a national of one of the countries participating in the PEC-PG programme", "Live in one of the countries participating in the programme", "Not have Brazilian nationality, including dual Brazilian nationality or the right to it", "Not hold a permanent residence permit for Brazil", "Have completed a higher education course equivalent to an undergraduate degree (graduacao)", "Not be taking in Brazil another course at the same level as the intended one", "Have a clean record, with no debts to CAPES or the Brazilian government", "Be able to start the course within the postgraduate programme's deadline", "Have an updated CV on the Lattes platform", "Not hold a doctorate degree", "Have spent at least two years in their country after obtaining a Brazilian diploma or a master's degree funded by a Brazilian funding agency, where applicable", "For a master's: not have held a full or sandwich master's scholarship from a Brazilian federal public entity", "For a doctorate: not have held a full or sandwich doctoral scholarship from a Brazilian federal public entity", "Meet the specific requirements of the chosen graduate programme (PPG), including language requirements"]
scholarships.eligibility_summary: Nationals and residents of countries participating in the PEC-PG programme, without Brazilian nationality (including dual nationality or a right to it) and without Brazilian permanent residence, holding a completed higher education course equivalent to a bachelor's degree, with an updated Lattes CV, and with no debts to CAPES or the Brazilian government.
benefits: ["Monthly stipend: R$ 2,100 for Master's degree, R$ 3,100 for Doctorate degree", "Access to the SUS public health system throughout Brazil without discrimination based on nationality or immigration status", "Financial aid to return to the country of origin, paid by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs depending on budgetary availability, with amounts set in the table annexed to MRE Ordinance No. 572/2024"]
coverage: ["Monthly scholarship stipend of R$ 2,100 (master's, 24 months) or R$ 3,100 (doctorate, 48 months)", "Access to the Brazilian public health system (SUS) on the same terms as Brazilian citizens", "Possible return-to-country-of-origin travel aid paid by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, subject to budget availability"]
requirements: ["Application is free of charge", "Wait for CNPq to publish the list of eligible institutions in December 2026", "Contact the institutions of interest and apply through their own selection process", "Submit the documents required by the chosen institution and by the Call Notice", "Comply with the Call Notice and the specific requirements of the graduate programme"]
documents: ["Digital copy of the personal information page of your passport", "Proof of CPF (Brazilian Individual Taxpayer Registry) registration status", "Proof of residence abroad, such as a water or electricity bill", "Valid ORCID number", "Research project in Portuguese, Spanish or English", "Statement of employment, where applicable, issued by the employer, confirming the stay in Brazil will not exceed the period allowed for the thesis or dissertation defence"]
required_documents: ["Digital copy of the personal information page of your passport", "Proof of CPF (Brazilian Individual Taxpayer Registry) registration status", "Proof of residence abroad, such as a water or electricity bill", "Valid ORCID number", "Research project in Portuguese, Spanish or English", "Statement of employment, where applicable, issued by the employer, confirming the stay in Brazil will not exceed the period allowed for the thesis or dissertation defence"]
scholarships.english_requirement: No general English requirement is published; language requirements are set by each specific graduate programme (PPG) the applicant chooses.
application_method: ["From December 2026, consult the CNPq list of eligible higher education and science and technology institutions", "Check the graduate programmes (PPGs) included and their specific requirements", "Contact the chosen institution and apply directly to its PEC-PG selection process", "Await the institution's result and prepare to start activities in Brazil between March 2027 and March 2028"]
scholarships.selection_notes: Selection is two-stage: CNPq first approves institutions, then each institution selects and implements candidates. Applicants are assessed only by the receiving institution, not by CNPq or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the Ministry states it does not receive applications for PEC-PG.
scholarships.program_type: Government scholarship (Brazilian postgraduate exchange programme run by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs with CNPq)
scholarships.best_fit: Master's and doctoral students from Latin American and other participating countries without Brazilian nationality or residence who want to study at a Brazilian postgraduate programme and can wait for institution-level selection from December 2026.
scholarships.notes: Regional and multi-country: eligibility is defined by nationality and residence in any country participating in the programme rather than by a single host or home country. The award is a stipend, not a tuition waiver, so fully_funded is false; institutional eligibility may carry its own funding rules. Schedule dates are published as indicative and the page warns they may change.

scholarships.program_type: University merit and socioeconomic need scholarship

scholarships.description: The Beca al Talento Académico Internacional is the Tecnológico de Monterrey scholarship for international applicants, reserved for candidates coming from secondary schools in a named group of Latin American and Caribbean countries. scholarships.title: Becas de apoyo a la investigacion del Instituto Riva-Aguero 2027
scholarships.name: Becas de apoyo a la investigacion del Instituto Riva-Aguero 2027
scholarships.deadline: Project submissions close 16 October 2026
scholarships.description: The Directorate of the Instituto Riva-Aguero, a research institute of the Pontificia Universidad Catolica del Peru, has published its 2027 research support call. Two modalities are offered: an individual research grant of PEN 10,000 and a group research grant of PEN 20,000, each for a maximum of ten months between 2 November 2026 and 3 September 2027. Project topics must fall within the institute's five research lines, covering Peruvian and Latin American history, the state and social processes, literature, art and cultural practices, tangible and intangible heritage, and philosophy, science and education in Peru. Winners must publish their results in a Scopus or Web of Science indexed journal or in an academic-press book, with their affiliation to the Instituto Riva-Aguero stated explicitly, and the individual modality requires the holder to supervise an undergraduate student assistant, which the institute presents as a way of promoting young researchers.
scholarships.duration: Maximum 10 months, from 2 November 2026 to 3 September 2027

For the group modality, any study or research group registered and approved by the institute's council is eligible.
benefits: ["Individual research grant of PEN 10,000", "Group research grant of PEN 20,000 for registered and approved research groups", "Funding period of up to 10 months, 2 November 2026 to 3 September 2027", "Possible complementary funding from PUCP or external sources, in cash or in documentary resources for the research"]

scholarships.selection_notes: Selection of winning projects is carried out by a committee made up of the institute's director or research coordinator, a representative of the PUCP Vice-Rectorate of Research and an institute member. The committee may call on additional members of the institute's governing council and national or international experts on the topics involved. Scoring criteria referenced in the bases include relevance, methodological and theoretical consistency, clarity of objectives, feasibility of the timeline, and expected results.

scholarships.description: The scholarship is set up and funded by the International School of Medicine of Zhejiang University and is open only to doctoral candidates in medical programmes at that school, whose teaching base is in Yiwu, in central Zhejiang Province. The official page sets out two full-scholarship tiers (A and B): both exempt tuition and provide free on-campus accommodation and comprehensive medical insurance for international students, with a monthly living allowance of RMB 7,000 under tier A and RMB 3,500 under tier B. Applicants apply by emailing the school's scholarship application form and uploading the same form into the Zhejiang University international student application system. The page is a standing terms document; the application deadline it currently publishes is 28 February for the cycle whose results are read out in late July or early August.
scholarships.duration: The scholarship period matches the length of the doctoral programme, stated as 3-4 years for doctoral study with the exact period as specified in the admission notice
scholarships.application_period: Annual cycle tied to the Zhejiang University international doctoral intake. scholarships.selection_notes: The university states that applicants are selected on the basis of research ability, academic performance, language level and video interview performance (学校将根据申请人的研究能力、学业成绩、语言水平和视频面试情况等因素综合考虑择优录取). No minimum English test score is published on the scholarship page; it refers applicants to the Zhejiang University international student (doctoral) admission guide for admission-level language requirements. Recipients are subject to an annual scholarship review, and scholarship status can be suspended or cancelled if the review is failed. If a holder suspends studies for serious illness they must return home at their own travel cost; with university approval the scholarship entitlement can be retained for up to one year but the living allowance stops during the suspension, and suspension for other reasons forfeits the entitlement. The living allowance is paid monthly from the date of enrolment: a full month if registered on or before the 15th, half a month if after the 15th; it continues over official holidays and can be paid retrospectively on return, but is suspended for that month if a holder is absent from registration or leaves without leave or is absent from class for more than two weeks for non-health reasons.

scholarships.notes: This is a school-level award created and funded by the International School of Medicine itself (本奖学金项目由浙江大学"一带一路"国际医学院设立), distinct from the Chinese Government Scholarship programmes that the same university administers. The page states that final interpretation rests with the International School of Medicine and the ZJU International Education College.

scholarships.description: Fu Jen Catholic University's International Student Admissions Office publishes a set of Fu Jen-funded scholarships for newly admitted international students. The scholarship is requested inside the admission application itself rather than through a separate form. Applications for Spring 2027 are open until 14 October 2026, and the first round for Fall 2027 opens on 15 October 2026.

The Fall 2027 first round opens on 15 October 2026 at 13:00 and closes on 4 December 2026 at 23:59, with review from 5 to 21 December 2026 and results on 8 January 2027; a Fall 2027 second round runs 1 March 2027 13:00 to 15 May 2027 23:59 with results on 9 July 2027.

scholarships.description: The Petroleum Technology Development Fund is a Nigerian federal government agency mandated with developing indigenous human capacity and petroleum technology for the oil and gas industry. The Fund invites applications from qualified Nigerians for its 2026/27 Undergraduate, Master's and PhD scholarships, restricted to Nigerian public universities and to a published list of sponsored courses grouped into engineering, science, environmental science, renewable energy and management. Undergraduate applicants must already be at 200 level in a Nigerian public university and must hold a valid admission letter; MSc and PhD applicants must hold full-time admission letters and a minimum Second Class Lower (2:2) in an oil and gas-related field. Selection is merit-driven and explicitly weighted toward equitable representation of the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.
scholarships.duration: Not published as a fixed award term; the scheme covers Undergraduate, Master's and PhD awards within Nigerian public universities, with undergraduate eligibility anchored to study at 200 level
scholarships.application_period: 27 April 2026 to 5 June 2026 for the 2026/27 cycle. No 2027/28 window is published as of 2026-10-04; PTDF publishes an annual cycle under the same scheme.
scholarships.official_source: Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF), a Federal Government of Nigeria agency

scholarships.eligibility_summary: Nigerian citizens in public universities, at 200 level for undergraduate applicants, with a valid admission letter, at least five WAEC/SSCE/NECO credits including English and Mathematics, and a minimum CGPA of 2.4 of 5.0 for undergraduates or Second Class Lower for postgraduates, in a sponsored oil and gas, energy or management-related course. A National Identity Number is mandatory before applying, and all applicants must submit a certificate of indigeneship.

scholarships.selection_notes: The scholarship is described as highly competitive and merit-driven. Undergraduate final selection is based on grades on transcripts, which must be signed and stamped by the HOD, Exams Officer or other authorised university personnel. A selection panel assesses postgraduate applications on academic merit as evidenced by quality of degrees, full academic transcripts, other professional qualifications and relevant publications; membership of professional bodies; the viability of the study or research plan for PhD applicants; the statement of purpose for undergraduate and MSc applicants; and the research proposal for PhD applicants. Selection is based on equitable representation of the 36 states of the Federation and the Federal Capital Territory, except where a state does not have the requisite number of candidates to fill its allotted slots.

scholarships.best_fit: Nigerian public-university students at 200 level, or MSc/PhD applicants with a 2:2 or better in an oil and gas, energy or management-related discipline, pursuing one of the Fund's named sponsored courses and prepared to serve the oil and gas sector and national development.
scholarships.notes: The 2026/27 window closed on 5 June 2026, so this record is status upcoming/recurring rather than open, and deadline_date is null because no 2027/28 window is published. The published guidelines do not itemise what the scholarship pays for, so tuition_coverage is recorded as false and funding_amount as null rather than assumed. Part-time admission is not considered in any category, and previous PTDF scholarship holders cannot apply for the same or a lower degree category. Note also that certificate of indigeneship and a state-level quota operate together, which makes the geographic distribution of candidates a practical constraint on who can be shortlisted.

scholarships.description: The Government of Brunei Darussalam Scholarship to Foreign Students Tenable in Brunei Darussalam (BDGS) is administered by Brunei's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and covers Diploma, Undergraduate Degree and Postgraduate Master's Degree study at Universiti Brunei Darussalam, Universiti Islam Sultan Sharif Ali, Universiti Teknologi Brunei, Kolej Universiti Perguruan Ugama Seri Begawan and Politeknik Brunei. The award covers full tuition including acceptance, examination, registration and orientation fees, economy-class air travel to and from Brunei, accommodation in the university or polytechnic residential college, comprehensive insurance and monthly allowances. Applicants must be aged 25 or under for undergraduate and diploma programmes and 35 or under for postgraduate master's programmes on the first day of July of the year the course starts, and must show English proficiency.

Applications are routed through a nominating agency in the applicant's own country, so the Ministry does not accept direct applications.

scholarships.description: The Killam Fellowships Program, administered by Fulbright Canada, lets exceptional undergraduates from universities in Canada and the United States spend one semester or a full academic year as an exchange student in the other country. Applicants do not apply for it: all undergraduate programme applicants from underrepresented nationalities are considered automatically, and the decision is normally communicated with the offer of admission. Awardees receive a full tuition waiver that is renewable for the normal duration of the study, subject to satisfactory academic performance, and a School or Programme Office may add a top-up as long as the combined limit of full tuition fee plus an HK$60,000 annual allowance is not exceeded. The University opened its online application system for 2027/28 entry in early October 2026, with a Priority Round deadline of 25 November 2026.

scholarships.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at The American University in Cairo
scholarships.name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at The American University in Cairo
scholarships.deadline: 2 November 2026
scholarships.description: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at AUC is a fully packaged graduate fellowship for African students, starting with the Spring 2027 cohort, under which AUC intends to award fellowships to 300 graduate students in fields that promote African economic development. It targets academically talented young Africans with leadership potential who face the highest economic and social barriers. The award is granted for the total study period of the degree on full-time enrolment, subject to review every semester for satisfactory academic performance, and it covers tuition, a stipend, a laptop, health insurance, university accommodation, local transport and, for fellows who do not already reside in Egypt, roundtrip airfare. Application requires two separate steps: the AUC graduate application and a dedicated Mastercard Foundation Scholars application.
